So he wrote 'waiting'. To carve it the day he remembered." …Forgotten. Not erased. And two tags lay one on the other under the pillar. Tell the captain. Tell him we came down.
Every night a beast howls on the southern plain. A different voice as the moon waxes and wanes. Kael picked up a cub on the march and raised it. They say it's grown and carries Kael's scarf in its jaws. Fight it in the open and the pack comes. Call it alone through a Memory Gate. …Not killing, the archivist says. Putting to rest.
Open the Memory Gate and put the beast that howls at the moon to rest.
(로란이 낡은 목도리를 쥔다.) 카엘 거다. 놈은 이걸 스무 해 동안 물: (Roran grips an old scarf.) Kael's. It carried this for twenty years. Never left the place its master set it down. …This land is full of things that wait. The knight at the door, the undertaker in the snow, this beast. And me. The scarf smells of sun. South.
남쪽 사바나에 태양 부족의 숲이 있다. 가면을 쓴 전사들이다. 놈들은 ': In the southern savanna is the grove of the sun tribe. Masked warriors. They serve a 'second sun'. On the last page of the log there's a line in Kael's hand: 'Under the sun the ember can't be seen.' I took it for nonsense. Look closely at the masks. I need to know why they wear them.
태양 부족의 숲을 찾아 가면들을 살펴보고, 가면 전사 3명과 사냥꾼 전사: Find the sun tribe's grove, examine the masks, and defeat 3 masked warriors and 1 hunter.
가면마다 이름이라. 죽은 조상의 얼굴을 깎아 쓰고 다닌다는 거군. 잊히지: A name in every mask. So they carve the faces of their dead and wear them. So they aren't forgotten. And the sun is the fire that lights those names. …They're archivists too. Writing on wood instead of paper. And one priest half lifted his mask and asked, you say: 'Did you come carrying an ember? Then he's watching too.' A scar on the left cheek. Kael. …Who is watching, Kael.
할 말이 있다. 스무 해 전 마지막 밤, 카엘은 나한테 이 지도를 쥐여: I have something to say. On the last night twenty years ago Kael pushed this map into my hands and said 'the southern sun is calling us, you go back north'. Nonsense. I lost my temper and left. Never looked back. For twenty years I thought he'd gone mad and abandoned me. He must think I abandoned him. What do I say when we meet?
…알겠다. 네 말대로 하마. 이제 태양조에게 간다. 놈이 카엘을 붙들고: …All right. I'll do as you say. Now to the sun chief. It holds Kael. Or maybe Kael holds it.
태양조다. 부족의 족장. 놈은 두 번째 태양을 지킨다. 그건 부족의 기억: The sun chief. Head of the tribe. It guards the second sun. That is the tribe's memory, the fire that lights the names in the masks. To them we're the ones come to put it out. Kael stands beside it. Burned by twenty years of sun, he can no longer tell the chief's will from his own. He strikes whoever carries an ember. He'll strike me. Open the Memory Gate. Keep to the shade.
Open the Memory Gate and put the sun chief to rest.
가면이 깨졌다. 카엘은… 스무 해 동안 볕 아래 있었다. 몸이 버티지 못: The mask broke. Kael… was under that sun for twenty years. His body couldn't hold. At the end he looked at me and grinned. 'Did you count three times.' And then: 'It wasn't the captain who froze the sea.' I don't know what it means. You take the mask. I can't carry it.
불에 비춰 본 편지: The Letter Held to the Fire
카엘 씨의 서툰 가면이요. 안쪽에 금 열한 줄이 그어진. 그 가면이 걸려: Kael's clumsy mask. The one with eleven notches inside. Please look under the pillar where it hung. The temple scribble said 'I held the letter to the fire'. I don't think he burned that letter. He was a man who kept evidence. Go with the captain. He shouldn't read it alone.
In the sun tribe's grove find the letter Kael hid and examine it together with Roran.
대장님을 붙잡았어요. 지팡이를 들고 그대로 수도회로 가시려는 걸요. 카엘: I held the captain back. He had his cane up and was going straight to the Order. This is what Kael burned twenty years to prevent. Confront him now and all of it is wasted. I'll keep the letter. Between the pages of the Chronicle. Nobody searches an archivist's book. …The Elder taught me my letters. That is his hand. No doubt.
모은 명패를 가져와라. 열 개. 카엘 것은 없다. 놈은 명패를 사원에 두: Bring the tags you gathered. Ten. There's none for Kael. He left his tag in the temple. With his ember. We have the mask instead. …For twenty years I thought: when I've gathered them all I'll burn the roster. Burn it and let them go. I've lit the fire.
Hand the 10 expedition name tags to Captain Roran.
(로란이 명단을 불에 넣으려는 손을 이사벨이 잡는다.) \"태우면 잊혀요: (Isabel catches Roran's hand as he reaches for the fire.) "Burn it and they're forgotten, Captain. Fire eats names. Give it to me. I'll write them." …Right. That's the kind of world this is. (Roran holds out the roster. And the logbook.) Write this too. Every silly line they wrote. And fix the lines I got wrong.
이름은 다 적혔다. 한 가지가 남았다. 지도 위 카엘의 자리는 왜 지워졌: The names are written. One thing is left. Why was Kael's mark erased from the map? Report the end of the expedition to the Elder. Don't mention the letter. The archivist is right. Not yet. I can't look him in the face. My cane would move first. You go. And watch his hands.
(에르윈이 지도를 받아 카엘의 자리를 손가락으로 쓸어 본다.) \"지운: (Erwin takes the map and draws a finger over Kael's place.) "It was I who erased it. It was the Order's custom to erase beforehand the place one would not return from." Meaning he erased it before the expedition ever left. A faint heat rose from the glove. The Elder changed the subject. "There is worse news. The ice of the northern sea is creeping toward the town. Go and see Oscar the fisherman."
빈 줄의 주인: The Owner of the Empty Line
빈 줄을 채울 수 있게 됐어요! 호르스의 투구 안쪽에 이름이 더 있었어요: We can fill the empty line! There were more names inside Horus's helm. Three posts their lord ordered to 'wait'. At the door, the squire Horus. At the place of the oath, Vice-Captain Helvar. The name from Bram's ledger. The fourth captain whose name was scorched away in the fortress. Helvar is an old word for 'the one who keeps hell's threshold'. Deep in Hell, in a soul sand valley, is the arena he guards. Read the writing by its door and tell me why he stayed alone.
지옥에서 저승의 투기장을 찾아 문 앞의 상소문을 살펴보고, 서약을 지키는: Find the Underworld Arena in Hell, examine the petition by its door, and defeat 3 knights who keep the oath.
\"동료를 무기로 만들 수는 없다.\" 세 대장이 머리를 내놓아 검은 별: "You cannot make a weapon out of your comrades." He alone opposed the oath by which three captains give their heads and become the Black Star. Overruled, he still did not leave. He guarded the place where it was sworn, so no one could take the three heads. …And we already took them. Not knowing that, he is still guarding the door.
브람이 붙인 검을 가져가라. 싸우기 전에 내밀어라. 받든 안 받든. 지옥: Hell isn't my road. I don't know what's what down there. But that one I do know. A man guarding a post with nothing left to guard. Helvar is no guardian bound to a seal; he stayed on his own feet. No Memory Gate needed. No seal to burst. No mercy either. His knights carry the arena key. The mark on his back is his weakness, they say. Same as Horus. Their lord's people all leave their backs open.
저승의 투기장에서 저승의 기사 헬바르를 잠재워라. (최대 체력의 10%: In the Underworld Arena, put Helvar the Underworld Knight to rest. (Deal at least 10% of his health.)
브람의 검을 내밀었더니 싸움을 멈췄다고. 받아 들고 이음매를 한참 봤다고: He drove his sword into the floor and stepped aside as he fell, you say. After looking at the three empty stands in the middle of the arena. …He knew. That the three heads were already gone. He stood there anyway until someone came and told him it was over. (Roran says nothing for a long while.) Go to the archivist. Tell her to fill the empty line.
카엘의 셋째 낙서는 남쪽을 가리켰다. 정글과 태양의 땅 사이에는 사막이: Kael's third scribble pointed south. Between the jungle and the sun lands lies the desert. The log says 'the caravan road collapsed, three days' detour'. We went around. Kael was alone, so he would have cut straight across. We never asked why the road collapses. Let's see what is under it.
Find the sandworm's nest in the desert and examine what is left on the tunnel wall.
수로라. 사막 밑에 물길을 파던 짐승이라는 거군. 왕국이 모래에 묻힌 뒤: A canal. So it's a beast that dug waterways under the desert. And it keeps digging to the plan even after the kingdom was buried. That's why the ground falls in where it passes. The plan ends 'as far as the king's garden', you say. …That garden was buried a thousand years ago. Another one that waits.
시로크. 놈은 악의가 없다. 그냥 일을 하는 거다. 시킨 사람이 '됐다': Sirok. It means no harm. It is just doing its work. Until the one who gave the order comes back and says 'enough'. But every time it digs, the caravan road falls in and people are buried. It isn't bound to a seal either. We fight it in the nest. The ground under your feet trembles before it bursts from the sand. Step away then. It spits poison. Bring antidotes.
모래벌레의 굴에서 모래벌레 시로크를 잠재워라. (최대 체력의 10% 이상: In the sandworm's nest, put Sirok the sandworm to rest. (Deal at least 10% of its health.)
물을 붓자 올라와서, 싸우기 전에 먼저 그 물을 마셨다고. 고개를 숙이고: Water sprang up where it fell, you say. One thread of it. Water in the channel it dug for a thousand years, for the first time. …It never reached the garden. But it did call the water. Have the archivist write it down. 'The work is done.' There's no king left to tell it so.
호르스의 투구에 새겨진 셋째 자리요. 문에는 호르스, 서약의 자리에는 헬: The third post carved in Horus's helm. Horus at the door, Helvar at the place of the oath, and a tower. Beside the tower there are no letters, only claw marks. The signature of someone who cannot write. It is the dragon that Arden, the knight-commander, rode. There is a tower beyond the mountains. Go and see what remains in it. The captain is going too. 'I have to see the ones who wait,' he said.
용의 탑을 찾아 깃발과 안장을 살펴보고, 탑을 지키는 수호병 3명을 물리: Find the dragon's tower, examine the banners and the saddle, and defeat 3 tower guards.
천 년 동안 안장을 닦았다고요. 숨결로 그을음을 태워 내면서. 주인이 언: It kept the saddle clean for a thousand years, you say. Burning the soot off with its breath. So its master could mount the moment he returned. …If the burning knight of the dreams is Arden, he cannot come back. He is a man with the fire shut inside him. Does the dragon know? Is it waiting without knowing, or knowing?
애쉬로드. 주인이 '기다려라' 하고 떠난 탑을 지키는 용이다. 놈에게 우: Ashlord. A dragon guarding the tower where its master said 'wait' and left. To it we are thieves in its master's tower. It has nothing to do with the seals either. We fight it in the tower. Its throat swells before it breathes fire. Get behind a pillar. The guards keep rising. Don't drag it out. …Whether it's right to put it to rest, I don't know. But I don't know that it's right to leave it waiting for someone who will never come, either. I say that as a man who did it for twenty years.
용의 탑에서 지옥의 용 애쉬로드를 잠재워라. (최대 체력의 10% 이상: In the dragon's tower, put Ashlord the infernal dragon to rest. (Deal at least 10% of its health.)
싸우는 내내 안장 쪽으로는 한 번도 불을 안 뿜었다고. 우리가 그 뒤로: At the end it fell across the saddle, you say. Covered it with a wing. Held its breath so as not to burn it. …Enough. No head count today. Let's just sit a while. Then sleep. Everyone turns in early tonight.
자네, 지난번에 본 그 장부 말이야. '부단장 헬바르의 검, 수선. 값은: That ledger line you saw. 'Sword of Vice-Captain Helvar, repair. Payment when his lord returns.' It kept me up all night, so I went through the storeroom. It's there. The sword he left. A thousand years at the bottom of my family's storeroom. In two pieces. Not broken. Snapped on purpose. You can tell by the edge. I want to join it again. It's steel forged in hellfire, an ordinary forge won't heat it. Bring gold and blaze rods.
Bring 4 gold ingots and 2 blaze rods to Bram the smith.
붙었네. 그런데 보게, 이음매를. 일부러 무릎에 대고 꺾은 자국이야. 장: It took. But look at the join. Bent over a knee and snapped. There's my grandfather's grandfather's hand in the margin of the ledger. 'The vice-captain came out of the council, snapped his own sword and left it. Said he would not carry a blade that would serve the oath. Said to mend it. Said he would come for it the day he could carry it again.' …He never came. In a thousand years.
천 년의 당번표: The Watch Roster of a Thousand Years
투기장 안쪽을 더 봐야겠다. 놈이 천 년 동안 뭘 했는지. 싸우기 전에: I want a closer look inside the arena. At what he did for a thousand years. Knowing how your opponent lives before you fight him is a captain's job. Twenty years ago I didn't do it. Walls, floors, wherever a man has lived long, his habits are left behind. Find them.
In the Underworld Arena examine the roster on the wall and the empty stands in the middle.
매일 같은 시각에 받침 셋을 닦았다는 거군. 빈 받침을. 그리고 당번표: So every day at the same hour he polished three stands. Empty stands. And the last line of the roster. 'Today too my lord did not come. I stand again tomorrow.' He wrote that three hundred and sixty thousand times. …I counted twenty years, some seven thousand days. I've nothing to say in front of him. Bring Bram's sword. It's time it went back.
돌아왔군. 검은… 그래, 받았다고. 쓰러지기 전에 자네 손에서 그걸 받아: You're back. The sword… yes, he took it, you say. Before he fell he took it from your hands and looked at it a long while. Then drove it into the floor. Sit. The ledger must be closed. Striking out a thousand-year-old line happens once in a smith's life, if that. I called the archivist girl too. I strike out; she writes in.
Watch Bram the smith close the ledger.
'값 받음.' 됐네. 뭘로 받았느냐고? 검이 주인한테 돌아갔잖나. 대장장: 'Paid.' Done. Paid with what? The sword went back to its owner. To a smith that's payment. …One more thing. There's another line in the ledger with the same crest. 'Saddle of Knight-Commander Arden, repair.' That one is marked collected. A dragon saddle. Which means there was a dragon.
마른 우물의 달력: The Calendar on the Dry Well
사막을 가로지르기 전에 사막 마을에 들른다. 원정 때도 그랬다. 길은 사: Before crossing the desert we stop at the desert village. We did on the expedition too. You ask the road of those who live by it. An old man there said something odd back then. 'The road doesn't collapse, it sinks in order.' I let it pass. He said something was carved by the well. Let's go and read it.
Find a desert village and examine what is carved on the stone by its well.
꺼진 날짜와 자리가 전부 적혀 있었다고. 삼백 년치가. 그리고 간격이 똑: Every date and place of collapse written down, you say. Three hundred years of them. And the interval never changes. Once every seventeen days, one stretch at a time, west to east. That's not collapse. That's someone working. To a calendar. …And the villagers call it 'the guest who calls the water'? Unafraid? Because grass comes up a few days later where it sank. Damp rising from below.
사막의 왕 아므라트요. 연대기에는 '모래 속의 눈을 받았다'는 한 줄뿐이: Amrat, King of the Desert. The Chronicle has one line: 'he took the eye in the sand'. Nothing about why he left the canals to a beast and went. The pyramid you saw in chapter one. It wasn't a tomb, they say, but the king's water store. There should be pictures on the wall. See what the king promised the beast. And take water with you when you go to the nest. You'll understand why once you've seen the pictures.
Examine the wall paintings of the desert pyramid and bring 3 water buckets.
왕은 봉인의 눈을 받으러 가면서 짐승에게 약속했군요. '정원에서 기다리마: So the king promised the beast as he left to receive the eye of the seal. 'I'll wait in the garden. The day the water reaches it I'll open the gate.' And as the price of the eye his kingdom went under the sand. The beast digs on, believing the promise. …The last panel. When it hears water it stops work and comes up, because the king used to pour water and tell it 'well done'. That's the water we're taking. Whether that's right on the way to a fight, I don't know.
탑 아래층에 수호병들의 방이 있다. 죽어서도 당번을 서는 놈들이다. 용을: On the lower floor of the tower is the guards' room. The ones who stand watch even dead. Who feed the dragon and rehang the banners. See what they fed it. A beast remembers the hand that fed it. Even on the way to putting it to rest, let's know whose hand it is waiting for.
On the lower floor of the dragon's tower examine the guards' log and the basket.
주인이 있을 땐 사과였다고. 지옥에 사과가 어디 있다고. 지상에서 날마다: Apples, while its master was there. In Hell, of all places. Carried down from the surface every day. By the knight-commander himself. After he left, the log says, the dragon wouldn't eat them. It leaves them to rot and looks at the southern sky. On nights the southern sky is red, it cries. …The red sky we saw in chapter one. It knows where its master is. By the smell of the fire. It can't go. Because he said 'wait'.
탑의 용을 재웠다고 들었네. …앉게. 그 이야기를 처음부터 해 주게. 깃: I hear you put the dragon of the tower to rest. …Sit. Tell me the story from the start. The banners, the saddle, the basket by the window. I have never been to that tower. I know it only from books. So I want to hear it as you saw it.
Tell Elder Erwin what you saw in the dragon's tower.
(장로는 끝까지 듣고 한참 말이 없었다.) …기다리게 한 사람이 가장 나: (The Elder listened to the end and said nothing for a long while.) …The one who made them wait is the worst of it. Not the ones who waited. 'I'll be right back' is easy to say. Nobody says 'I can't come back'. As if saying it made it true. (He presses a gloved hand to his eyes.) You said it for him. To that dragon. Thank you. I mean it.
The snowfield hunters winter in igloos. They leave things on the walls. What they saw and where. Twenty years ago there was already talk of a 'corpse thief'. Bury a comrade lost to the blizzard and next day he's gone. I put it down to wolves. Let's read it again. To the end, this time.
Find an igloo in the snowfields and examine what the hunters wrote on its wall.
The graves weren't dug up. The snow was brushed aside, you say. By hand. A large hand. And the last entry. It carried a living man back and left him. Not a corpse thief, then. Something that tells the frozen dead from the freezing. It takes the dead and brings back the living. …Now I'm curious what it is.
얼어 죽은 사람을 세워 둔다는 얘기, 연대기에서 찾았어요. 서리 왕국의: Standing the frozen dead upright. I found it in the Chronicle. It's the funeral of the Frost Kingdom. The ground there was frozen too hard for graves. So they froze their dead standing. In rows at the edge of the village. They called it 'the standing forest'. And there was a beast that helped. Look at the innermost wall of the den. What that beast was taught should still be there.
Examine the innermost wall of the hideout in the snowfields.
서리 왕국은 왕이 스스로 수호자가 되면서 통째로 얼어붙었어요. 장의사들도: The Frost Kingdom froze whole when its king made himself a guardian. The undertakers too. Only the beast was left. Its teachers are gone and it still does as it was taught. Finds the frozen dead, stands them up, keeps them uncovered. Whoever they belong to. For a thousand years it has held the funerals of the whole snowfield alone. …I write names. Skor stands people up. It's the same work. Keeping them from being forgotten.
조사대원님, 편지를 연대기에 끼우다가 봤어요. 아래 귀퉁이가 한 번 더: While I was slipping the letter into the Chronicle I noticed it. The bottom corner is folded over once more. Glued down. Kael didn't glue it. It was like that when the Elder sent it. I got it open. There is one more line. I've brought the captain. Please hear it with us. I don't trust myself to look at his face alone.
Read the last line of the letter with Isabel the archivist and Captain Roran.
대장님이 수첩 첫 장을 폈어요. '광맥. 천장 무너짐. 토마스, 리아.': The captain opened his notebook to the first page. 'The lode. Roof collapsed. Thomas, Lia.' He looked at that line for a long while and said, 'The roof never collapsed. I wrote it that way. Because I didn't know what it was.' …The Elder knew. What was down there. Something that is not a seal. He knew, and he still marked that cave as the first stop.
가기 전에 하나만 확인하고 싶어요. 조각가의 수도원이요. 마당의 본 말고: Before we go I want to check one thing. The Sculptor's monastery. Not the models in the yard. The plinths where the real stones were cut and set should still be at the back of the workshop. The eighth plinth, too. A stone carver first cuts an under-inscription into the plinth. What will be carved on the stone that stands there. Lay paper on it and rub with charcoal and it shows. A rubbing. I'll give you the paper. Oh. No. Please bring the paper yourself. I used all mine on the Chronicle.
조각가의 수도원에서 여덟째 받침에 종이를 대고 탁본을 뜨세요. (종이 3: At the Sculptor's monastery, lay paper on the eighth plinth and take a rubbing. (3 paper)
떴어요? 보여 주세요. …이름이 아니에요. 일곱 받침에는 전부 왕의 이름: You have it? Show me. …It isn't a name. The seven other plinths all have a king's name underneath, but the eighth has one word. In the old tongue. 'Chesed.' It means mercy. And the Sculptor wrote beside it, small: 'The name to carve is gone. I carve only what was received.' And below that, scratched in another hand: 'Throw it away. Deep.' With seven seals stamped round it. Oh, and this rolled out from under the plinth, you said. An eye cut from stone. The Sculptor left it there. Throw it into the air and it flies one way only. An eye that knows where its stone was thrown.
We go. Under the first cave. The way I said 'down' twenty years ago. I walk in front again. Not to fight. To look. At what I failed to see that day. There will be marks. Lightning leaves marks on stone. We follow them in order. See one and the next will show.
광맥 밑의 굴을 찾아 로란과 함께 스무 해 전의 흔적을 순서대로 따라가라: Find the cave under the lode and follow the marks of twenty years ago in order, with Roran.
(로란이 굴 벽에 등을 대고 앉아 있다. 투구 둘을 무릎에 올려놓고.): (Roran sits with his back to the cave wall, two helmets in his lap.) …Fused together. They stood back to back. Shielding each other. I didn't see that either. I was blind by then. That hum from further in, you hear it. It hummed twenty years ago too. I took it for the ringing in my own ears.
도끼와 거울돌: The Axe and the Mirror Stone
로란한테 들었네. 땅 밑에서 벼락을 치는 돌이라고. 펠릭스가 굴 안쪽을: Roran told me. A stone that throws lightning underground. Felix drew the inner cave. Crystal pillars rising, the thing in the middle, polished slabs set in the walls. To a smith's eye that is no battlefield. It's a furnace. A furnace that holds lightning. And a furnace can be worked. Bring me two iron axes. I'll regrind the edges to the angle that breaks crystal. No charge.
철 도끼 2자루를 대장장이 브람에게 가져가고, 굴 안쪽을 다루는 법을 들: Bring 2 iron axes to Bram the smith, and hear how to work the inner cave.
날은 섰네. 잊지 말게. 순서가 전부야. 수정을 깨고, 벼락을 몸에 싣고: The edges are set. Don't forget. The order is everything. Break the crystal, carry the lightning, stand before the mirror stone. And one more thing. I told Roran, and you hear it too. That is no guardian. Nobody raised it. It was thrown away and it grew. So no one will thank you for putting it to rest, and no one will blame you. That is the loneliest kind of fight.
굴 앞에 모닥불을 피웠다. 스무 해 전 그 자리다. 그때는 열두 명이 둘: I've lit a fire at the cave mouth. The same spot as twenty years ago. Twelve of us sat round it then. Kael put too much salt in the soup and Bren ate all of it. Sit a while before we go down. That time we just went down. Didn't even count. Bring bread and roast meat. This time we eat first.
빵 4개와 구운 양고기 4개를 가져와 굴 앞 모닥불에서 로란과 이야기하라: Bring 4 bread and 4 cooked mutton and talk with Roran by the fire at the cave mouth.
If you've eaten, up. Head count. Two. …No. (Roran opens his notebook. He lays the ten tags round the fire one by one. In the empty place he sets the clumsy mask.) Twelve. This time we all go down together. What they didn't see twenty years ago, they see today with us. Move.
이름을 받지 못한 돌: The Stone That Was Given No Name
굴 맨 안쪽에 놈을 깨우는 자리가 있다. 다가가면 놈에 대해 적힌 것이: At the very back of the cave is the place that wakes it. Go close and you will see what is written about it. Read, then go in. Remember what Bram said. Crystals with the axe, carry the lightning, stand before the mirror stone. The four standing stones first. I hold the entrance. With this leg I'm a burden inside. But this time I stand at the door to the end. I'll see who falls behind.
광맥 밑의 굴에서 케세드를 잠재워라. (굴 맨 안쪽의 소환 자리에서 싸움: Put Chesed to rest in the cave under the lode. (Start the fight at the summoning place at the very back. Everyone who fights there is credited.)
놈이 갈라졌다. 검푸른 게 재처럼 떨어져 나갔다. 흰 돌만 남았다. 사람: It split. The dark blue stuff fell away like ash. Only white stone was left. A well-cut stone the height of a man. One word carved on it, and beneath that an empty space for a name. Room for eight letters. The archivist measured. …For a thousand years something else filled that space. The forgotten. We set Thomas's and Lia's helmets down in front of the stone. It seemed the right place. Up we go. There's a roster to finish.
장로님이 보냈소? 얼음 얘기겠지. 맞소. 올겨울 들어 하루에 한 뼘씩 마: The Elder sent you? About the ice, then. It's true. Since this winter began it comes a hand's width a day toward the village. After fifteen years of sitting still on the horizon. The northern sea froze in a single night fifteen years ago. My son Elric was aboard Captain Cornelia's ship that day. Neither ship nor crew came home. Sit. It isn't a long story, but it isn't one to hear standing.
같이 가 주겠다고. …고맙소. 나는 물길은 아오. 얼기 전 그 바다를 손: You'll come along. …Thank you. I know the waterways. Before it froze I knew that sea like my own palm. I don't know why it froze. For fifteen years that's what I most wanted to know, and least wanted to know. Let's not hurry. The ice swallows the hurried first. We start with the catch. Fish are the first to know how the sea is doing.
얼음 가장자리에 구멍을 뚫고 낚싯대를 드리워 보시오. 요즘 뭐가 올라오는: Cut a hole at the edge of the ice and drop a line. See what comes up these days. Cod and salmon will do. It used to be an hour's work for a full basket. See how long it takes you. That is the answer.
Catch 4 raw cod and 2 raw salmon and bring them to Oscar.
Took a while, didn't it. And look at these eyes. Clouded. These live deep. With no shallow-water fish left, the deep ones have come up. Means something has taken the shallows for itself. There's something big under the ice. Shut in for fifteen years. …That's for later. The sun's going. Time to light the lantern. Will you come? There's something I want to show you.
저기 얼음 위에 등이 하나 서 있소. 내 거요. 열다섯 해 동안 밤마다: There's a lamp standing out on the ice. Mine. I've lit it every night for fifteen years. Fresh wick every third day, and on windy nights I relit it three times. Tonight you change it. One lump of coal will do. Listen while you work. I've told this to no one.
Change the wick of the lantern on the ice with 1 coal, and hear Oscar's story.
잘 갈았소. 불빛이 곧군. (오스카가 등불을 한참 본다.) 저 불은 돌아: Well changed. The flame's standing straight. (Oscar looks at the lantern a long time.) You light it for the one coming home to see. But light it for fifteen years and you learn. It isn't for the one coming home. It's so the one who lights it can hold out. Tomorrow morning, go and meet the villagers. Hear about that night before we set out. Go without knowing and what you see on the ice won't mean anything to you.
오스카 씨가 보내셨습니까. 그날 밤 일이라면 기록이 있습니다. 시청 서기: Mr. Oscar sent you? There is a record of that night. A town clerk is bound to take down what people say on the day of a great event. I took down that day's too, fifteen years ago. But I only wrote. Others saw. Hear it from three of them. The smith, the cook, and the guide. When you've heard them all, come back and I will check it against my record.
대장장이 브람, 식당 주인 로렌초, 안내인 모리스에게 그날 밤 이야기를: Hear about that night from Bram the smith, Lorenzo the cook and Morris the guide, then return to Haru the town clerk.
세 분 말씀이 제 기록과 맞습니다. 하나만 보태겠습니다. 그날 밤 부두에: The three accounts agree with my record. I will add one thing. That night fishing boats put out from the dock to save the captain's ship. Not one came back. Mr. Oscar was on the dock that night, and that is all he himself remembers. The village decided not to correct that memory. You will see why for yourself out on the ice. Please do not ask him until he raises it first.
얼음 위를 걷겠다고. 그 신발로? 사흘이면 발가락이 떨어지네. 쇠 징을: Walk on the ice, you say. In those shoes? Three days and you lose your toes. I'll make you overshoes with iron studs. Oscar's too. He's worn the same pair fifteen years. Won't let me make new ones. They're what he had on the day his boy left. So his get new soles and nothing else. Bring me iron and leather.
Bring 6 iron ingots and 4 leather to Bram the smith.
됐네. 신어 보게. 발뒤꿈치부터 디디게. 얼음은 발끝으로 디디면 미끄러져: Done. Try them. Heel down first. Put your toe down first on ice and you slide. I've resoled Oscar's as well. Don't tell him. If he thinks I swapped them for new he won't wear them. And a favour for me. There was an Order outpost at the mouth of the ice maze. I hung the hinges on that door. Six were on watch that night. One was my apprentice. If you get there, just see whether the door was open or shut.
얼음 미로 초입의 전초기지다. 바다가 얼던 밤 당번이 여섯이었다. 한 명: The outpost at the mouth of the ice maze. Six were on watch the night the sea froze. Not one got out. The Elder said it the day you arrived: one day you'd see what happens when a guardian is touched without a Gate. This is it. I don't know ice. Oscar does. Go with him. There'll be no fighting. Look, and bring back what you see.
Find the outpost in the ice maze and examine the inside with Oscar.
숟가락을 든 채로라. 도망칠 틈이 없었다는 거군. 장로님은 그걸 '되먹임: Spoons still in their hands. No time even to run. The Elder called that 'backlash'. What everything around takes when something bursts all at once. They didn't die fighting. They froze at supper. …The door was open, you say. Tell Bram so. The watch left it open. Because they saw someone walking in.
당번표 뒷면의 요리법이요. '얼음 위에서 온 사람에게 먹일 것.' 전초기: The recipe on the back of the roster. 'For those who come in off the ice.' The outpost crew were cooking soup for the sailors walking out. That soup never reached anyone. I'll make it. Six bowls. They say that deep in the maze your lungs freeze from breathing. Eat it and go. As far as where those who were walking out stopped.
Bring 6 spinefish and 4 bowls of mushroom stew to Isabel the archivist.
됐어요. 식기 전에 드세요. 맛은… 로렌초 씨한테는 비밀이에요. 그런데: There. Eat while it's hot. As for the taste… don't tell Lorenzo. But listen. The roster said 'many lights'. The sailors were walking with lamps. Somewhere in the maze is where they stopped. A sailor always writes something where he stops. Oscar told me so. Please find them in order. The first written, the next, the last.
미로 안쪽에 선원들이 숨었던 은신처가 있다. 배에서 내려 얼음 위를 걸어: Deeper in the maze is the shelter where the crew hid. The ones who left the ship and were walking out over the ice. Tortured souls drift there. They are that crew. If they come at you, put them to rest. Don't hate them. They are still walking out. Read the wall in order. From what was written first.
얼음 미로의 은신처에서 벽의 글을 순서대로 읽고, 길을 막는 고통받는 영: In the shelter in the ice maze, read the writing on the wall in order, and put to rest 3 tortured souls in your way.
서른이 내려서 열여덟이 되고 일곱이 됐군. 일곱은 거기까지 왔고. 그리고: Thirty went ashore, then eighteen, then seven. The seven got that far. And to the end they did not blame the captain. 'The scholar in the grey cloak' sold the route. That cloak again. Two name tags turned up. Take them to Oscar. He's the one who must read them. Whether one is Elric's, I didn't look. That is not mine to see first.
Name tags, you say. …Give them here. No, wait. Let me breathe. All right. Hand them over. Elric's or not, a sailor's name tag has to be read out loud. That's how the man hears his own name.
Hand the 2 crew name tags to Oscar.
하산. 그리고 마레. 둘 다 아는 이름이오. 하산은 그물을 잘 기웠고 마: Hassan. And Mare. I know both names. Hassan mended nets well and Mare couldn't sing. (Oscar calls both names out loud toward the ice.) …Not Elric. I can't tell whether that's a mercy. As long as no tag turns up I can keep lighting the lantern. Ask the archivist girl to write them down. And what was on the wall. That boats came out from the village. …Where was I that night? No, don't answer. Not yet.
미로 밑은 캄캄하오. 내 등불로는 안 되오. 아귀를 잡으시오. 놈들 머리: It's pitch dark under the maze. My lantern won't do. Catch anglerfish. The lure on their heads is the only light that won't go out under the ice. Bring me one lure. And see which way they're holding their lures. A fish doesn't look one way for no reason.
Catch 2 anglerfish and bring 1 esca to Oscar.
이 불빛이면 되오. 그런데 놈들이 전부 미로 한가운데 쪽으로 초롱을 들고: This light will do. But they all held their lures toward the middle of the maze, you say. …Bait. The big one uses the little ones' lights as bait. To eat whatever comes to the light. The sailors walked with lamps. They'd have gathered toward each other's lights. And the thing in the middle would have seen those lights too.
조사대원님! 오스카 아저씨가 혼자 미로로 들어갔어요. 얼음 틈에서 목소리: Oscar has gone into the maze alone. A voice came out of a crack in the ice. 'Father,' it said. Elric's voice, he says. I heard it too. It sounded real. I did the same, remember. In that deep city where the Warden was. I followed my mother's voice down and… it wasn't my mother. Please hurry. He needs someone to tell him that.
Put to rest the 3 tortured souls holding Oscar in the ice maze.
(오스카가 얼음 위에 주저앉아 있다.) …알았소. 가까이 가니 알겠더이다: (Oscar is sitting slumped on the ice.) …I know. Once I got close I knew. Elric never called me 'Father'. He called me 'old man'. Since he was twelve. That was something else wearing his voice. The big one below takes out the voices it swallowed and uses them. …Which means he's in there. The archivist girl said she'd been fooled too. We wanted to be fooled. Both of us.
미로의 어머니다. 얼음에 갇혀 굶은 심해의 물고기라더군. 삼킨 영혼의 목: The Mother of the Maze. A deep-sea fish shut in the ice and starved, they say. She uses the voices of the souls she's swallowed as bait. Elric's voice came out of her belly too. Oscar knows it. He says he's coming as far as the door anyway. Take him that far and no further. She is bound in the same ice as what the captain's anchor caught. Put her to rest inside the Gate. She is only starving. She still has to be put to rest.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Mother of the Maze to rest.
놈이 쓰러지면서 목소리를 다 토했다. 수십 명이 한꺼번에 제 이름을 말했: When she fell she gave up every voice. Dozens of them saying their own names at once. And among them, one. 'Elric. Oscar's son.' Just as the captain used to call him. A name tag came out. And a frozen key. The ghost ship's. …I'll tell Oscar myself. That's for someone who has done his own waiting.
(오스카가 이름표를 손바닥에 올려놓고 있다. 오래 그러고 있었던 것 같다: (Oscar is holding the name tag on his open palm. He seems to have been doing so a long time.) Captain Roran told me all of it. He's clumsy with words. That's why I believed him. …There's a place on the ice where I set a stone. Beside the lantern. Not a grave. A marker. Would you hang this there. My hands won't do it.
Hang Elric's name tag on the stone marker on the ice.
걸었소? …고맙소. (오스카가 돌 앞에 앉는다.) 그 애가 먹혔다는 건: It's hung? …Thank you. (Oscar sits down before the stone.) That he was eaten, I understand. But there's something strange. His voice was still there. For fifteen years. Inside a fish, and not rotted away. A dead man's voice doesn't last like that. The crew didn't die. They weren't able to. By that ship's law. …I have to meet the captain. The way to the ship lies through the graveyard of ships.
미로 너머는 배들의 무덤이다. 그날 밤 선장의 배를 구하러 마을에서 나간: Past the maze lies the graveyard of ships. The fishing boats that put out from the village that night to save the captain's ship are caught there. Sharks and great eels circle between the hulls. Clear a way. And count the prows. The clerk wouldn't give me the number. He means us to count for ourselves, I suppose.
배들의 무덤에서 상어 3마리와 큰 뱀장어 1마리를 물리치고, 뱃머리들을: Defeat 3 maws and 1 eel in the graveyard of ships, and examine the prows.
스무 척이었다고. 열아홉은 이름이 있고 하나는 없고. 뱃머리가 전부 북쪽: Twenty, you say. Nineteen with names and one without. Every prow pointing north. Not boats that were running. Boats that were going. …And a scarf in the bottom of the nameless one. A long one, to wrap twice. (Roran says nothing for a long time.) Go to Oscar. Don't ask. Only tell him what you saw. He'll do the rest. I know that face. I saw it in the mirror for twenty years.
이름 없는 배가 있었다고. 바닥에 목도리가 있었다고. …앉으시오. 방금: A boat with no name. A scarf in the bottom. …Sit. It just came back to me. What hasn't in fifteen years. What the clerk never told me. What the village never told me. I'll say it. With my own mouth.
그게 다요. 나는 나갔소. 스무 번째로. 제일 늦게. 그리고 혼자 돌아왔: That's all of it. I went out. Twentieth. Last. And I came back alone. On foot. Leaving the boat. The village let it be that I'd stayed on the dock. A man who never went hurts less than one who went and turned round. …The lantern I lit for fifteen years wasn't only for him. I was marking the spot where I turned back. So I wouldn't turn back the next time. Come. This time I go to the end.
오스카 아저씨 얘기, 적었어요. 뭐라고 적었느냐고요? '스무 번째로 나갔: I wrote down what Oscar said. What did I write? 'He went out twentieth, and came back and lit a lantern.' That's all. I didn't write that he ran. I wrote only what was seen. And the writing on the wall. 'The captain meant to win back the Morning Star.' I've found what the Morning Star is. A wreck report from thirty years ago. When Captain Cornelia was twenty-two. Please read it with me.
Read the thirty-year-old wreck report with Isabel the archivist.
선장은 첫 배와 선원 서른둘을 바다 밑의 큰 짐승에게 잃었어요. 혼자 살: She lost her first ship and thirty-two crew to something huge from under the sea. Only she lived. After that she kept one line her whole life. No one dies on my ship. The grey cloak knew that when he went to her. He said there was 'a power that brings back what is forgotten'. That she could have her thirty-two back. He knew exactly where it hurt most, and named his price there. …But 'it did not break the ship, it carried it' troubles me. Oscar said it the day you first met him. Something big is shut under the ice.
무덤 북쪽에 새 배가 한 척 물려 있소. 열다섯 해 묵은 게 아니오. 지: There's a newer ship caught at the north end of the graveyard. Not fifteen years old. Last autumn's. Pirates. Iron on the prow, breaking ice as they came. They'd heard there was treasure on the ghost ship. I want to see why that ship stopped. A hull caught in ice is squeezed from the sides. But from a distance that one is humped in the middle. Pushed from below.
얼음에 갇힌 해적선을 찾아 오스카와 함께 갑판을 살펴보고, 남은 해적을: Find the pirate ship trapped in the ice, examine the deck with Oscar, and defeat 2 remaining pirates.
부순 게 아니라 안아 봤다는 거군. 무게를 재듯이. 그리고 돛대만 뽑아: Not broken. Embraced. As if weighing it. And only the mast carried off. The men not even touched. …The wreck report from thirty years ago said the same. It's that one. The one that took the captain's first ship. Shut in when the sea froze, and starved for fifteen years. Starved of ships. The old fishermen have a name for it. The one that cradles ships. Nerakyss.
그림이 펴졌어요. 선장이 열흘 동안 그린 거요. 연대기에는 네라키스가 없: The drawing has opened out. The one the captain drew for ten days. Nerakyss isn't in the Chronicle. It's no guardian of a seal. Only a sea beast that has lived a very long time. But look at this drawing and I think you can see why it takes ships. Please look with me. Tell me if it matches what you saw on the pirate ship.
Examine Cornelia's drawings with Isabel the archivist.
It's a nest. Built of ships. It cradles ships the way a bird sits on eggs. There's no malice in it. It's simply what it does. But at the very heart of that nest is the Morning Star. The captain drew it so. Down to the star on the prow. With the thirty-two still aboard. …I think we must do this before we go to the captain. We can't go to her empty-handed. We can't only say 'let go'. What she couldn't let go of for thirty years, we have to bring ashore first.
놈은 사람을 안 쫓소. 배를 쫓지. 그러니 배로 불러내야 하오. 해적들이: It doesn't chase people. It chases ships. So we call it up with a ship. The channel the pirates broke hasn't frozen over yet. We'll float an empty boat there. When it rises to cradle it, that's the one time it shows itself above water. Get me an oak boat. And raw cod to line the bottom. It likes a boat a fisherman has sailed. Chooses by smell. …My own boat is in that graveyard, true. But it hasn't even a name.
생대구 6마리를 오스카에게 가져가고, 해적선 곁의 물길에 참나무 보트를: Bring 6 raw cod to Oscar, and launch an oak boat on the channel by the pirate ship.
띄웠소. 이름도 새겼소. 뱃사람은 이름 없는 배를 안 띄우오. 열다섯 해: She's afloat. Named, too. A sailor doesn't launch a boat without a name. I did it once, fifteen years ago, and saw what came of it. She's the Evening Star. Because she goes to fetch the Morning Star. (Oscar stands at the edge of the ice watching the boat.) When it comes up, I throw the harpoon. This time I don't let go of the oar.
저녁별이 물길 끝에 닿았소. 놈이 올라올 거요. 네라키스는 봉인에 묶인: The Evening Star has reached the end of the channel. It will come up. The archivist says Nerakyss isn't bound to a seal, so it can't be called inside a Gate. You fight it as it is, beside the pirate ship. When its arms wrap the boat, that's your opening. Strike the arms first. It isn't angry. After fifteen years of hunger it has a ship at last and thinks we're taking it. It still has to be put to rest. The captain couldn't do it in thirty years.
얼음에 갇힌 해적선 곁에서 크라켄 네라키스를 잠재우세요. (최대 체력의: Put Nerakyss the kraken to rest beside the pirate ship trapped in the ice. (Deal at least 10% of its max health)
놈이 가라앉으면서 다리를 풀었소. 품고 있던 걸 전부. 얼음이 갈라지며: As it sank it opened its arms. Let go of everything it held. The ice split and ships came up. Thirty years old, a hundred years old. And one with a star on the prow. The Morning Star. Not even rotted. …The thirty-two were still on deck. Just as the captain drew them. Down to the way each one stood. Their names have to be called. From the list Elena took down. Let's bring them to the village. After thirty years.
아침별의 서른두 분을 부두에 모셨습니다. 서른 해 전 엘레나 기록관이 받: The thirty-two of the Morning Star have been brought to the dock. The list Elena the archivist took down thirty years ago is at the town hall. I will call them one by one. A flower laid for each name is how this village buries its sailors. You need not lay them all. Four will do. Bow, stern, port, starboard. One for each corner of the ship.
Bring 4 flowers, lay them at the dock, and hear the thirty-two names.
서른두 분, 호명을 마쳤습니다. 한 분도 빠지지 않았습니다. 명단 맨 끝: Thirty-two, all called. Not one missing. At the foot of the list is the captain's signature. 'Captain Cornelia. Survivors: 1.' Today I struck that number out. I made a column that is neither survived nor died and wrote in it. 'Returned to port: 32.' Thirty years a clerk and I have never made such a column before. Please tell the captain. They have come home.
장례에 온 사람들이 그러더라고요. 선장 배가 마지막으로 떠나던 날도 부두: People at the burial said so. The dock was this full the day the captain's ship last sailed. The second floor of the Spiral Abyss is the dock on that day. The Abyss shows the memories of those who passed through. Fifteen years ago the captain took her crew through it before sailing. Please see who saw that ship off. Haru's record has no list of well-wishers. Only for that day.
Pass through the second floor of the Spiral Abyss.
부두였다고요. 선장이 선원들 앞에서 법을 읽고, 삼백 명이 손을 들고,: A dock, you say. The captain reading her law to the crew, three hundred hands raised, the village clapping. And in the back row someone in a cloak. Not clapping. Hands behind his back. He was there. He watched the ship leave. He saw three hundred people waving and sent them anyway. …I don't think Haru failed to keep the list of well-wishers. Someone took that one page.
벽에 적혀 있었지. '닻이 밑의 무언가를 침. 종소리가 남. 바다 밑에서: It was on the wall. 'The anchor struck something below. A bell rang. Under the sea.' I know that bell. Every fisherman does. In the middle of the northern sea, where the water is deepest, on calm days a bell would sound from below. Since my grandfather's time. We called it 'the king calling us to supper'. An old tale. Will you hear it? And go to the clerk as well. The town hall has a thousand years of harbour tax ledgers. The first volume is from that king's time.
어부 오스카에게 바다 밑의 왕 이야기를 듣고, 시청 서기 하루에게 옛 장: Hear the tale of the king under the sea from Oscar the fisherman, and ask Haru the town clerk to show you the old ledger.
장부 맨 앞 권에 그 왕이 있었다고. 세금을 거둔 줄은 한 줄도 없고 내: So that king is in the first volume. Not one line of tax collected, only lines of things given. That would be right. Just as the old tale has it. And the last line was 'the stones of the seawall, to the seven kings'. …And that winter the citadel sank. That's what the anchor struck. The bell of the sunken citadel. The captain's ship dropped anchor on top of it. On the roof of a king who gives whatever he's asked.
바다 밑으로 내려간다고. 얼음 밑으로. 미쳤군. 좋아, 미친 일은 채비를: Down under the sea, you say. Under the ice. Mad. Fine, mad work needs good preparation. That brass helmet you picked up in the graveyard of ships. It's from the Order's expedition twenty years ago. My father made it. The rubber's all perished. I'll rebind the seams in copper. And kelp. The glass has to be fed kelp oil or it freezes.
Bring 4 copper ingots and 8 kelp to Bram the smith.
됐네. 물이 안 새. 그리고 이건 로란이 맡긴 거야. 스무 해 전 원정대: Done. Watertight. And this is something Roran left with me. The expedition fished it out of the northern sea twenty years ago, he says. An eye cut from stone. Red on one side, blue on the other. Throw it into the sea and it goes one way only. They didn't know what it was and left it in the store. Roran said, 'I think I know what it is now, so give it to the expedition.' He could have handed it over himself, but he always sends me. He's shy of being thanked.
돌눈이 가리키는 데로 갑시다. 깊은 바다요. 나도 가겠소. 얼기 전에 그: Let's go where the stone eye points. Deep sea. I'm coming. Before the freeze I passed over it hundreds of times. Never once saw what lay below. When you're in, look in order. The door, the wall, then before the throne. If the old tale is right, something will be hanging on the door. Something that came down fifteen years ago.
깊은 바다의 가라앉은 성채를 찾아 오스카와 함께 문, 벽, 왕좌 앞을 순: Find the sunken citadel in the deep ocean and examine the door, the wall, and the space before the throne in order, with Oscar.
닻이 문고리에 걸려 있었다고. 선장 배의 닻이. 그 닻이 종을 쳤고, 종: An anchor on the door ring. The captain's ship's anchor. That anchor rang the bell, and the bell woke the king. And the captain's request is carved on the wall. 'Let no one die on my ship.' …The king granted it. That's the ice. It was the only way that king had to keep people from dying. To stop everything. It wasn't the captain who froze the sea. It was the one who granted the captain's request. Meaning well. That's the most frightening part.
오스카한테 들었다. 왕이 선장의 청을 들어줘서 바다가 얼었다고. 그럼 우: Oscar told me. The king granted the captain's request and so the sea froze. Then there is one thing for us to do. We ask too. For the ice to be taken back. That king can't refuse, they say. The trouble is that the two requests are at odds. The captain's 'let no one die', and ours 'take it back'. It was written on the floor. When requests are at odds, they are settled by a duel. Sit. We plan how to fight it. The archivist has read the rest of what is written before the throne.
Plan the duel with Captain Roran and Isabel the archivist.
정리한다. 대포는 제 약한 쪽 것만 쏜다. 불에 약할 때는 불 대포, 얼: To sum up. You fire only the cannon of the side you're weak to. Weak to fire, the fire cannon. Weak to ice, the ice cannon. When the king leaps to the wall and fires his own, that's when ours can be used again. And do not leave the arena. Not one step. That king can't abide a turned back. …The captain isn't there. So the king will stand in her place. We aren't duelling the captain. We're duelling the captain's request. Don't forget that. Because once we win we have to look her in the face.
청은 말로 하는 게 아니래요. 화로에 얹는 거래요. 붉은 화로에는 마그마: A request isn't made in words, it seems. It's laid on the braziers. Magma cream on the red one, packed ice on the blue. Looking at the old petitions on the wall, everyone laid on the hottest and the coldest thing they owned. Say your request as you lay it and it's carved into the wall. We've settled what to ask. Captain Roran cut it down to one line. Please lay them on. I'll give you the words.
가라앉은 성채의 붉은 화로에 마그마 크림 2개를, 푸른 화로에 꽁꽁 언: At the sunken citadel, lay 2 magma cream on the red brazier and 2 packed ice on the blue brazier.
It's carved? You saw? One more line at the end of the wall. 'The Storm Expedition. Request: take back the gift. Let the bound go ashore.' And the answer. Not 'Granted', is it. An answer no one has seen before. 'Another asked first. It shall be settled by a duel. As that one is not here, I take up that one's part.' …The king is rising. He's fighting for the captain. To keep what he gave her.
왕이 일어섰다. 말쿠트. 달라는 걸 다 주고 가라앉은 왕이다. 봉인의 수: The king has risen. Malkuth. The king who gave everything asked of him and sank. He is no guardian of a seal. He can't be called inside a Gate. We duel in that citadel, by that law. Go close to the summoning place before the throne and you'll see what is written about the king. Read, then begin. Only the cannon of your weak side. Do not leave the arena. The whole expedition stands at the door. We'll watch your back. Go.
가라앉은 성채에서 베푸는 왕 말쿠트와 겨뤄 잠재워라. (왕좌 앞 소환 자: Duel Malkuth, the Giving King, in the sunken citadel and put him to rest. (Start at the summoning place before the throne. Everyone who fights there is credited.)
왕이 무릎을 꿇었다. 칼 두 자루를 바닥에 내려놨다. 붉은 것과 푸른 것: The king knelt. He laid his two swords on the floor. The red and the blue. And he said, 'The duel was fair. The request is granted.' Then he put his hand into the blue brazier and put the fire out. With his own hand. …There was a sound from above. Ice splitting. The whole sea. The king said one more thing at the last. 'Tell the captain. It is the first time I have taken back what I gave. Tell her I am sorry.' Let's go and tell her. The anchor is still on the door ring.
들리오? 얼음이 우는 소리요. 열다섯 해 만에 듣소. 봄마다 강 얼음이: Hear that? The ice crying. First time in fifteen years. The sound river ice made every spring when it let go. The sea is loosening. But come out onto the ice. It isn't only the ice that's crying. Stand with me and hold up a lantern. Only a little while. There's too much sound to hear alone.
Stand on the ice with Oscar, hold up a lantern, and listen to the thawing sea.
선원들이오. 얼음 밑에서 열다섯 해 묶여 있던. 왕의 선물이 걷히니 풀려: It's the crew. Bound under the ice for fifteen years. With the king's gift taken back they're coming loose. But they don't leave. They go toward the ship. All of them. Toward the ghost ship. The captain is calling them. The king can't hold them now, so she holds them with her own hands. Without even weighing anchor. …She won't give up her law. Even if the king takes his gift back. I know that feeling. I lit a lantern for fifteen years. Let's go and meet her. Not to fight. To bring her word of the Morning Star.
아무도 죽지 않는 배: The Ship Where No One Dies
유령선이다. 얼음에 물린 채 열다섯 해. 돛도 안 삭았다. 이제 왕의 힘: The ghost ship. Fifteen years in the ice's jaws. The sails haven't even rotted. Now it isn't the king's power holding it but the captain alone. Go aboard and read the ship's law and its roster. Know what kind of person the captain is before you meet her. We learned that in the land of the sun. Oscar goes with you. There's a line in that roster he needs to find.
Find the ghost ship and examine the articles on the mast and the crew roster with Oscar.
'내 배에서는 아무도 죽지 않는다.' 그 한 줄 밑에 삼백 명이 서명했다: 'No one dies on my ship.' Three hundred signed under that one line. And the roster has no column for death. The day they boarded, the day they left, and that's all. It's a ship you can't die on. Because the captain won't let go. Keeping her law. …Oscar read Elric's line and stood there a long time, I hear. He understood why fifteen years of trying to hate her never took. So the best kind of captain can become the most frightening kind. I was the opposite. A bad one. Which of the two loses more people, I couldn't say.
선장을 재우기 전에 말을 해 봐야 해요. 헬바르 때도, 그 용 때도 우리: Before we put the captain to rest we have to try speaking to her. With Helvar, and with that dragon, we only read. This time we have something to tell. The Morning Star. There's a table in the captain's cabin. She ate every evening at one table with her crew. One seat will be empty. The guest's seat. By sailors' law, when a guest sits at the table the captain must listen. Oscar told me. You can't sit down empty-handed. Take bread. Bread from the land.
유령선의 선장실에서 빵 3개를 들고 손님 자리에 앉아 선장에게 아침별의: In the captain's cabin on the ghost ship, sit in the guest's seat with 3 bread and give the captain word of the Morning Star.
뭐라고 했어요? …'전원 하선. 그 말은 내가 한다. 내 입으로. 그러려: What did she say? …'All hands ashore. That is for me to say. With my own mouth. And for that I must send my own three hundred ashore with my own mouth. But I cannot say those words. In thirty years I have never once said them.' And she drew her blade, you say. Not in anger. The captain can't break her law herself. Someone has to break it for her. If she duels and loses, then she hasn't abandoned it. She isn't one to throw a fight. And still she wants to lose.
코넬리아 선장이다. 기억의 문을 열어라. 닻이 가라앉은 성채의 종에 걸린: Captain Cornelia. Open the Memory Gate. Her anchor has hung on the bell of the sunken citadel for fifteen years. Put her to rest outside a Gate and that bell rings whole. You saw the outpost. Inside the Gate. Her blade is poisoned. Bring antidote. She will see you as the death come for her crew. She isn't wrong. Go anyway. She wants to lose. She just doesn't know how to let someone win.
Open the Memory Gate and put Captain Cornelia to rest.
선장이 쓰러지면서 이름을 불렀다. 삼백 개를. 하나도 안 틀리고. 마지막: As she fell she called the names. Three hundred. Not one wrong. The last was Elric. Then she called thirty-two more. The Morning Star's. Down to Tobin. Only when she'd finished did she let go of her blade. And she said one thing. To her crew. The archivist took it down. Go and hear it. What's left is a frozen logbook. The anchor has come up. The bell did not ring.
선장이 마지막에 한 말, 적었어요. '전원 하선. 선장의 명이다.' 서른: I wrote down what the captain said at the end. 'All hands ashore. Captain's orders.' The first time she'd said it in thirty years, they say. I thawed the logbook. Slowly, over three days. Thaw it fast and the ink runs. Let's read it together. After we write down the captain's name.
Read the thawed logbook with Isabel the archivist.
적었어요. 코넬리아. 그리고 삼백 명과 서른둘. 명부째로요. 일지 사이에: It's written. Cornelia. And the three hundred and the thirty-two. Roster and all. This stone was tucked between the pages. Carved with a storm. And the last page has a map. What the captain saw inside the storm. Seven dots shaped like eyes. I don't know what they are. I think we must ask the Elder. But listen. Some of these pages are stuck together. Glued, on purpose. There's a side the captain hid. It'll take me days to get them apart.
선장이 '내려도 좋다'고 했다지. 그런데 열다섯 해 묶여 있던 사람들이: The captain said 'you may go ashore', did she. But men bound for fifteen years don't walk off at one word. They've forgotten how to leave. They're still circling the ship. Take my lantern. A sailor sees a light and takes it for the dock. Once at the shelter, once at the ship. First the ones who were walking out, then the ones who stayed aboard. That's the right order. Those who went ashore first, go first.
Carry Oscar's lantern and gather the crew into it at the shelter and at the ghost ship.
(등불 안에서 작은 빛들이 흔들린다.) …들리오? 노래가 그쳤소. 대신: (Small lights waver inside the lantern.) …Hear that? The singing's stopped. Someone's laughing instead. Loud. 'Old man!' …It's Elric. He's in there. In the lantern. Fifteen years I lit this for him to see, and now he's come inside it.
등불이 따뜻하오. 열다섯 해 만에 처음으로. 이 안에 그 애가 있소. 불: The lantern's warm. First time in fifteen years. He's in here. Put it out and he goes. Where he's meant to go. Leave it lit and… he's here. Beside me. So this is what the captain did. Now I'm the captain. What do I do.
…Then that's what I'll do. Thank you. Not for deciding for me. For standing here.
항해일지의 붙은 쪽을 떼었어요. 김을 쐬어서요. 선장이 일부러 숨긴 쪽이: I got the glued pages apart. With steam. It's the side the captain hid on purpose. Not writing. A sketch. Under the floorboards of her cabin. She put something there. The ship should be quiet now. Please go and bring it out. I'd come, but Mia has a fever.
In the captain's cabin on the ghost ship, examine what is hidden under the floorboards.
구슬이요? 금이 간. …조사대원님, 그거 우리 기록고에 있는 것과 같은: An orb? Cracked? …That's the same as the one in our archive. The orb from my mother's things. And a drawing of the stand, you say. In purple ink. In mirror writing. And a note. 'Write down what you hear.' Signed with a gloved hand. …Two people. Two people gave the captain something. One sold her the route and one gave her the orb. That's what Haru meant about the grey coin having two different faces.
미아가 열이 내렸어요. 그리고 그 도면을 거울로 다 읽었어요. 그 애,: Mia's fever has broken. And she read that whole drawing in a mirror. She reads mirror writing better than I do. Perhaps because she's left-handed. She found something odd while reading. Hear it for yourself. After I heard it I stood in front of the archive's orb for a long time.
Hear from Isabel the archivist what Mia the apprentice read.
룬 제단이라고 부르는 그 받침대요. 용을 재우고 돌아온 뒤부터 우리가 써: The stand we call the Rune Altar. The one we've used since we came back from putting the dragon to rest. Those five stones were never decoration. The drawing calls them 'five letters'. It doesn't say which. Whoever made it writes in the same hand as 'I rewrote this book' on the archive wall. The one who altered the Chronicle made a mirror that shows what's forgotten. Why? Why would the one who changed it try to hold on to what was lost? …I haven't told the Elder. I'll give him only the map. The orb can wait until we know a little more.
바다가 풀렸소. 얕은 물에 고기가 돌아왔고. 열다섯 해 만에 그물을 던졌: The sea's loose. Fish are back in the shallows. I cast a net for the first time in fifteen years. My hands remembered. Come and eat. Grilled cod. Done the way Elric liked it. Salt and nothing else. Let's eat it hot.
Eat grilled cod with Oscar the fisherman and talk.
맛이 어떻소. …뜨거운 걸 다시 먹게 됐소. 로렌초가 울더이다. 주방에서: How is it. …I can eat hot food again. Lorenzo cried. In the kitchen. Slamming pot lids so no one would hear. And one thing I want to ask you. The captain's logbook says the storm looked into the ship. One person at a time. I went inside it once myself, when I was young. We'll talk about it another time. When my heart has settled a little more.
오스카 아저씨가 부두에 등을 하나 다신대요. 얼음 위 그 등 말고, 새: Oscar is hanging a lamp on the dock. Not the one out on the ice, a new one. For any boat coming in. He'd like you to hang it. If he does it himself, he says, he'll only think of one person again. Meanwhile I'll take the captain's map to the Elder. The one with seven eyes marked on it. The Elder will know what it is. …That he'll know frightens me a little, these days.
부두에 새 등불을 달아 주세요. (등불 1개): Hang a new lantern on the dock. (1 lantern)
달았어요? 저도 봤어요. 기록고 창에서 보여요. 그리고 스무 번째 배 이: It's hung? I saw it too. You can see it from the archive window. And I saw the twentieth boat's name. 'Scarf.' …I shouldn't have laughed but I did. It's a good name. The Elder took the map and said nothing for a long while. Then, 'Send the expedition to me tomorrow.' His hands were shaking. Whether from the map or from the sea outside the window, I can't tell. His is the only room in the Order with a view of the sea, and he sits with his back to the window. I only just noticed. After fifteen years of going in and out.
앉게. 코넬리아의 지도를 밤새 봤네. 일곱 봉인 가운데 여섯 자리가 그려: Sit. I spent the night over Cornelia's map. Six of the seven seals are marked on it. The seventh lies at the very bottom of hell, and even the captain couldn't draw it. Each of the six holds an eye, and at each eye a guardian is awake. You saw it at Roran's old expedition sites: the seals are rotting. A rotten seal bursts. Like the captain's table on that ship. Before they burst, each must be put to rest inside a Gate.
눈은 자네들이 갖게. 나는 보기만 하면 되네. 정말일세. 늙은이한테 그런: Keep the eyes yourselves. I only need to see them. Truly. What use would an old man have for such things? The first place is the Soul Forge in hell. Take Bram. Nobody hears what iron says better than he does. (The Elder straightens his glove. He seems in unusually good spirits today.)
영혼 대장간은 칼데라 왕국의 지하 대장간이었네. 화로의 왕 브라간이 첫째: The Soul Forge was the underground smithy of the Caldera kingdom. Bragan, King of the Furnace, took the first eye and buried it there. Its guardian is a giant the smiths forged. They say the hammering has not stopped in a thousand years. Look at the door first, with Bram. I'll wait outside it.
지옥의 영혼 대장간을 찾아 브람과 함께 문을 살펴보고, 불타는 망령을 2: Find the Soul Forge in hell, examine the door with Bram, and put 2 ignited revenants to rest.
밖에서 잠갔다고. 그래. 그게 브라간일세. 대장장이 백 명을 안에 두고: Barred from the outside, you say. Yes. That was Bragan. He left a hundred smiths inside and barred the door. So the way to make the giant would never get out. The king wrote that he had 'entrusted' it to them. …The revenants were still standing at their anvils, you say. The order was never finished, so they can't leave. And there is no door to leave by.
대장간 큰 화로가 반쯤 죽어 있더군. 거인은 그 불로 사는데, 불이 약하: The great furnace in there is half dead. The giant lives on that fire, and with the fire weak it grows uneasy and hammers all the harder. If we mean to put it to rest inside a Gate, the furnace has to be revived first. Bring me beacon cores and netherite scrap. One more thing. I want to heat the expedition's blades in that furnace, once each. Only steel tempered in that fire will bite the giant's hide.
영혼 대장간의 큰 화로에 블레이즈 막대 4개를 넣어 불을 살리고, 네더라: Feed 4 blaze rods into the great furnace of the Soul Forge to wake its fire, and bring 2 netherite scrap to Bram the smith.
살아났네. 봤나, 불빛이 달라졌지. (브람이 조사대의 날을 하나씩 화로에: It's alive. See how the light's changed. (Bram puts the expedition's blades into the furnace one by one and draws them out.) Done. But when the furnace came back, an iron plate showed under the anvil. An order sheet. What the king ordered. I can read, but not the old script. Go and read it. And about that hook with no name. …No, read the order first, then we'll talk.
주문서를 읽어 주게. 대장장이는 주문서를 보면 그 물건이 뭘 하려고 태어: Read me that order. A smith looks at an order and knows what the thing was born to do. Know that, then put it to rest. Berserkers circle the furnace. Fiercer than the revenants. Take care.
영혼 대장간에서 모루 밑의 주문서를 살펴보고, 불타는 광전사를 2명 잠재: Examine the order sheet under the anvil in the Soul Forge, and put 2 ignited berserkers to rest.
'이름을 주지 말 것'이라. 그래서 그놈은 이름이 없군. 이름이 없으니: 'Give it no name.' So it has none. With no name there is nothing for the fire to eat, and that's how it lasted a thousand years. And the last line. 'See that it cannot strike the door.' …But it does. With its fists. For a thousand years. Though its own body was forged not to. It's trying to let the hundred out. The hands that made it. The nameless hook is the hundredth smith's place. The one who never carved a name on anything. There's a saying in my family. 'The night the door was barred, the hundredth passed a handful of caged fire out through the gap. And stayed.' The one who took it, outside the door, was our founder.
주문서를 읽었다고. 그래, 브라간은 그런 왕이었네. 솜씨를 사랑하고 솜씨: You read the order. Yes, that was the kind of king Bragan was. He loved skill and did not trust those who had it. Open the Memory Gate. The giant must be put to rest inside. When the hammer comes down, don't hide, roll aside. And do not hate it. All it has done for a thousand years is knock on a door. Asking to be let out.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Netherite Monstrosity to rest.
놈이 쓰러지면서 마지막으로 한 번 더 문 쪽으로 팔을 뻗었다지. …잘했네: As it fell it reached for the door one last time, you say. …Well done. Truly well done. Have Isabel write the name. It has none? Then have her write that. 'The son who was given no name.' With the names of the ninety-nine, and a place for the one without. I've left the door open. Even an old man's strength was enough to draw the bar. A thousand years rots lead too.
조사대원님, 잠깐만요. 봉인 얘기가 아니에요. 대장간 이름을 적다가 수도: Wait a moment, please. This isn't about the seals. While writing down the forge's names I looked up the Order's history. The portraits of the past Elders hang in the gallery. Twenty-nine of them. I walk past every day and I've never really looked. Today I looked. Please look with me, just once. Tell me if I'm seeing things.
Examine the portraits of the past Elders with Isabel the archivist.
제가 이상한 게 아니죠. 스물아홉 분이 전부 장갑을 꼈어요. 전부 왼손을: I'm not seeing things, am I. All twenty-nine wear gloves. All with the left hand laid over the right. And every painter is different. And on the back of the first Elder's portrait the painter wrote: 'Told not to paint the hands.' …It could be a family custom. Manners handed down. I'm going to think of it that way. For now. The next seal is the desert, isn't it. I'll come too. There will be a lot to read.
저번에 사막에서 시로크가 쓰러진 자리에 물이 솟았잖아요. 그 물이 안 말: Back in the desert, water rose where Sirok fell. It hasn't dried up. It's running down the thousand-year-old canal. The villagers told me. It flows only one way. Toward the king's garden. That's the second mark on the map. The Cursed Pyramid. Let's follow the water. Where it stops, that's where the king is waiting.
사막의 저주받은 피라미드를 찾아 이사벨과 함께 마른 수반을 살펴보고, 코: Find the Cursed Pyramid in the desert, examine the dry basin with Isabel, put 4 koboletons to rest, then examine a fallen gardener.
물은 문 앞에서 멈췄어요. 한 뼘 앞에서요. 수반은 말라 있고요. 시로크: The water stopped at the door. A hand's width short. And the basin is dry. That's the last stretch Sirok never dug. And the koboletons. There were water-yoke marks on their bones. They were gardeners. They followed the king in and never came out. There's writing on the door. A lot of it. Before I read, let's look at the canal. There were stones standing along it on the way. Half buried in sand. Markers someone raised.
문 글씨를 다 읽었어요. 왕의 글이에요. 정원 안에서 문에 대고 쓴 거예: I've read the whole door. It's the king's writing. Written from inside the garden, on the door. For someone outside to read. Did you bring the water? Fill the basin while you listen. We'll bridge the last hand's width. In Sirok's place.
저주받은 피라미드 문 앞의 수반에 물 양동이 3개를 붓고, 이사벨에게 왕: Pour 3 water buckets into the basin before the Cursed Pyramid's door, and hear the king's words from Isabel.
수반이 찼어요. 문 안에서 뭐가 일어났어요. 아주 큰 게요. 뼈 부딪는: The basin's full. Something stirred behind the door. Something very large. I heard bone on bone. It's the gatekeeper. The beast the king rode. He knew the price of the eye was a kingdom buried. So he walked into the garden himself and had the door shut, so the sand would swallow the garden before the villages. He saved his people. But he never told his two beasts. That he wasn't coming back. He only said 'wait'. That's what the king handed off. The telling of the truth.
조사대원님… 저 갇혔어요. 문지기가 일어나니까 피라미드 안쪽 길이 다 바: I… I'm trapped. When the gatekeeper rose, every passage inside the pyramid shifted. Sand came pouring down. Where I am looks like an arena. It's where they tested who could enter the garden. It says so on the wall. And one gladiator is still standing. It's looking at me. I think it's asking whether I'm worthy. All I have is a pen.
Put the Kobolediator in the Cursed Pyramid to rest and rescue Isabel the archivist.
(Isabel brushes off the sand and laughs. Her hands are shaking.) Thank you. That gladiator. It knelt before it fell. Not the way the loser kneels. The way the one who lets you pass kneels. It means we were worthy. The first to pass in a thousand years. There was a space on the wall for the names of those who passed. It was empty. I wrote one in. The expedition.
…사막의 왕은 내 스승의 벗이었네. 아니. 그렇게 읽었네. 책에서. 문지: …The King of the Desert was a friend of my teacher's. No. So I've read. In books. The gatekeeper is the beast the king rode. They call it the Ancient Remnant. Nothing left but bone, and still it kept the door. Open the Memory Gate. Keep clear of where the sand heaves. It hides underground.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Ancient Remnant to rest.
(장로는 한참 말이 없다.) 짐승이 쓰러지며 고개를 숙였다지. 누구에게: (The Elder says nothing for a long time.) The beast bowed its head as it fell, you say. As if greeting someone. The door opened and the king was sitting inside the garden. By the dry fountain. Facing the door. In his bones. …So he waited too. Knowing it wouldn't open. That was not in the books. Have Isabel write it down. I… am going to walk a while. Alone.
나선의 심연 3층이 열렸어요. 수도회 옛 기록에 3층은 '회의'라고만 적: The third floor of the Spiral Abyss has opened. The Order's old records call it only 'the council'. The council a thousand years ago where they agreed to divide the Flame. The Chronicle says seven kings sat. The page we found early on said 'the eighth seat is empty; the seven emptied it'. Please see for yourself. How many seats there are.
여덟이었군요. 그리고 여덟째 왕이 반대했다고요. '나눈 불은 언젠가 누군: Eight, then. And the eighth king objected. 'A fire divided will one day be gathered again.' And the youngest king, shaking, said what? 'Feed it a prisoner's name.' …What does feeding a name mean? Dividing the Flame needed a name? And beside the eighth king stood a young apprentice in a grey cloak. And the memory broke off there. As if someone cut it. It's what my mother's echo said. 'When all are gathered, someone will use it.'
셋째 자리는 톱니의 여왕 오르델의 도시일세. 지금은 공장만 남았지. 여왕: The third place is the city of Ordel, Queen of Cogs. Only the factory remains. The queen built a machine to reckon what was to come. And when she saw its answer she stopped every clock in the city. Go and see why. This time I'll come inside. I must see with my own eyes what that machine reckoned.
고대 공장을 찾아 에르윈과 함께 큰 시계를 살펴보고, 감시자를 3기 멈추: Find the Ancient Factory, examine the great clock with Erwin, and stop 3 watchers.
열두 시 한 분 전이라. 온 도시의 시계가. 여왕은 기계한테 물었지. ': One minute to twelve. Every clock in the city. The queen asked the machine, 'When is the end?' The machine answered, and she stopped the clocks so that hour would never come. If the clocks don't run, the end doesn't arrive. A child's idea. …I know that feeling. The watchers are clock-keepers. They watch for anyone who winds a spring. What comes when one is wound, you'll soon learn.
기계가 잠들어 있네. 도시의 시각이 멈춰서 기계도 멈춘 걸세. 깨우려면: The machine is asleep. The city's hour stopped, so the machine stopped. To wake it the great clock has to run again. Bring a clock and redstone. I'll do the winding. When it's wound, the hunter will come. The Prowler. A machine that seeks whoever winds a spring. It will chase me. You strike it from behind while it does. …An old man playing bait. What next.
시계 1개와 레드스톤 가루 8개를 가져오고, 큰 시계의 말뚝을 뽑은 뒤: Bring 1 clock and 8 redstone dust, pull the stake from the great clock, then stop the Prowler in the Ancient Factory.
(장로가 숨을 고른다. 웃는다.) 이 나이에 뛸 줄이야. 로란이 봤으면: (The Elder catches his breath. He laughs.) Running, at my age. Roran would have teased me. The clock is going. Do you hear it? One minute has passed, for the first time in a thousand years. It's twelve. The machine has opened its eye. It has begun spitting paper. Everything it reckoned. A thousand years' worth at once. Your names are in it.
하빈저일세. 끝을 보라고 만든 기계. 여왕은 제가 물은 것의 답을 감당하: The Harbinger. A machine built to see the end. The queen couldn't bear the answer to her own question, so she handed it to the machine. 'You saw it, so you guard it.' Open the Memory Gate. Whatever reckoning it recites as it falls, let it pass. A machine only says what it saw. It doesn't know what it means.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Harbinger to rest.
\"마지막 문을 여는 것은 불씨를 쥔 자들이다. 그 손을 이끄는 것은 장: 'Those who open the last door are the ones who hold the embers. The hand that guides them wears a glove.' That's what the machine recited. (The Elder strikes the floor with his staff. A face you have never seen on him.) What does a lump of iron know! A sum done a thousand years ago! People do not go the way they're reckoned. They do not. …Forgive me. I shouted. Patience wears thin with age. Give the printout to Isabel. The road you've walked is written on it. It reckoned even that.
따지러 가지 않는 사람: The One Who Doesn't Go to Ask
기계가 '장갑'이라고 했다지. 기록관이 인쇄지를 들고 왔더라. 그리고 카: The machine said 'glove', I hear. The archivist brought me the printout. And Kael's letter. The one she tucked into the Chronicle back then. There was a hidden line. I know. I saw it that day. I pretended not to. Sit down. I'll tell you why a captain doesn't go and demand answers.
증거 없이 따지면 장로는 웃고 만다. 그리고 다음부터는 더 조심한다. 스: Go at him without proof and the Elder smiles and that's the end of it. And from then on he's more careful. I learned that twenty years ago. Hammer on a door in a hurry and all you do is ready whoever's behind it. Four seals left. Walk beside him to the end. Watch as you walk. A man who walks long enough starts to limp. On the side he's hiding. I can't go, with this leg. So I'm asking you. Be my eyes.
미아가요, 룬 제단을 닦다가 받침대 밑판이 헐거운 걸 찾았어요. 선장실: Mia was polishing the Rune Altar and found the base plate of the stand is loose. Going by the drawing from the captain's cabin, the plate was always meant to open. There's writing inside, she says. Mirror writing. She read it and won't tell me. 'Look for yourself, teacher.' Please look with me. And while you're at the altar, watch who comes by.
Examine the inside of the Rune Altar's stand.
\"이 글자들을 그 아이에게 보이지 마라.\" …그 아이가 누구예요. 다: 'Do not show these letters to that child.' …Who is 'that child'? We learned from that blueprint that the five stones are letters. Who are they hidden from? You saw the Elder pass just now. He stopped at the altar. He looked at the five stones a long time. Then he said, 'I feel I've seen this hand somewhere.' And walked on. He can't read them. Right in front of him. Mia cried when she saw it. She says she doesn't know why.
넷째 자리는 바다 밑이라지. 내가 가겠소. 바다가 녹은 뒤로 밤마다 밑에: The fourth place is under the sea, they say. I'll go. Since the thaw, singing comes up from below every night. Not that bait-voice from the ice maze. People singing. Many. Without rest. But these last days they drop out one by one. Fewer voices. Let's go see. The Elder says he'll stay ashore. He won't board a boat.
가라앉은 도시를 찾아 오스카와 함께 노래의 석판을 살펴보고, 딥링을 4명: Find the Sunken City, examine the slab of the song with Oscar, and defeat 4 deeplings.
자장가였군. 천 년째 부르는. 여왕이 사제들한테 그랬다는 거요. '멈추지: A lullaby. Sung for a thousand years. The queen told the priests, 'Don't stop. If you stop, it wakes.' No relief. When a priest fell, the child took it up. That's what the queen handed off. The lullaby she should have sung herself. …But why fewer voices? Something lay under the slab. A grey coin. Off a priest's neck. Someone paid the priests. To stop singing.
노래를 끊는 자들: Those Who Would Cut the Song
남은 사제가 둘이오. 둘이서 밤낮으로 부르오. 목이 다 쉬었지. 그런데: Two priests left. Two of them singing day and night. Their voices are worn to nothing. And big brutes and spell-casters stand round them. Not guarding. Trying to stop their mouths. Those ones wear the coins too. Clear them off. Don't touch the priests. Those two are the last line of a thousand years of lullaby.
Defeat 2 deepling brutes and 2 deepling warlocks in the Sunken City.
늦었소. 놈들은 치웠는데, 사제 하나가 그 틈에 쓰러졌소. 지쳐서. 하나: Too late. We cleared them, but one priest dropped in the gap. Worn out. The last one sings alone and hasn't the breath. There are breaks between the bars. Below, something big rolled over. It's waking. Before its time. …The last priest pressed something into my hand. An eye. The Eye of the Abyss. It means: we can't sing any more, put it to rest. In place of the lullaby.
리바이어던이오. 여왕이 기르던 짐승이라더이다. 봉인이 생기기 전엔 바다: The Leviathan. A beast the queen raised, they say. The slab said that before the seal the children of the city under the sea rode on its back. The queen buried the eye inside it, and since the city would fall if it woke, she put it to sleep. A thousand years. Open the Memory Gate. Out of water it has no strength. Draw it to the shallows. I'll be at the door singing that song. I've got the eight bars by heart.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Leviathan to rest.
놈이 눈을 감았소. 자는 눈이 아니라 쉬는 눈으로. 마지막 사제가 노래를: It closed its eyes. Not sleeping eyes. Resting ones. The last priest stopped singing. First time in a thousand years. Know the first thing that priest said in a speaking voice? 'It's quiet.' (Oscar takes off his cap.) I went to tell the Elder and he wasn't on the shore. He was over the hill. Where you can't see the sea. With his back turned. I said, 'The sea's gone quiet.' He said, 'Has it. I didn't see.' Wouldn't see, not couldn't.
다섯째 자리는 허공일세. 자네들이 용을 재운 그 땅. 거기 무너진 성채가: The fifth place is the void. The land where you put the dragon to rest. There's a fallen citadel there. Where the eight kings held council. The void's mist hides it from the naked eye. Grind a lens from the shell of the great crab that lives in the amethyst nest underground and you can see through the mist. …I found that method when I was young. In a book. Yes, in a book.
Find the amethyst nest underground and defeat the amethyst crab.
잘 깎였네. (장로가 렌즈를 눈에 댄다. 오래 본다. 렌즈를 내린 손이: It's cut well. (The Elder holds the lens to his eye. He looks a long time. The hand that lowers it is shaking.) I see it. The room that held eight thrones. You saw it in the Abyss, you said. The council. How far did you see? As far as the eighth standing up. …And nothing after. Yes. What came after, I too… it isn't in the books. Come. I'll go inside this time as well. This place I must go to.
성채일세. 왕좌를 하나씩 보게. 왕들은 회의가 끝나고 제 자리에 하나씩: The citadel. Look at the thrones one by one. They say that when the council ended each king left something on his seat. To use when they met again. They never met again. Endermaptera will have gathered. Clear them as you go.
엔드의 폐허 성채를 찾아 에르윈과 함께 일곱 왕좌를 살펴보고, 엔더맙테라: Find the Ruined Citadel in the End, examine the seven thrones with Erwin, and defeat 4 endermaptera.
일곱 자리에 일곱 가지가 남았군. 망치, 물동이, 태엽 열쇠, 조가비,: Seven things on seven seats. A hammer, a water jar, a winding key, a shell, a shard of ice, a lump of sealing wax, and an empty scabbard. That one is Caldern's. A scabbard and no sword. He gave the sword to his knight-commander. Along with the fire. Each of them left something. What remained after they'd handed off everything they could. The eighth seat is at the very back. Come. …No, wait. Let me get my breath.
조사대원님, 저도 왔어요. 로란 대장님이 혼자 두지 말랬다면서요. 저는: I've come too. Captain Roran told you not to leave me alone, didn't he. I came so the Elder wouldn't be alone. Strange, isn't it. There's a golem standing before the eighth seat. Built of void stone. It isn't guarding a door. It's guarding the seat. So no one sits there. Put the golem to rest and let's look at the seat together. The Elder is back there. He can't come any closer.
Put the Ender Golem in the Ruined Citadel to rest, and examine the eighth throne.
장로님이 그 자리 앞에서 무릎이 꺾였어요. 제가 부축했어요. 팔이… 뜨거: The Elder's knees gave way in front of that seat. I held him up. His arm… was hot. Even through the glove. And he said, 'Don't read it. You won't be able to. Neither can I.' The scratched-out name. It was eight letters long. You can count them. The shapes are gone. But listen. The scrap of cloth on the back of the seat. It's grey. The hem of a cloak. A thousand years old and not rotted. No one was trying to sit here. Someone was hanging on here. Holding on to a person being dragged away.
…You saw me at my worst. Old knees. Nothing more. Put the Ender Guardian to rest. The keeper Velas set before his lock. To stop anyone who asks. Open the Memory Gate. The grey cloth? Old cloth. Nothing rots in the void. Nothing more than that. Hurry.
Open the Memory Gate and put the Ender Guardian to rest.
가디언이 무너지며 여덟째 자리를 가리켰다지. 묻지 말라고 세운 것이 마지: As the Guardian fell it pointed at the eighth seat, you say. The thing set there to forbid asking pointed, at the last. (The Elder is silent a long while before he speaks.) It was under the wax, you say. That the question was sent to the scale. The Island of the Scale is not far. It was built apart from the citadel, so that judgment would not look at the kings' faces. If you want the answer, go. Isabel has already gone toward the bridge. I… do not set foot on that island. I will not step onto the scale.
