마지막 자리예요. 서리 감옥. 장로님은 정말 안 오셨어요. 수도회 문 앞: The last place. The Frost Prison. The Elder truly didn't come. He only raised a hand at the Order's door. This king is unlike the others. The Chronicle says 'the King of Frost entrusted his eye to no one'. I took that as praise, but after seeing that small seat among the seven thrones I'm not sure. The seat with 'I'm afraid' scratched into it. Let's look at the prison first. At who locked up whom.
얼어붙은 감옥을 찾아 감방을 살펴보고, 드라우그 4명과 정예 드라우그 1: Find the Frosted Prison, examine the cell, and put 4 draugr and 1 elite draugr to rest.
감방 문이 전부 안에서 잠겨 있었어요. 열쇠는 감방 안에 있고요. 간수가: Every cell door was locked from the inside. The keys are inside the cells. It's a prison with no jailers. The prisoner walked in and locked himself up. The draugr are the king's soldiers. He went in, so they followed. The king's writing was on the wall. An eighteen-year-old's hand. He keeps getting his spelling wrong. He wrote down, himself, what he said at the council.
왕의 묘실 앞에 근위대가 있어요. 왕관을 쓴 드라우그와, 문짝만 한 앞트: The king's guard stands before his tomb chamber. A draugr wearing a crown, and an aptrgangr the size of a door. The crowned one is the king's brother. It was on the wall. 'My brother said he didn't want to be king. So I became king. He was sorry, and followed me in.' And listen. I'm done pretending not to know. The glove on the printout. The grey cloth. The portraits. My mother's last page. When we meet the king I'm going to ask. Who the grey cloak is. Someone who has lived a thousand years will know.
Put the Royal Draugr and the Aptrgangr in the Frosted Prison to rest.
근위대가 쓰러졌어요. 왕관이 굴러서 묘실 문 앞에 멈췄어요. 문 틈으로: The guard has fallen. The crown rolled and stopped at the chamber door. A voice is coming through the gap. It's young. About our Mia's age. It's calling, 'Brother?' …There's no one left to answer. We put him to rest. Please go and take what he says. I'll write it down. Don't open the door yet. He hasn't spoken with anyone before a fight in a thousand years.
Please stand at the gap in the chamber door. The king will speak. Listen, and answer him. I'll write every word. And if the king asks you something… answer however you wish. There won't be a right answer.
Hear the king through the gap in the tomb chamber door of the Frost Prison, and answer him.
(이사벨의 펜이 멈춰 있다.) 다 적었어요. '회색 망토는 한 달 전에도: (Isabel's pen has stopped.) I have all of it. 'The grey cloak came a month ago too. In a thousand years he has come a hundred times. Each time his face was a little different. The glove was the same.' And the promise. 'A life without end.' The king was to take that and open the door. Give up the eye. But after your answer he was quiet a long time. Then he said, 'Then put me to rest. The promise was made with that man. You owe it nothing.' …The door opened from inside.
왕이 문을 열었어요. 스스로요. 기억의 문을 열어 주세요. 봉인이 터지지: The king opened the door. Himself. Please open the Memory Gate. He must be put to rest inside so the seal doesn't burst. He flies through the air throwing spears and reaps the souls of the fallen. He'll fight as a fight is fought. A thousand years of habit. But he asked to be put to rest. Please don't forget that.
Open the Memory Gate and put Maledictus, King of Frost, to rest.
왕이 쓰러지며 한 말이요. '회색 망토의 학자에게 전해라. 나는 약속을: What the king said as he fell. 'Tell the scholar in the grey cloak. I take back the promise. And that one did not blame you. I was there. I saw.' …I wrote it down. The king's name too. Maledictus. Eighteen years old. Someone was standing at the prison entrance. The one who said he couldn't come. Holding the door frame. Smoke was rising from his glove. He heard all of it. Then he turned and left. Toward the Order. Let's go. Now.
There's a light in the Elder's room. Let's go. I've brought everything I mean to ask about. The hands in the portraits. The hidden line in Kael's letter. The note from the captain's wallet. The machine's printout. The scrap of grey cloth. And my mother's last page. I'll lay them out. Please just stand beside me. He promised to answer when we came back and asked. The Elder doesn't break promises. That's what frightens me most.
Go to Elder Erwin with Isabel the archivist.
(The Elder takes off his glove. Slowly. One finger at a time. There is fire on the back of his right hand. Not burning. Carved. In the shape of a flame. No. Look again and there are strokes.) "I told you to keep the eyes. They are husks. Six have closed, and that is enough. The rest is at the bottom of hell. I have waited a thousand years. Your expedition… you were good people. That was the hardest part." The Elder put his hand into the archive lantern. The fire passed into his hand. And he was gone.
…기록고 등불이 꺼졌어요. 어머니의 등불이요. 재의 잉크를 찾던 날 같이: …The archive lantern has gone out. My mother's lantern. The one we lit together when you first came. The Elder took it. I'm all right. Really. Only sit here with me a little while. You don't have to say anything.
장로님 책상에 제 습자 공책이 있었어요. 일곱 살 때 거요. 장로님이 빨: My copybook was on the Elder's desk. From when I was seven. The one he corrected in red ink. He never threw it away. On the last page there was one line in his hand. 'This child will read to the end, like her mother. What do I do with her then?' …There was no answer written. I'm going to read to the end. And this time I'm going to write to the end. Captain Roran is gathering the expedition. They're going to the bottom of hell.
조사대원님, 떠나기 전에 잠깐만요. 선장의 지도를 수도회 벽지도 위에 겹: Before we leave, one moment. I want to lay the captain's map over the Order's wall map. She wrote a line at every mark. Short, like a clause of law. Read them with me. We should know where we're going.
Lay the two maps over each other with Isabel in the archive.
여섯 줄이 다 '들어간 자'로 시작해요. 선장은 자리가 아니라 사람을 센: All six lines begin with 'those who went in'. The captain counted people, not places. And the Order's wall map has none of these six places. Not the map from a hundred years ago, not the one from three hundred. Yet the Elder said he saw the captain's map for the first time last night, and he never once asked the way. He read it in a book, I suppose. I'll ask which shelf when we're back. The first place is the forge. Bram is waiting.
집안 장부 첫 쪽: The First Page of the Ledger
자네들이 지옥의 대장간에 간다고. 장로님이 나를 데려가라 했다지. 그 양: So you're going to the forge in hell, and the Elder said to take me. How did he know I know that door? Sit. I'll show you our family ledger. Eighteen generations of it. The first page isn't writing, it's a drawing. And help me pack. Hell's fire isn't like ours. Charcoal won't do; it has to be coal.
Look at the ledger with Bram the smith, and bring 16 coal and 4 iron ingots.
됐네. 이만하면 망치 자루가 불 앞에서 안 터질 걸세. 그림 얘긴데. 문: That'll do. The hammer hafts won't split in that heat. About the drawing. A barred iron door. A hand passing something through the gap. A hand receiving it. The receiving hand is our founder. Whose the giving hand is, nobody wrote. Grandfather only said 'go there and you'll know'. He never went. …Eighteen generations, and it's me who goes. My hands are shaking a little. They never shook in front of iron.
망령들이 쓰러진 자리에 망치가 남았네. 손에서 놓지를 않았던 거야. 천: The hammers are lying where the revenants fell. They never let go. A thousand years. We can't just leave them. In a smithy you hang your hammer on your peg when the work is done. That's how you go home. Those people haven't gone home in a thousand years. Hang them with me. I'll read the name tags.
영혼 대장간에서 브람과 함께 망치를 걸이에 거세요. (세 줄): Hang the hammers on their pegs with Bram in the Soul Forge. (Three rows)
아흔아홉 자루 다 걸었네. 걸이마다 높이가 달랐지. 키에 맞춘 거야. 왼: Ninety-nine, all hung. Every peg at a different height. Fitted to each one's reach. The left-handers' pegs bend the other way. That's how well they knew each other. …My family name isn't there. Not among the ninety-nine. Then who handed our founder the fire? The hundredth peg, the one with no tag. That's the only hammer I couldn't find. It isn't in here. Let's wake the furnace. More shows in good light.
Let's ask the door whether the family story is true. Smiths have a knocking speech. You can't hear across a furnace, so you strike the anvil. 'Three, pause, two' means 'the fire is alive'. I thought only my family used it. If it came from here, it will understand. You strike. My hands can't be trusted just now.
Knock on the inner door of the Soul Forge and listen for the answer.
들었나. '둘, 쉬고, 셋.' 그건 '문 열어라'야. 아니, 우리 집에서: Did you hear? 'Two, pause, three.' That's 'open the door'. No, we don't use it that way at home. We use it for 'come and eat'. …So it was 'come and eat' all along. The hundredth taught it that. For a thousand years it's been knocking 'come and eat' at the door. Not to the ones inside. To the fire that was sent out. Asking if it's well. (Bram rests his forehead on the door a long while.) The Elder says it must still be put to rest. If the seal rots it bursts too. All right. Then while you fight, I'll keep knocking. Three, pause, two. So it doesn't fall asleep alone.
돌아왔군. 나도 방금 왔네. 대장간에서 하나 들고 왔어. 백 번째 걸이일: You're back. So am I. I brought one thing from the forge. The hundredth peg. Pulled it from the wall. It isn't stealing. Who else was going to bring it? It goes in my smithy wall. Bring me some iron. There's a peg and no hammer, so we forge one. You strike the first blow. The hand that put it to rest.
철 주괴 3개를 가져가고, 브람의 대장간에서 새 망치를 백 번째 걸이에: Bring 3 iron ingots and hang the new hammer on the hundredth peg in Bram's smithy.
걸렸네. 이름표는 안 새겼어. 그 사람이 안 새기던 사람이니까. 로렌초가: It's hung. I carved no name. He wasn't one to carve his. Lorenzo came by and said he finally knows why I rap every piece of iron with my knuckles. A door-knocking family, he says. Nonsense. …But my grandfather did it too, and his father. See a thing, knock on it. Waiting for an answer. Eighteen generations of that. The first answer came today.
놋쇠판마다 '먼 지부에서 옴'이라고 돼 있잖아요. 스물아홉 번 다요. 그: Every brass plate says 'came from a far chapter house'. All twenty-nine. If I only knew where that house is, I'd have been worrying over nothing. I don't know the roads. Morris knows every road, and Haru keeps the record of who came to town and when. Ask them for me. I… can't yet ask the Elder to his face.
Ask Morris the guide and Haru the town clerk about the 'far chapter house'.
없군요. 길에도 없고 장부에도 없고요. 그래도 그게 없다는 증거는 아니에: So there is none. Not on the roads, not in the ledgers. Still, that isn't proof. Not being in the record and not existing are different things. An archivist must know that. …Haru said the Elder straightens his glove when he is thinking hard. Twenty years beside him and I never knew. I thought he was cold. This morning, when I brought up the portraits, he did it three times. I'll call it a family custom a little longer. Only until we're back from the desert.
수로를 따라 표석이 서 있어요. 시로크가 판 구간마다 누가 돌을 세웠어요: There are marker stones along the canal. Someone raised one for each stretch Sirok dug. The garden-keepers. A line on each. Three are left before the break, buried in sand. Clear them for me. I'll read. And the last handspan has to be dug by hand. Not with a shovel. Sirok had no shovel.
저주받은 피라미드 앞에서 이사벨과 함께 표석 셋의 모래를 걷고, 끊긴 수: In front of the Cursed Pyramid, clear the sand from three markers with Isabel and join the broken canal.
이어졌어요. 물이 넘어왔어요. 봤어요? 한 뼘을 넘는 데 천 년이 걸렸어: It's joined. The water crossed. Did you see? A thousand years to cross one handspan. I copied the markers. The garden-keepers spoke to Sirok every day. 'Twenty paces today, well done.' Sirok can't read. They wrote it anyway. Not for anyone to see. Because a day you write down is a day that happened. …That's why I write, too. Fetch water, please. The canal reaches, but filling the basin will take a while. I want it full while I read the king's writing.
문이 열렸어요. 정원이에요. 천 년 동안 아무도 못 본. 장로님은 혼자: The door is open. A garden no one has seen in a thousand years. The Elder went off to walk alone. Let's go in, the two of us. The king is sitting there, you said. Facing the door. The fountain is dry. Bring one bucket of water. The gatekeeper kept the promise, so this isn't a promise. Just a greeting.
저주받은 피라미드의 정원에서 왕의 자리를 살펴보고, 마른 분수에 물을 부: In the garden of the Cursed Pyramid, look at the king's seat and pour water into the dry fountain. (1 water bucket)
분수에 물이 고이니까 바닥에서 뭐가 떴어요. 씨앗이에요. 한 알. 분수: When the water pooled, something floated up. A seed. Just one. It must have been wedged in a crack. Will a thousand-year-old seed sprout? Who knows. Let's take it anyway. The writing on the king's knees. Only the last line again. 'When the door opens, to the one who opened it. I could not say that there is no end. You say it.' …Who is that for? Why does reading it make me think of the Elder?
그게 사막 왕의 정원에서 나온 씨예요? 와. 심어요! 수도회 올라가는 길: That's the seed from the desert king's garden? Wow. Let's plant it! I keep a patch by the road up to the Order. I tend it while I wait for travellers. You can have the sunniest spot. I called Lorenzo too. Nobody is more curious about what will grow.
Plant the garden's seed in Morris the guide's patch.
심었어요. 물은 제가 줄게요. 날마다요. …저기요, 조사대원님. 이상한: Planted. I'll water it. Every day. …Can I tell you something odd? Last night the Elder came down this road. Alone. The night you came back from the desert. He stood a long time in front of my patch. In front of an empty row. I asked what he was looking at and he said 'good sun here'. That's the very spot we just planted. And I only offered you that spot a moment ago.
기계 앞에 서랍이 있네. 벽 하나가 통째로 서랍일세. 이 도시 사람들은: There are drawers before the machine. A whole wall of them. This city asked the machine everything. You punched your question into a card and the machine reckoned an answer. The questions will still be there. The queen's too. Turn them over. See what people were asking by the time they stopped the clocks.
Go through the drawers of questions with Erwin in the Ancient Factory, in order.
밀값에서 시작했군. 그다음엔 혼삿날, 그다음엔 아들이 돌아오느냐. 그리고: It began with the price of wheat. Then wedding days, then whether a son would come home. And then when the end would be. When something that answers is always at hand, people cannot stop asking. They ask even what they must decide themselves. The queen was not a bad queen. She only asked what her people asked. …The bottom drawer was empty, you say. Yes. It would be. The machine was stopped, so whatever was put in never went through. Start the clock and it will. Whatever it holds.
기계가 종이를 뱉네. 밀린 답들일세. 천 년 치. 주워 보게. 나는… 저: The machine is spitting paper. The answers it owed. A thousand years of them. Gather them up. I… only need one sheet, in that corner. No, never mind. You gather. An old back can't. Don't read what you pick up; give it to me. It isn't fit reading. Dead people's questions.
Gather the answers spilled on the floor of the Ancient Factory in three places.
(장로는 받은 종이를 넘기지 않고 접는다.) 읽었군. 읽지 말랬는데. 괜: (The Elder folds the sheets without turning them.) You read them. I said not to. It's all right. Sera's answer was late. A thousand years. Her daughter lived, it said. The mother died not knowing. And the one sheet from the bottom drawer. 'Cannot be reckoned; the entry has been erased.' …Somebody's prank. The paper is recent. Some drifter got in. I'll keep that one. It isn't fit for the record. Don't mention it to Isabel. That child writes everything down.
인쇄지 받았어요. 장로님이 주라고 하셨다면서요. 표정이 어떠셨어요? …됐: I have the printout. The Elder told you to give it to me, didn't he. How did he look? …Never mind. Sit. This is about us. From the day we stepped onto the dock. The machine reckoned all of it a thousand years ago. But there's a mark at the end of each line. Look with me. I don't want to look alone.
Read the Harbinger's printout with Isabel the archivist.
'오차 있음'이 있죠. 여러 군데요. 기계가 셈한 대로 안 간 데가 있다: There are lines marked 'error'. Several. Places where things didn't go as reckoned. The Elder was right. People don't follow the sum. But why was he so angry saying it? People who are right don't get angry. People who hope they're right do. And the last line. 'The one who removes the glove is'. It breaks off there. The machine fell. What came after? A name? …I'll write it down. Broken off, as it is.
석판 뒤에 방이 있소. 사제들이 살던 데요. 마흔 대가. 돈 받고 그만둔: There are rooms behind the slab. Where the priests lived. Forty generations. I want to see what sort of people the six were who took the coin and stopped. Not to curse them. I held a lantern fifteen years. You think there was no day I wanted to stop? Their rooms will tell us why. I'll pick up the coins myself. I won't believe it till I've counted.
Walk through the priests' rooms in the Sunken City with Oscar, in order.
여섯 닢이오. 한 사람에 한 닢. 사람 하나가 대대로 부르던 노래를 한: Six coins. One each. A song a family sang for generations, sold for one coin. They didn't sell cheap. They didn't count the price at all. They needed an excuse. They were only waiting for someone to say 'you may stop'. Nobody said it in a thousand years. …The grey cloak knew that. That one knows what people wait for. Do you know why the last two refused? It was on the practice slab. They're brother and sister. If one stops, the other sings alone.
사제가 숨이 넘어가오. 혼자서는 마디 사이를 못 메우오. 우리가 메웁시다: The priest is out of breath. Alone, the gaps between bars can't be filled. Let's fill them. There are three sounding-stones in the temple, where the priests took turns. Sing there and the water carries it down. I'll take the middle. You move from stone to stone and take the bar up. Wrong notes don't matter. Only don't let it break. While the priest catches breath, we ready the Gate.
Carry the song on at the three sounding-stones of the Sunken City, in order.
됐소. 밑에서 돌아눕던 것이 다시 가라앉았소. 잠깐이오. 사제가 그럽디다: That's it. The thing that was turning over below has sunk back. For now. The priest says our singing is a 'dialect'. It's quiet because it's listening to something strange. It won't be fooled long. (Oscar starts to laugh and stops.) I held a lantern on the ice fifteen years. Couldn't stop. You ended that for me. My turn now. That song has to be ended for its singer. Let's put it to rest. Properly.
조사대원님! 오스카 씨가 바다에서 사람을 하나 데려왔어요! 물에서요! 사: Oscar brought someone up from the sea! A priest! The last of a family that did nothing but sing for a thousand years! But they won't eat. They've never had anything hot. You can't light a fire under the sea. I've never had a guest like this. I'm making mushroom stew; bring me the makings. It's a first meal. In a thousand years. It has to be good.
붉은 버섯 3개, 갈색 버섯 3개, 그릇 2개를 로렌초에게 가져가고, 사: Bring 3 red mushrooms, 3 brown mushrooms and 2 bowls to Lorenzo, and sit beside the priest.
드셨어요! 반 그릇이나요! 한 숟갈 드시고 한참 가만히 계시다가 '따뜻하: They ate! Half a bowl! One spoonful, then sat still a long time and said 'warm'. A word they'd never had cause to say. And all the while they hummed. Those eight bars. Without knowing. It comes out like breath. Mia and the village children heard and started singing along. Skipping rope to it. A thousand years of lullaby turned into a skipping song in half a day. The priest saw and laughed. Oscar says it's the first time he's seen it too.
벨라스의 자리 뒤에 벽감이 있네. 회의록을 넣어 두던 데지. 그는 회의가: There's an alcove behind Belas's seat. Where the minutes were kept. At the end of every sitting he sealed the record in wax. Whole. To read it the wax must come off. You do it. My hands… the gloves catch. Don't read aloud what you uncover. Sound stays long in this room.
Peel the wax from the alcove with Erwin in the Ruined Citadel, in order.
읽었군. 그래. 그게 회의일세. 일곱이 여섯 날을 앉아서 아무도 정하지: You read it. Yes. That was the council. Seven sat six days and none could decide. So they asked the scale. The scale that weighed the kings' disputes. Built on an island apart from the citadel. So that judgment would not look at the kings' faces. What the scale answered would have been in the last case, and that case is gone, you say. …Of all Belas covered, the deepest. Not covered. Removed. Let's go to the eighth seat. See that first.
장로님은 성채 다리 끝에서 멈추셨어요. '나는 저울에 오르지 않겠네.': The Elder stopped at the end of the bridge. 'I will not step onto the scale.' Then he sat with his back turned. We'll go ourselves. This was lying where the guardian fell. It looks like an eye, but it's no seal. It's a pathfinder. Throw it and it flies toward the island. The minutes said the question was sent to the scale. What the answer was, what was in the case Belas destroyed, will still be there. The one who answered wouldn't have erased it.
허공에서 저울의 섬을 찾아, 이사벨과 함께 법정을 차례로 살펴보세요. (: Find the Island of the Scale in the void and walk through the court with Isabel, in order. (Throwing the Eye of Geburah shows the way.)
판결이 없어요. 저울은 답을 못 했어요. 기울지 않았으니까요. 한 이름과: There is no judgment. The scale couldn't answer. It didn't tip. One name and the world weighed the same. So it sent back 'no judgment', and Belas destroyed that case. Why? With no judgment, the kings had to decide. And deciding made it their crime. …But the fire was divided. So who decided? No line anywhere says anyone did. And the scale is still turning. Still holding the same question after a thousand years. Unable to close the trial, it now tries whatever walks in. Walking. Standing still.
저울 얘기는 기록관한테 들었다. 재울 거라면서. 들어가기 전에 내 말을: The archivist told me about the scale. That you mean to put it to rest. Hear me first. I've stood before a thing like that. A man, not a stone. I came back having lost eleven and was questioned. There are places where anything you do is a crime. Run and you fled. Stand and you abandoned them. There's one way out of such a place alive. Hear which crime is being asked about now, and don't do that one thing. Try to keep them all and you'll keep none.
탐험대장 로란에게 저울 앞에서 싸우는 법을 듣고, 철 주괴 8개와 황금: Hear from Captain Roran how to fight before the scale, and bring 8 iron ingots and 2 golden apples.
됐다. 정리한다. 저울은 싸우는 동안 죄목을 바꿔 가며 내건다. 화면에: Good. Summing up. During the fight the scale posts one charge after another. It shows on your screen. Don't jump, don't stand still, don't circle sunwise, things like that. Keep only the one that's posted. Break it and you're marked a sinner and it hits harder. It floats where you can't reach, so watch for when the weapons come down. The fight begins on the Island of the Scale, when you lay a hand on the stand before it. A Memory Gate won't work there. One more thing. (Roran looks at his bootlace. Leaves it.) After the inquiry I was given 'no fault'. That was the hardest part. Don't say that to the scale. It's been unable to say it for a thousand years.
기울지 않는 저울: The Scale That Will Not Tip
가요. 저울을 재워요. 저는 판결의 벽 앞에 있을게요. 저 재판은 누가: Let's go. Put the scale to rest. I'll be at the wall of judgments. Someone has to close that trial. The ones who asked left a thousand years ago. You close it. I'll write that it's closed. Its name was at the top of the wall. Geburah. An old word for 'severity'.
On the Island of the Scale, lay a hand on the stand to open the trial, and put Geburah to rest.
It's closed. As it stopped, the scale tipped for the first time. Not to either side. Both pans sank together. And a new line was cut at the foot of the wall. Its last judgment. 'Judgment: this question cannot be weighed. Those who asked shall answer.' …It should have written that a thousand years ago. Not 'none' but 'you answer'. The kings pushed it onto the scale, and the scale had no words to hand it back. The Elder is waiting at the bridge. Let's tell him there was no answer. Then who decided? This time I'll be the one to ask.
다리 끝에서: At the End of the Bridge
…닫았군. 소리가 여기까지 들렸네. 접시가 내려앉는 소리가. 이사벨이 묻: …You closed it. I heard it from here. The pans settling. Isabel asked me: with no judgment, who decided? I didn't answer. It's the first time that child has asked me like that. Without looking away. You want to ask too. Sit. I can't tell all of it. I'll tell as far as I can.
하나 남았네. 서리 감옥. 그 자리는 나는 못 가네. 문 앞까지도. 거기: One left. The Frost Prison. I can't go there. Not even to the door. The child there… the king there knows me. Don't ask why. Ask when you return. I'll answer then. With the gloves off. I promise. (The Elder rises with a hand on the rail. The stone is warm only where he touched it.)
서리 감옥은 너희 조사대만 간다. 장로님은 못 간다 했고, 기록관은 따라: Only you go to the Frost Prison. The Elder says he can't, and the archivist follows only as far as the tomb door. I stay here beside the Elder. As eyes. Before you go, walk round the village once. Not an order. It's what's done before an expedition. I left without doing it and lost eleven. Those you never said goodbye to, you can't say it to even when you come back.
대장장이 브람, 어부 오스카, 안내인 모리스를 만나고 탐험대장 로란에게: See Bram the smith, Oscar the fisher and Morris the guide, then return to Captain Roran.
돌았나. 됐다. 다들 뭘 줬나. 묻지 않겠다. 줬을 거다. 이 마을 사람: Done? Good. What did they give you? I won't ask. They gave something. People here don't send a traveller off with empty pockets. Go. Sound carries far over snow. If anything happens I'll hear it. (Roran raises a hand. Doesn't lower it. Not until you've turned the corner.)
감방마다 벽에 한 줄씩 있어요. 왜 따라 들어왔는지요. 얼음이 덮어서 안: There's a line on the wall of every cell. Why they followed. The ice covers it. A torch will melt it. I can't read them all, but I want to read a few. Who they were, the ones who locked themselves in after an eighteen-year-old king. They can't all have been soldiers.
얼어붙은 감옥에서 횃불로 감방 셋의 얼음을 녹이세요. (횃불 3개): Melt the ice of three cells in the Frosted Prison with torches. (3 torches)
A cook, a drummer boy, a writing master. All wrote the same thing. 'It didn't seem right to leave him alone.' They didn't follow a king. They followed a child. Those are the draugr now. The ones we put to rest. …I came this far hating the kings. The ones who pushed things onto others. This king didn't. But everyone beside him took it on with him. Maybe neither is the answer, pushing it off or carrying it alone. I don't know. I'll only write.
왕관이 문 앞에 굴러가 멈췄잖아요. 그대로 두면 안 될 것 같아요. 문: The crown rolled to the door and stopped. It shouldn't be left like that. Set it upright at the door. Where the king can see it through the gap. If he calls 'brother?' and no one answers, he should at least know his brother came this far. Something is tucked inside the crown. Paper, I think. Look at that too.
Set the crown upright before the tomb door in the Frosted Prison.
편지였어요. 형이 썼어요. 부치지 못한. '네가 왕이 된 건 내가 싫다고: It was a letter. From the brother. Never sent. 'You became king because I said I wouldn't. It should have been me at that council. Then I'd have named the prisoner, I'd have been the one afraid, and you'd have been outside listening to the drum. A thousand years of sorry isn't enough. So I stand at the door.' The brother pushed something off too. The throne, onto his little brother. And then stood at the door a thousand years. …I read it through the gap. After a long while there was a voice. With the spelling of a boy. 'Brother is a fool.' And a little later. 'So am I.'
왔나. 장로님은 한 시간 전에 지나갔다. 뛰지 않았다. 걸었다. 나를 보: You're here. The Elder passed an hour ago. He didn't run. He walked. He saw me and bowed his head. First time in thirty years that man has bowed to me. I didn't stop him. It isn't a thing to stop. He went into the archive. Didn't lock it. He's waiting. Before you go in, count what you carry. One who goes to ask should know what they're bringing.
Count what you have gathered with Captain Roran and Isabel the archivist.
다 셌나. 그럼 가라. 나는 문밖에 선다. 칼은 안 뽑는다. 뽑을 일이: Counted? Then go. I stand outside the door. I won't draw. I hope I needn't. That man is the only one who took my side in the inquiry twenty years ago. Whether it was heart or reckoning, I don't want to know today. You find out. (Roran ties his bootlace. Slowly. And doesn't stand even when it's tied.)
장로님 방이에요. 문은 열려 있었어요. 잠근 적이 없는 방이에요. 저는: This is the Elder's room. The door was open. It has never been locked. I learned my letters here. But I have never once opened a drawer. Please open them with me. I said I'd read to the end.
Examine what is left in Erwin's room with Isabel the archivist.
문은 장로님이 지은 거였어요. 기억의 문이요. 우리가 온 첫 주에 장로님: The Gate was the Elder's own work. The Memory Gate. The first rule he taught us himself in the prologue. 'A guardian is put to rest only inside a Gate.' So the seals wouldn't burst, he said. That was true. But there was a second truth. The share of whatever is put to rest inside does not scatter. It runs to one place. To the brand. …We did that. Six times. With our own hands. But listen. In the corner of the drawing the Elder wrote down one worry. When I read that line I breathed for the first time.
이름을 적는 게 그냥 버릇인 줄 알았어요. 잠든 것들한테 미안해서 적은: I thought writing the names was only a habit. I wrote them because I felt sorry for the ones we put to rest. It was holding something, it turns out. Then I must write more. First I'll light the lantern again. Half a jar of my mother's ink is left. It was the Elder who told me that ash comes from the fire as it was before it learned the taste of names, that light at dusk. Funny, isn't it. Bring me just one blaze rod. Like the first time.
Bring 1 blaze rod to Isabel the archivist.
(등불이 켜진다. 전보다 작다. 그래도 켜졌다.) 됐어요. 이 불 밑에서: (The lantern lights. Smaller than before. But lit.) There. Under this light I read back every name I've written. The three captains of the Black Star. Horus. Helvar. Cornelia and the three hundred and thirty-two. The son who was given no name. The gatekeeper. Maledictus. Not one line has faded. The world has half forgotten them already, and here they're sharp. If this is what worried the Elder, this is our blade. Please go to Captain Roran. I'll write one more line and follow.
기록관한테 들었다. 문이 그 양반 거였다고. 그래서 스무 해 전에 나한테: The archivist told me. The Gate was his. So that's why he never taught it to me twenty years ago. Back then he was still counting how the shares burst and scattered. With eleven people. …I'll be angry later. He's gone to the Burning Arena. The bottom of hell, the seventh seal. Where the wick sleeps. I'm gathering the expedition. This time I go too. Even into land I don't know.
오스카, 브람, 펠릭스, 하루, 모리스. 다 왔다. 인원 확인은 돌아와서: Oscar, Bram, Felix, Haru, Morris. All here. I'll count heads when we're back. And get it right. …But the archivist is missing. The girl who said she'd write one more line and come. The lantern's lit in the archive and the pen is gone. The ink jar too. He took her. Or she followed on her own feet. She is that kind of girl.
지옥이다. 펠릭스가 그러더라. 열다섯 해 전 엘레나는 가는 데마다 잉크: Hell. Felix told me. Fifteen years ago Elena left an ink dot everywhere she went. For whoever came after. You followed them once already. Look. There on the basalt. A dot. Still wet. The girl made it. While being led away. This time the daughter marks and we follow. Stay behind me. Never mind the leg.
지옥에서 로란과 함께 이사벨이 남긴 잉크 점을 따라가고, 길을 막는 불타: Follow the ink dots Isabel left through hell with Roran, and put to rest 3 ignited revenants blocking the way.
점이 경기장 문 앞에서 끝났다. 마지막 점 옆에 글씨가 있다. 급하게 쓴: The dots end at the arena door. There's writing beside the last one. Hurried. 'I'm all right. I won't write it. Except one name.' …Except one name. She knows what has to be written. Did you pick up the ash the revenants dropped? They say it makes a sound in your fist. That's memory the fire spilled while eating. Listen and you'll know whose.
Give me that ash. The archivist's gone, so I'll do the listening. A fisherman has good ears. I listened under the ice for fifteen years. Makes a sound when you hold it, you said. I'll hold all three at once.
Hand the 3 memory shards to Oscar the fisherman.
(오스카가 조각을 쥐고 오래 눈을 감았다.) 아이요. 고아였소. 궁정 필: (Oscar holds the shards with his eyes shut a long time.) A boy. An orphan. Taken into a court scriptorium. Had no name till the king gave him one. Erwin. That king taught him his letters too. The next shard is loud. The day of the council. Someone dragged the boy out of the room. On the king's order. 'See that this child does not watch.' He clung to the arm of the throne and wouldn't let go, and his cloak tore. The last shard. When he broke the door and got back in, his teacher was already in the fire. The seven stood round it. The boy put his hand in. To pull him out. …That's all the man ever saw. Seven standing round, and his teacher burning.
꺼지지 않는 문: The Door That Won't Go Out
불꽃 경기장이다. 문 앞 결계는 최초의 불꽃 그 자체다. 물로는 안 꺼진: The Burning Arena. The ward on its door is the First Flame itself. Water won't put it out. That crystal Frostmaw was holding in the snow. The one the Elder said never to sell. He already meant it for this door. We use the key he had us make ready with his own hands. Hand me the crystal. I'll set it. Three of mine fell guarding that. The captain sets it.
결정이 녹으며 불길이 갈라졌다. 안이 보인다. 왕좌 앞에 기록관이 서 있: The crystal melted and the flames parted. You can see inside. The archivist is standing before the throne. Not bound. Her pen hand pressed to her chest. He's on his knees in front of her. Begging. Her. 'Write one line for me. The name the fire will give back. Even your mother couldn't.' She shakes her head. He stands and puts his hand into the fire. Something in armour rises out of it. The knight from the dreams.
손바닥에 적은 이름: A Name Written on a Palm
(불길 너머에서 이사벨이 소리친다.) 조사대원님! 들려요? 저는 괜찮아요: (Isabel shouts from beyond the flames.) Can you hear me? I'm all right! The Elder can't hurt me. He needs my hand! But he took my paper. I have ink and nowhere to write. Arden's name has to be written before he's put to rest. Anywhere! Revenants are in the way. Berserkers. Please clear them. Just while I write!
Put to rest the 3 ignited berserkers surrounding Isabel in the Burning Arena.
(이사벨이 왼손을 들어 보인다. 손바닥에 잉크로 세 글자가 적혀 있다.): (Isabel holds up her left hand. A name is written on the palm in ink.) I wrote it. Here. I had no paper. 'Arden.' The Elder saw. He saw and said nothing. He could have cut off my hand and he didn't. He only… smiled. A little. 'Just like your mother,' he said. Now put him to rest. Inside the Gate. The share won't go to the Elder. It'll stay on my palm. It will be a little hot, they say. I don't mind.
아르덴이다. 지금은 이그니스라고 부른다. 천 년 동안 불을 제 몸에 가둔: Arden. They call him Ignis now. A man who held the fire inside his own body for a thousand years. He kept saying it in the dreams. Don't come, the fire is rising past me. It has. That thing is half Arden and half fire. He splits the ground with a sword of flame, guards with his shield, and at the last wraps himself in blue fire. The whole expedition goes. Open the Memory Gate. His Gate, and this time we use it our way.
Open the Memory Gate and put Ignis to rest.
기사가 쓰러졌다. 눈에서 불이 꺼지고 사람의 눈이 돌아왔다. 몫은 문지방: The knight fell. The fire left his eyes and a man's eyes came back. The share ran over the threshold, and bent away in front of that man's hand. It went to the archivist's palm. And six strands came out of his brand after it. Without the wick they can't stay pooled. The six strands ran toward the archive. To the written names. Back where they belong. He sat down in the ash. The back of his hand went cold. For the first time in a thousand years. Arden looked at him and spoke. I heard it clearly. Go and hear it from the archivist. She took it down.
그 문을 지킨 사람: The One Who Kept That Door
아르덴 님이 잠들기 전에 한 말이에요. 장로님한테 한 말이요. 저는 손이: What Arden said before he slept. He said it to the Elder. My hand shook and I got it wrong twice. But I have all of it. Please read it with me. The Elder is sitting over there. In the ash. He hasn't said a word yet.
Read Arden's words, taken down by Isabel the archivist, together.
스스로 걸어 들어가신 거였어요. 여덟째 왕은요. 쫓겨난 게 아니라. 일곱: He walked in himself. The eighth king. He wasn't driven out. The seven didn't feed him to it. When someone said to use a prisoner's name he stood and said, 'A world kept with someone else's name has not been kept.' And he sent his apprentice out of the room. Because that boy would follow him in if he saw. The Elder never knew. For a thousand years. Hating the seven. …The Elder just spoke for the first time. 'Then who was I angry at?' I don't think he was asking me.
(재 위에 노인이 앉아 있다. 장갑이 없다. 손등의 획은 식어서 흉터가: (An old man sits in the ash. No glove. The stroke on his hand has cooled into a scar. He looks far older. He looks his age.) …Sit. I haven't the strength to stand. Take out what's inside my coat. My hands can't hold paper now. It's the original of the oath. What Elena was looking for. With the third line.
Take the original oath from inside Erwin's coat and read it together.
그분의 글씨일세. 불에 들어가시기 전날 밤에 내 필통에 넣어 두신 쪽지지: It is his hand. A note he slipped into my pen case the night before he went into the fire. Three lines. 'Keep the Flame. Keep the seals. And when the time comes, let me go.' I built the Order on the first two. The third I erased. For a thousand years I read that line as 'let the world drop him'. Words the seven made him write. Forced. …If he went of his own will, then that line was a request. Made to me. For a thousand years I disobeyed the last thing my teacher asked of his apprentice.
이그니스가 쓰러진 자리에 남은 회색 재요. 그건 불의 재가 아니에요. 장: The grey ash left where Ignis fell. That isn't the fire's ash. It fell from the Elder's brand. A thousand years of it. The ink of ash is made from ash. Mix ink from that and you can write one line. Exactly one. Whether to write the name 'Erwin' in the Chronicle or not, that's the line. I can't decide. I learned my letters from his hand, and I lost my mother because of him. Please decide for me. Either way I will write it as you say.
Hand the thousand-year-old ash to Isabel the archivist, and decide the one line.
썼어요. 정해 주신 대로요. 잉크가 마르는 동안 장로님이 옆에서 보고 계: It's written. As you decided. While the ink dried the Elder stood beside me watching. He said nothing. When it was dry he said one thing. 'Good strokes.' …That's all. He has gone down to the Order's cellar. To the room where Kas was. On his own. The door isn't locked. Captain Roran's orders. 'Come out if you want. But each time you do, say the eleven names first.'
부두로 와 주세요. 폭풍이 그친 날 처음 내린 그 부두요. 다들 나와 있: Please come to the dock. The one where you first landed in the prologue. Everyone is there. I want to write the last page of the Chronicle there. Not in the archive. My mother was the one who read to the end. I'll be the one who writes to the end. Before I write, say a word to each of them. That's what an expedition does, I'm told.
부두에서 어부 오스카, 탐험대장 로란과 인사하고, 기록관 이사벨과 마지막: At the dock, speak with Oscar the fisherman and Captain Roran, and write the last page with Isabel the archivist.
\"불을 지키고, 봉인을 지키고, 그리고 때가 되어 놓아주었다.\" 마지: "We kept the Flame, we kept the seals, and when the time came we let go." The last page. I wrote it in the name of every member of the expedition, one by one. Everyone who came on the seventeen ships. Yours too. In the ink of ash. Fire can't eat it. The First Flame is still there. Every seven days it will burn again in Arden's shape. Each time, put it to rest inside the Gate. The share goes to no one now. It goes to the name. That is what keeping meant. From the beginning.
조사대원님, 미아가 할 말이 있대요. 그날 불 속에서 구해 준 그 아이요: Mia has something to tell you. The girl you carried out of the fire that day. Hearing that you saw the council of eight kings in the Abyss reminded her of something. She says she can't tell me. She will if you're here.
보랏빛으로 고친 자국이라니. 누가 연대기를 고쳐 썼다는 거예요. 불에 탄: Corrections in purple. Someone rewrote the Chronicle. The shelves burned, but it stayed in Mia's eyes. And Mia says the corrected hand 'wasn't in a hurry'. Not altered like a theft. Altered like something cherished. Stroke by stroke. That's stranger still.
항해일지 사이의 도면이요. 보랏빛 잉크였죠. 늪의 마녀 단지 밑바닥에 있: The drawing between the logbook's pages. Purple ink, wasn't it. The colour at the bottom of the witch's jar in the swamp. Her tag said 'Left here by the people in the mirror.' If someone leaves a thing, someone comes to collect it. Please look at that shelf again. Take a glass pane with you this time. Reversed writing has to be held up to glass to be read.
늪지대 오두막의 보랏빛 단지를 유리판에 비춰 보세요. (유리판 1개): Hold the purple jar in the swamp hut up to a glass pane. (1 glass pane)
빈 병을 하나 들고 오셨군요. 바닥에 거울 문양이 있어요. 그리고 병 안: You brought back one of the empty bottles. There's a mirror mark on the base. And tiny writing on the inside. Reversed. 'Bring the pages and I will fill it. Before that child does.' …Before that child. Two bounties were posted in your first days here. The grey coin with two different faces. One was the Elder's, one was this person's. For the same pages, each trying to reach them first.
안개가 걷힌 저택: The Mansion Out of the Mist
마지막 장을 쓰고 나서요. 빈 줄 하나 남겨 뒀다고 했죠. 그 줄을 채울: After I wrote the last page. I told you I left one line empty. If anyone can fill it, it's the owner of the purple ink. The mansion in the dark forest. The Ashen Band's ancestral house. Wrapped in purple mist for a thousand years so no one could enter. But the mist has lifted since yesterday. Since the day the Elder's brand went cold. Let's go together. This time I'll follow you. There will be things to read.
Find the woodland mansion in the dark forest and examine the mirror room underground with Isabel.
Eight mirrors. Five of them showed the five stones of the Rune Altar. Attack, defence, evasion… the five letters with those silly names laid over them. The sixth showed the back of a hand. The seventh a single dot. The eighth was dark and only hummed. Eight letters. It's a name. This person held up a mirror at the moment the name burned and saved five letters. And for a thousand years had us touch them every day. As a gacha. …Not hidden. Entrusted.
천 번 고쳐 쓴 한 줄: One Line Rewritten a Thousand Times
거울 뒷면에 문이 있었어요. 필경실이에요. 책상 하나, 의자 하나, 그리: There was a door behind the mirrors. A scriptorium. One desk, one chair, and paper. The room is full of paper. All the same page. One page of the Chronicle rewritten a thousand times. There are doorkeepers. The Ashen Band's axemen. They won't stop us reading. They will stop us if we try to carry out even one sheet. Please don't hate them. To them the master of this house is the only elder who ever promised to find their lineage.
숲속 저택에서 필경실의 초고를 살펴보고, 초고를 들고 나오는 길을 막는: Examine the drafts in the scriptorium of the woodland mansion, and defeat the 2 doorkeepers who bar the way out with a draft.
천 번이에요. 같은 한 줄을요. '일곱이 여덟째를 일으켜 세웠다.' 처음: A thousand times. The same single line. 'The seven raised the eighth to his feet.' In the first hundred sheets the hand shakes. The strokes waver. The handwriting of someone writing a lie for the first time. Further on it steadies. He got used to it. And the note in the desk drawer. 'That child must not know. If he learns the teacher went of his own will he will read it as being abandoned. Give him something to hate. Hate keeps a person alive.' …He means the Elder. This person rewrote the Chronicle to keep the Elder alive.
거울 속 사람이 우리를 막아요. 벨로크래요. 초고 귀퉁이마다 서명이 있었: The one in the mirror is barring our way. Velok. The signature was in the corner of every draft. Court scribe to the eighth king. The Elder's senior. He bars the way because he fears we'll take the original to the Elder. He doesn't know the Elder already knows. News from outside doesn't seem to reach inside a mirror. Let's try speaking to him first. They say he reads what you write with a finger on a fogged mirror in the scriptorium. If that fails… being inside a mirror, he can only be reached through a Memory Gate. Then please put him to rest. And tell him as you do. That the child bore it.
필경실의 거울에 글을 써 말을 걸어 본 뒤, 기억의 문을 열고 거울 속의: Write on the scriptorium mirror to speak to him, then open the Memory Gate and put Velok, the scribe in the mirror, to rest.
거울이 전부 깨졌어요. 여덟 장이 한꺼번에요. 깨지면서 벨로크가 물었대요: Every mirror broke. All eight at once. As they broke Velok asked, 'The child knows? Knows and is still standing?' And after a long while: 'Then for a thousand years I underrated him.' One sheet was left among the shards. Not purple. Black ink. The original, unaltered. Just one. He rewrote a thousand sheets and never could alter that one.
고치지 못한 한 장: The One Page He Couldn't Alter
The original. The one page Velok never managed to alter. I washed my hands before reading. Please read it with me. This was written by someone who was in the room that day. Arden was outside the door, and the King of Frost shut his eyes in fear, he said. Velok was inside, taking it down. He was the scribe.
Read the unaltered original with Isabel the archivist.
다 읽었어요. 여덟째 왕은 제자가 손을 넣을 걸 알았어요. 그래서 벨로크: I've read it all. The eighth king knew his apprentice would put his hand in. So he asked Velok. To hold a mirror. To catch the name as it burned. Not all of it could be saved, but some letters might remain. 'When that child is able to let me go, give them back to him then.' Velok waited a thousand years for that 'when'. For the child to become able to let go. And he knew the hatred he had handed him was keeping that day from coming. …Five letters are in the altar. The sixth is on the Elder's hand. Only the seventh and eighth remain. I think I know where they are.
일곱째 글자는 점이에요. 어머니가 찾은 곳마다 찍던 잉크 점요. 어머니는: The seventh letter is a dot. The ink dot my mother left wherever she found something. She saw that shape on one unaltered page. She used it as a mark without knowing what it meant. It was a letter. The eighth is a sound. Some letters are written only as sound, it seems. The cry the dragon of the void gave as it fell. That dragon kept the eighth king's dirge. For a thousand years it held the last sound of its master's name in its throat. The echo shard took it down. Down in the deep dark. Bring me one shard. I'll fit them together at the altar.
메아리 조각 1개를 기록관 이사벨에게 가져가고, 룬 제단 앞에서 여덟 글: Bring 1 echo shard to Isabel the archivist, and fit the eight letters together at the Rune Altar.
(이사벨이 한 줄을 적는다. 재의 잉크로. 천천히. 또박또박.) 다섯 돌: (Isabel writes one line. In the ink of ash. Slowly. Each stroke clear.) Five stones. The stroke on a hand. An ink dot. And a dragon's cry. Joined, they make a sound. 'Orel.' In the old tongue it means dawn. King of the Isle of Dawn. Through hundreds of pulls at the altar you were touching five letters of this name. I'd been looking at the seventh since the first day you arrived. The Elder held the sixth in his hand for a thousand years. Each of us carrying a piece, and none of us able to read it. I've filled the empty line. One thing is left. Whether to let the Elder hear this name.
(수도회 지하. 문은 열려 있다. 노인이 벽을 보고 앉아 있다.) 자네군: (The Order's cellar. The door is open. An old man sits facing the wall.) It's you. I know the step. And Isabel. Carrying a sheet of paper. …I won't ask what that paper is. If I ask, I shall ask for it. He asked to be let go. I have chosen to let go. Only days ago. My hand still feels empty. You decide. I have no right to.
Decide whether to let Erwin hear his teacher's name.
(이사벨이 연대기를 덮는다.) 적었어요. 이것도요. 조사대원님이 정한 대: (Isabel closes the Chronicle.) I wrote it. This too. As you decided. I wrote Velok's name as well. 'The senior who wrote a kind lie. For a thousand years he repeated his teacher's name, one letter a day.' The mirrors are all broken but the Rune Altar stands. The five stones look like letters now. I'll still call them by those silly names. Attack, defence, evasion. The teacher would have laughed, he said. So let him laugh.
조사대원님, 장부를 정리하다 이상한 것을 찾았습니다. 폭풍 조사대의 배: Surveyor, I found something odd while tidying the ledgers. The Storm Survey Corps' ships. Seventeen have come from across the sea so far. Would you look at the arrival records side by side.
Go through the arrival ledger with Haru the town clerk.
정리하겠습니다. 열일곱 척 전부 폭풍 속에 입항했습니다. 한 척도 예외가: Let me sum up. All seventeen came in under a storm. Not one exception. Yet no ship was wrecked. Not a sail torn. The crews say the same thing: 'the storm circled the ship once and passed.' …The Order gave the 'Storm Survey Corps' its name. I took it to mean you survey storms. Perhaps it meant the ships a storm surveys. Ledgers cannot lie.
조사대원님 앞으로 꾸러미가 왔어요. 동쪽 망루 쪽에서 화살에 묶여 날아왔: A bundle came for you. Tied to an arrow, from the direction of the eastern tower. One line in charcoal on the outside: 'The debtor remembers.' It's Kas. The captain you let go. Let's open it together. …Honestly, I'm a little afraid.
Open the bundle Kas sent together with Isabel the archivist.
깃발 조각이었어요. 노래의 둘째 절이 수놓인. 그리고 그 사이에 깨진 인: A scrap of banner. With the second verse of the song stitched on it. And between the folds a broken piece of a seal. Handed down in Kas's family, he says. 'What an ancestor who stepped off a ship was holding.' So not all of the Ashen Band descend from those left on land. Some stepped off ships. Which ships?
벽에 남은 둘째 절: The Second Verse on the Wall
조사대원님, 수도회 지하에 같이 가 주세요. 카스의 방이요. 밥을 가져갔: Surveyor, come down under the Order with me. To Kas's cell. I brought his meal and it was empty. Still locked. I asked the Elder and he said only 'I let him go.' He wouldn't say why. There's something scratched on the wall. I'm afraid to read it alone.
In the empty cell under the Order, examine what is left on the wall.
노래의 둘째 절이었어요. 손톱으로 긁은. 그리고 침상 밑에 이 인장 조각: It was the second verse of the song. Scratched with fingernails. And this piece of a seal under the cot. Left on purpose. The lowest line on the wall is for us. 'Your Elder listened to this song at the door every night. He wept at the second verse. Ask him why.' …I can't ask. Not yet.
서기 양반이 폭풍 얘기를 묻더군. 조사대 배마다 따라붙는 그 폭풍 말이오: The clerk asked me about storms. The one that follows every Corps ship. I've cast nets in that sea all my life. Once, just once, I went into the middle of it. When I was young. I'll tell you. In return bring me a nautilus shell. They only came up in the net the day after that storm passed. Haven't caught one in years. The storm's been pinned in the north.
Bring 1 nautilus shell to Oscar the fisherman and hear his story.
그래, 이거요. 귀에 대 보시오. 파도 소리가 아니지. 가락이오. 그 폭: Yes, this. Hold it to your ear. That's not waves. It's a tune. The tune I heard inside that storm. …I heard it the year the sea froze, too. The night before. Very near. From where Captain Cornelia's ship had gone. I never told anyone. I didn't know whether the storm followed the ship or the ship sailed into the storm.
다섯 개를 다 모으셨군요. 은화, 비늘, 악보, 일지 조각, 인장. 책상: You have all five. The coin, the scale, the song, the log scrap, the seal. I laid them out on the desk and looked at them for three days. They aren't separate things. They all belonged to one person. They fell out of one logbook. Let's piece them together. You picked them up, so your eyes will see it first. And I don't think I'll want to be alone when I've read it.
Fit the five clues together with Isabel the archivist.
여덟째 왕에게는 쌍둥이 누이가 있었어요. 새벽의 섬의 제독. 왕을 회의에: The eighth king had a twin sister. Admiral of the Isle of Dawn. She carried the king to the council by ship and promised to come out and welcome him when he returned. The day his name burned she was at sea, and she wrapped her fleet in a storm. Because the world cannot see inside the eye of a storm. So she was not forgotten. But she forgot whom she had come to meet. For a thousand years she has looked into every passing ship. Ours too. …Surveyor, she is no monster. She is keeping a promise.
기록관 아가씨한테 들었소. 그 폭풍 안에 사람들이 천 년째 있다고. 내가: The archivist girl told me. That there have been people inside that storm for a thousand years. The ones I saw on that deck. …Let's find a wreck. Now and then a ship gets pushed out of the storm. Once it's outside the eye it eats a thousand years in a day. Rots and sinks. What's left aboard will tell us how they live in there. I'm coming. I know a little about waiting at sea.
Find a shipwreck with Oscar and examine what is left in the cabin.
밧줄이 전부 사려져 있었소. 던질 수 있게. 천 년 동안 매일 다시 사렸: Every rope was coiled. Ready to throw. Re-coiled every day for a thousand years. And that roster. The column for the day each sailor disembarked, empty all the way down. Not one went ashore. Nobody leaves until the admiral has finished her welcome. …Just like Captain Cornelia. Nobody dies on my ship. Nobody leaves this one. Captains.
폭풍의 눈 속으로: Into the Eye of the Storm
…앉게. 이사벨이 내게 왔었네. 다섯 조각을 들고. 아무 말도 안 하고: …Sit. Isabel came to me. With the five pieces. Laid them on my desk without a word. She did not ask. So I will tell. I know her. My master's… no. The old king's sister. You hold the storm eye? Then the storm will let you in. Go to the palace on the sea. And see there, for yourself, what I did.
Carrying the storm eye, find the palace on the sea and examine the empty banquet hall.
보았군. 차려 둔 상을. …그래. 내가 보냈네. 코넬리아의 배를. 그분이: So you saw the table she keeps laid. …Yes. I sent it. Cornelia's ship. I wanted to hear whether, when she looked into a ship, she would speak the name of the one she sought. I told the captain to write it down. She did not speak a name. She does not know it. And in the middle of the storm a frightened sailor dropped anchor, and the anchor struck the seal. The sea froze. I burned a ship to hear one name. I have no excuse. Go and put her to rest. I cannot. She knows my face. She would ask me: 'Where is the boy?'
가는 거요? 그럼 이걸 들고 가시오. 내 등불이오. 아들이 돌아온 날 끈: You're going? Then take this. My lamp. The one I put out the day my son came home. You don't tell someone who waits 'that's enough' with a sword. Still, there's no getting through that storm without one. She isn't bound to a seal but to a promise, the archivist says, so she can't be brought into a gate. You face her in the heart of the storm. The lightning has eight forks. Mind the eighth. That one she throws herself.
바다 위의 궁에서 폭풍의 여제 스킬라를 잠재우세요. (최대 체력의 10%: In the palace on the sea, put Scylla the Storm Empress to rest. (Deal at least 10% of her health.)
The storm lifted. I saw it all from the dock. Stars in the northern sky for the first time in a thousand years. And the ships came in. Ships with lightning on their sails. People stepped ashore. One by one. Each touched ground and looked back. For the admiral. …Go to the archivist. She's standing on the dock with the roster. Says she'll fill in the 'day disembarked'.
You were on the dock. I was taking down the sailors' names. More than three hundred. Every one wrote today's date under 'day disembarked'. But the top line is left. The admiral's. She asked you at the end, they say. Where that person is. You know, don't you. Where the eighth king is. And that he chose it. What did you tell her?
Tell Isabel the archivist what you answered the Storm Empress.
적을게요. 맨 윗줄에. 「마중하는 이」. 새벽의 섬의 제독. 누구를 맞으: I'll write it. On the top line. 'She Who Welcomes'. Admiral of the Isle of Dawn. Who laid a table for a thousand years after forgetting whom she had come to meet. Day disembarked… I'll leave it blank. She did not disembark. She went to meet him. Truly, this time. (Isabel closes the roster.) Surveyor. In the prologue they said our ship broke through a storm. It didn't. She looked at each face, and let us pass.
(장로의 자리는 비어 있다. 책상 위에 장갑 한 켤레가 놓여 있다. 안쪽: (The Elder's seat is empty. A pair of gloves lies on the desk. The insides are scorched.)
…It's you. I know your footsteps. The door is open. Roran told me not to lock it.
불을 지키고… (장로의 눈이 창날에 머문다.) …오늘은 그 빛이 조용하군: Guard the flame… (The Elder's eyes rest on the spearhead.) …That light is quiet today. I am glad of it.
…그 창. (장로가 한 걸음 물러선다. 장갑 낀 손을 등 뒤로 감춘다.): …That spear. (The Elder takes a step back and hides his gloved hand behind him.) The light of dusk. Where did you come by it?
천 년 전, 일곱 왕이 불을 일곱 눈에 나누어 봉인했지. 그 봉인을 지켜: A thousand years ago, seven kings divided the fire among seven Eyes and sealed it. Watching over those seals is our work.
Is your ember well? If the inside of your pocket is warm, it is well.
불씨는 쥔 사람의 이름을 한 번 붙들어 주네. 한 번뿐일세. 그러니 아끼: The ember will hold on to its bearer's name once. Only once. So spend it with care.
Do not give it to another. Especially… no, it is nothing.
가까이 대지 말게. …아니, 위험해서가 아닐세. 내 쪽이 부끄러워서 그러: Do not bring it close. …No, not because it is dangerous. Because I am ashamed.
That is the fire from before it devoured everything, from when it still kept memory. The First Flame did not burn names at first. It only remembered. By the light of dusk. People sat beside it and spoke the names of their dead, and the fire listened. That was all.
먹였기 때문일세. 일곱 왕이. 자기 왕국이 영원히 기억되길 바라서, 족보: Because it was fed. By the seven kings. They wanted their kingdoms remembered forever, so they burned their lineages and chronicles into the fire. 'Remember this too, and this.' The fire tasted names for the first time. After that it began to eat without being given.
The Chronicle says only that 'the fire overflowed.' It does not say who made it overflow. …I read this in a book. A very old book.
자네가 든 그것은 불이 맛을 들이기 전날에 떼어 낸 걸세. 그래서 자신을: What you carry was taken from the fire the day before it learned that taste. That is why it will not let the name of one who accepts it burn. Not in any hand. Only in a hand that accepted that fire without fearing it. (He looks down at his gloved hand.) It is not like stolen fire. I never accepted it. I only clutched it.
Where did you hear that song? …As far as the second verse.
\"마중 나간 누이는 돌아오지 않았다.\" 그래. 돌아오지 않았지. 마중: "The sister who went out to meet them did not return." Yes. She did not return. Because she went out to meet someone. One cannot come back until the one awaited has come.
나는 바다를 잘 안 보네. 눈이 시려서라고 했지. 거짓말일세. 폭풍이 보: I do not look at the sea much. I told you it stings my eyes. That was a lie. I do not look because I might see the storm. Because the storm might know me.
Ask me no more. When the time comes, I will speak first.
천 년이 길었느냐고. 길지 않았네. 매일 첫 줄이 같았으니. 하루를 천: Was a thousand years long, you ask. It was not. Every day began with the same first line. I lived one day for a thousand years.
이제 일기 첫 줄을 바꿨네. '오늘은 이사벨이 등불 심지를 갈았다.' 그: I have changed the first line of my diary now. 'Today Isabel changed the lantern wick.' I write things like that. There turns out to be a great deal to write.
There is no way to repay what I did to you all. So I will not say that I will repay it. I will remember. That is something I am good at.
형은 왼손잡이였네. 그래서 글씨가 뒤집혀 보였지. 거울 글씨는 형이 숨기: My brother was left-handed. That is why his writing looked reversed. He did not write mirror script to hide anything. He simply wrote that way.
스승님이 그러셨지. '벨로크는 세상을 거울로 보는 아이다. 그러니 남들이: Our master used to say, 'Belloc is a child who sees the world in a mirror. So he sees the side others cannot.' My brother saw the side I could not bear to.
Surveyor! If you learn anything new, please tell me first.
(이사벨이 잉크병 뚜껑을 슬쩍 닫는다.) 아, 조사대원님. 그 창이 가까: (Isabel quietly closes the lid of her inkwell.) Oh, Surveyor. When that spear comes near, the ink gets restless. It's all right, I don't mind it.
조사대원님, 그 창이요. …잠깐만요. 창날에 제 잉크병이 비쳤는데, 잉크: Surveyor, that spear. …Wait a moment. My inkwell was reflected in the blade, and the ink glowed. Just now.
일곱 왕과 눈: The seven kings and the Eyes
The Chronicle says the seven kings divided the fire into seven Eyes.
화로, 물길, 톱니, 물결, 눈꽃, 닫힌 입, 그리고 불꽃. 왕마다 문장: Hearth, waterway, cogwheel, wave, snowflake, closed mouth, and flame. Each king has one crest.
눈이 어디 있는지는 연대기에 없어요. 잊은 게 아니라 일부러 안 적은 것: The Chronicle does not say where the Eyes are. I don't think it was forgotten. I think it was left out on purpose.
I hear the Sculptor said 'the seals are eight.'
연대기에는 일곱뿐이에요. 그런데 왕의 문장을 그린 쪽을 보면 자리가 여덟: The Chronicle has only seven. But the page with the kings' crests has eight spaces. One is empty.
긁어낸 자국이 없어요. 처음부터 비워 둔 것처럼 매끈해요. 그게 더 이상: There are no scrape marks. It is smooth, as if it was left blank from the beginning. That is what's stranger.
놓아준 선장: The captain who was let go
카스는 깃발의 노래가 적힌 한 장을 품에 넣고 갔어요. 읽을 줄 모른대요: Kass left with one page tucked in his coat, the one with the banner's song. He says he can't read. He took it anyway.
문턱에서 돌아보더니 그랬어요. '빚은 진 쪽이 기억한다.' …무슨 뜻인지: He looked back at the threshold and said, 'The one who owes is the one who remembers.' …I still don't know what he meant.
그 뒤로 동쪽 망루의 깃발이 하나 줄었대요. 로란 대장님이 세어 보셨어요: Since then there is one flag fewer on the eastern watchtower. Captain Roran counted. Twice.
넘겨진 선장: The captain who was handed over
Kass is beneath the Order. The Elder took charge of him personally.
밥을 가져다주러 갔더니 노래를 부르고 있었어요. 그 노래요. 가사를 받아: When I went to bring him food, he was singing. That song. I wrote down the words.
장로님이 그 방 앞에 오래 서 계시는 걸 봤어요. 문은 안 여시고요. 그: I saw the Elder stand outside that room for a long time. He didn't open the door. He just… listened.
불씨를 내미는 척하셨죠. 그 틈에 제가 등불을 들고 물러섰어요. 불은 뺏: You pretended to hold out the ember. In that moment I took the lantern and stepped back. The fire was taken, but the lamp remained.
\"불을 지키고, 봉인을 지킨다.\" 장로님 앞에서 장로님이 가르친 서약: "Guard the flame, guard the seals." You refused him, in front of the Elder, with the oath the Elder taught.
천 년 묵은 재로 쓴 한 줄: One line written in thousand-year-old ash
에르윈. 적었어요. 정해 주신 대로요. '스승이 지어 준 이름. 천 년을: Erwin. I wrote it. As you decided. 'A name given by his master. He defied for a thousand years, and at the end he let go.'
어머니 이름 바로 아래 줄이에요. 일부러 그랬어요. 어머니가 그 사람을: It is the line right under my mother's name. I did that on purpose. Because my mother read that man to the very end.
I don't know if I have forgiven him. I wrote him down. Writing and forgiving are different. Still, I wrote.
그 한 줄에는 엘레나부터 적었어요. 카엘, 원정대 열한 명, 코넬리아의: In that one line I wrote Elena first. Kael, the eleven of the expedition, Cornelia's three hundred and thirty-two. I wrote small in case the ash ran out.
장로님 이름은 없어요. 그분도 그게 맞다고 했어요. '내 이름은 스승님이: The Elder's name is not there. He said that was right. 'My name was given to me by my master, so it is enough that my master knows it.'
…없다고 잊는 건 아니에요. 저는 기억해요. 글씨 가르쳐 준 손을요. 적: …Not being written is not being forgotten. I remember. The hand that taught me my letters. I only did not write it down.
기록관의 잉크에는 불씨의 재를 섞어요. 그래서 불이 못 먹어요. 그런데: We mix ember ash into an archivist's ink. That is why the fire cannot eat it. But no one ever knew why the ash keeps it from burning. We were simply taught so.
그 창 곁에 잉크병을 두면 재가 가라앉지 않고 떠요. 같은 불이에요. 잉: If I set my inkwell beside that spear, the ash does not sink. It rises. It is the same fire. The ash in the ink was never the ash of the fire that burns names. It is the ash of the fire before it devoured, the dusk light inside that spear.
첫 기록관들은 그 불 곁에서 썼대요. 연대기 첫 장 여백에 한 줄 있어요: They say the first archivists wrote beside that fire. There is a line in the margin of the Chronicle's first page: 'Write at dusk, and dry it by the fire of dusk.' I thought it was a timetable.
▷ 그럼 지금 쓰는 재는 어디서 나오죠?: ▷ Then where does the ash you use now come from?
…천 년 전에 긁어모은 걸 아껴 쓰는 거예요. 수도회 창고에 단지가 일곱: …We are sparing what was scraped together a thousand years ago. There were seven jars in the Order's storeroom. Half a jar is left. When it runs out, I can write names but I can no longer keep them. That spear is… the only one of that fire that remains.
하빈저가 뱉은 종이요. 천 년 전에 셈한 건데 우리 얘기가 있어요. 날짜: The paper the Harbinger spat out. It was reckoned a thousand years ago, and yet it speaks of us. Down to the date.
\"불씨를 쥔 자들, 열일곱 번째 배로 도착.\" 맞아요. 하루 씨 장부: "Those who hold the ember arrive on the seventeenth ship." It's true. Haru's ledger says seventeen ships.
그런데 줄마다 끝에 숫자가 있어요. '오차'래요. 어떤 줄은 오차 없음이: But every line ends with a number. It says 'error.' Some lines have no error, and some have a large one. The lines where you chose something, Surveyor.
"The Ashen captain, handed over." That is what the machine reckoned. But you let him go.
그 줄 끝에 이렇게 찍혀 있어요. '오차 있음. 다시 셈할 수 없음.': At the end of that line it is stamped: 'Error. Cannot be reckoned again.' The machine was wrong. Because of you.
"The Ashen captain, handed over. No error." It got this line right.
그 다음 줄이 이상해요. '넘겨진 자, 문 안에서 노래함. 듣는 자 있음: The next line is strange. 'The one handed over sings inside the door. Someone listens.' The machine reckoned even that. It does not say who listens.
인쇄지: 태양의 땅: Printout: the land of the sun
\"남은 대장, 죽은 벗에게 진실을 말하지 않음.\" 기계는 그렇게 봤어: "The captain who remained does not tell his dead friend the truth." That is how the machine saw it. But he told him.
'Error.' I never knew I could be so fond of one word.
\"남은 대장, 죽은 벗에게 진실을 말하지 않음. 오차 없음.\": "The captain who remained does not tell his dead friend the truth. No error."
기계가 맞혔다고 그게 틀린 선택은 아니에요. 로란 대장님은 그걸 지고 걷: The machine being right does not make it the wrong choice. Captain Roran is carrying that as he walks. That is walking, too.
\"어부, 등불을 끄지 못함.\" 그런데 껐죠. 조사대원님이 옆에 있어서: "The fisherman cannot put out the lantern." But he did. Because you were beside him.
'Error.' It seems the machine cannot reckon with someone standing at your side.
\"어부, 등불을 끄지 못함. 오차 없음.\" 그런데 그 뒤에 한 줄 더: "The fisherman cannot put out the lantern. No error." But there is one more line after it.
'바다가 다 녹는 날, 두 손이 끔.' 두 손이요. 약속하셨다면서요. 기: 'On the day the sea has fully thawed, two hands put it out.' Two hands. I hear you promised. Let the machine be right about that one.
마지막 줄은 장갑 얘기예요. '그 손을 이끄는 것은 장갑이다. 오차 없음: The last line is about the glove. 'What guides that hand is the glove. No error.'
그런데 그 밑에 한 줄이 반쯤 찍히다 말았어요. '장갑을 벗기는 것은': But under it, a line was half printed and stopped. 'What removes the glove is' and no further. The paper ends there. Because the machine fell.
…우리가 끊은 거예요. 답을 못 듣게. 아니면, 아직 안 정해져서 못 찍: …We cut it off. So we could not hear the answer. Or perhaps it could not print what has not been decided yet.
서리의 왕에게 한 대답: The answer to the King of Frost
'무섭다, 그래서 이름을 적어 줄 사람 곁에서 싸운다'고 하셨죠. 묘실: You said, 'I am afraid, so I fight beside the one who will write my name.' At the door of the burial chamber.
My hand shook as I wrote that down. Because the one who writes the names is me. I did not know then how great a thing that was.
지옥에서 손바닥에 이름을 적을 때 그 말이 생각났어요. 무서웠어요. 그래: When I wrote a name on my palm in the Nether, I remembered those words. I was afraid. I wrote anyway. Because someone was fighting beside me.
'무섭지 않다, 끝이 있으니까 걷는 거다'라고 하셨죠. 묘실 문 앞에서요: You said, 'I am not afraid. I walk because there is an end.' At the door of the burial chamber.
왕이 그 말을 듣고 한참 조용했잖아요. 천 년 동안 끝이 없어서 무서웠던: The king was quiet for a long while after hearing that. To a man who had been afraid for a thousand years because there was no end, you said you walk because there is one.
The Elder heard it too, from the doorframe. The man who sold a life that does not end. …I think those words hurt the Elder most of all.
인쇄지의 끊긴 줄: The broken line of the printout
The last line of the Harbinger's printout. The one that broke off at 'What removes the glove is.'
저는 그 뒤에 조사대나 칼 같은 말이 올 줄 알았어요. 아니었어요. 장갑: I thought words like 'the surveyors' or 'a blade' would follow. They did not. The Elder took off the glove. Himself. Because he promised.
기계가 못 찍은 게 아니라 찍을 수 없었던 거예요. 사람이 스스로 하는: It is not that the machine failed to print it. It could not. It seems what a person does of their own will does not enter the reckoning.
이름을 들려주셨죠. 한 번만, 천천히. 장로님이 따라 하셨어요. 입 모양: You spoke the name to him. Once only, slowly. The Elder repeated it. Only with his lips. Without a sound.
그러고는 '이제 됐네' 하셨어요. 다시 쥐지 않으셨어요. 듣고도 놓을 수: Then he said, 'That is enough.' He did not grasp it again. He has become someone who can hear it and still let go. It took a thousand years.
들려주지 않은 이름: The name that was not spoken
'놓을 수 있게 된 날 직접 읽으라'고 하셨죠. 장로님이 고개를 끄덕이셨: You told him to read it himself on the day he is able to let go. The Elder nodded. He said thank you.
연대기는 기록고에 펴 놨어요. 그 쪽으로요. 장로님 방 문은 안 잠겨 있: The Chronicle lies open in the archive. At that page. The Elder's door is not locked. I don't know when he will come up. There is no hurry.
대장님은 누가 마을을 나설 때마다 사람을 세요. 나갈 때 한 번, 돌아와: Whenever anyone leaves the village, the Captain counts heads. Once going out, once coming back. At first I thought he was just strict.
신참 신발 끈도 세 번씩 보세요. 제 것도요. 저는 그걸 연대기 여백에: He checks a newcomer's bootlaces three times. Mine too. I wrote that in the margin of the Chronicle as 'nagging'… I think I should erase it. He had his reasons.
장로님은 식당에 안 오세요. 뜨거운 걸 못 드신대요. 차도 다 식혀서 드: The Elder never comes to the restaurant. He says he cannot take hot things. He even lets his tea go cold before drinking it.
그리고 장갑요. 글씨를 가르쳐 주실 때도, 한여름에도 끼고 계셨어요. 어: And the gloves. He wore them when he taught me my letters, even in high summer. When I was little I thought all grown-ups did.
옛 뱃노래에 이런 절이 있어요. '우리에겐 배가 있었다. 마중 나간 누이: An old sea song has this verse: 'We had a ship. The sister who went out to meet them did not return.' The Chronicle has not one line about that sister.
왔냐. …이제 견습이라고는 못 부르겠군. 그래도 인원 확인은 한다. 하나: You're here. …Can't call you apprentice any more. I still count heads. One.
You're here. I didn't burn the roster. The archivist wrote it down. Now you're written there too. In the column for those who came back.
…또 그걸 들고 왔군. (로란이 잠깐 눈을 감았다 뜬다.) 됐다. 용건이: …You brought that thing again. (Roran closes his eyes for a moment, then opens them.) Fine. State your business.
그 창 좀 치워라. …아니, 됐다. 들고 있어라. 그 옆에 서니 놈들 얼: Put that spear away. …No, never mind. Keep hold of it. Standing next to it, I can see their faces clearly. Strange thing.
The leg? Twenty years old. The day before rain, I know before the clouds do.
녹슨 기사, 얼음 거인, 산꼭대기 석공, 태양의 사제. 스무 해 전 내: The rusted knight, the ice giant, the mason on the mountaintop, the priest of the sun. The places my expedition passed twenty years ago.
그때는 괴물인 줄만 알았다. 벽에 뭐가 적혀 있는지 읽어 볼 생각도 안: Back then I only thought they were monsters. It never crossed my mind to read what was written on the walls.
이번에는 읽고 간다. 싸우기 전에 상대가 어떻게 사는 놈인지 아는 건 대: This time we read before we go. Knowing how your opponent lives before the fight is a captain's job.
유령선 선장 코넬리아. 열다섯 해 전 삼백 명을 태운 채 얼음에 멈춘 배: Cornelia, captain of the ghost ship. A ship that stopped in the ice fifteen years ago with three hundred aboard.
선장을 욕하는 사람은 이 마을에 없다. 그 배를 구하러 나간 어선들도 못: No one in this village curses that captain. The fishing boats that went out to save the ship never came back either.
I know nothing about fire or names. I only know the people I know.
그런데 이건 안다. 스무 해 동안 놈들 얼굴이 흐려졌다. 토마스 코가 어: But this I know. For twenty years their faces have been fading. What Thomas's nose looked like, which eye Lia winked with. The fading was what frightened me most.
Under that spear's dusk light, it comes back. All of it. Thomas had a crooked nose. Lia, the left eye. …I don't know if this is good. Some things you have to forget to go on living.
Show it to the archivist. That girl will know what it ought to be used for.
길을 터 준 무리: The band that cleared the way
지옥 가는 길목에 잿빛 무리가 진을 치고 있었다. 싸울 줄 알았다. 놈들: The Ashen Band had made camp on the road to the Nether. I thought we'd fight. They cleared the way. Stood aside, left and right.
앞에 선 놈이 그러더라. '빚은 진 쪽이 기억한다.' 카스다. 네가 창고: The one in front said, 'The one who owes is the one who remembers.' Kass. The captain you let go at the storehouse.
기록관이 끌려가는 걸 봤다더군. 어느 쪽으로 갔는지도 일러 줬다. …적을: He said he saw the archivist being dragged off. Told us which way they went, too. …I was taught that an enemy you let go stabs you in the back. Twenty years of learning it wrong.
장로가 들어간 방 말이다. 카스가 있던 방. 벽에 그 노래가 아직 긁혀: The room the Elder went into. The room Kass was in. That song is still scratched on the wall.
장로가 밤마다 그걸 읽는다더라. 소리 내서. 둘째 절에서 멈춘다고. 문지: They say the Elder reads it every night. Aloud. He stops at the second verse. The door guard told me.
가둔 놈이 갇혔던 놈의 방에 제 발로 들어갔다. 그걸 뭐라고 불러야 할지: The jailer walked into his prisoner's room on his own feet. I don't know what to call that. Ask the archivist.
그 아이는 종이가 없으면 손등에 적는다. 걸으면서도 적는다. 제 어미도: When that girl has no paper she writes on the back of her hand. She writes while she walks. Her mother was the same. Elena wrote all the way up her forearm.
그리고 뭘 찾으면 귀퉁이에 점을 찍는다. 본인은 모르는 버릇이다. 누구한: And when she finds something she puts a dot in the corner. A habit she doesn't know she has. I know who she got it from.
That man gets up mid-sentence when the sun goes down. Says it's time to go out on the ice. Fifteen years now.
He won't eat anything hot. The restaurant owner takes it hard. I don't ask why. I have eleven bunks of my own that I never clear away.
하루 씨는 누가 한 말을 꼭 한 번 되받아 말해요. '그러니까 이러이러하: Haru always says back what someone has just said. 'So what you mean is such-and-such?' He says it's the habit of someone who takes things down.
그리고 무슨 일이든 '기록이 있습니다'로 시작해요. 없을 때는 '기록이: And he starts everything with 'There is a record.' When there isn't, he starts with 'There is no record.'
Come to sell fish? A good heavy one fetches more.
You're here. I cast the net again. The hands remembered.
오셨소. (오스카가 제 등불 심지를 한 번 더 돋운다.) …그 옆에 두니: You've come. (Oscar turns up the wick of his own lantern once more.) …Next to that one, my light looks shabby, that's all.
그 창… 바람이 이렇게 부는데 불빛이 안 흔들리는군. 내 등불은 밤마다: That spear… the wind blows like this and its light doesn't flicker. My lantern goes out three times a night.
The sea is honest. It gives as much as you waited.
If you ever hook a golden fish, bring it to me. That one is luck.
Mending nets is work too. My fingers never get a day's rest.
얕은 물에서 고기가 사라지고 있소. 사십 년 바다 생활에 이런 건 처음이: The fish are vanishing from the shallows. Forty years at sea and I've never seen the like.
얼음이 올겨울엔 하루에 한 뼘씩 내려오오. 열다섯 해 동안 가만있던 것이: This winter the ice comes down a hand's width a day. After sitting still for fifteen years.
First the cod thinned out, then the salmon, and now even the squid are gone.
Fish are the first to leave when the sea is sick. It means the sea is sick.
어부들 사이에 도는 이야기가 있소. 안개 낀 밤엔 얼음 속에서 배 한 척: There's a tale that goes round among fishermen. On foggy nights, a light comes on aboard a ship inside the ice.
열다섯 해가 지났는데 돛이 안 삭았다지. 선장이 아직도 선원들 이름을 부: Fifteen years gone and they say the sails haven't rotted. They say the captain still calls her crew by name.
Elric cast a net better than I did. Had a loud laugh. Took after his mother.
코넬리아 선장의 배에 오르던 날 그랬지. '영감, 돌아오면 큰 놈 잡아: The day he boarded Captain Cornelia's ship he said, 'Old man, when I'm back I'll catch you a big one.' He'd called me old man since he was twelve.
부두에서 손을 오래 흔들었소. 그 애는 한 번 돌아보고 말았지. 뱃사람은: I waved from the pier a long time. He looked back once and that was that. Sailors are like that.
선장은 선원 삼백 명 이름을 전부 외웠소. 이름만이 아니라 누가 추위를: The captain knew all three hundred of her crew by name. Not just names. Who felt the cold, who couldn't sing.
원망하려고 열다섯 해를 애썼소. 안 되더이다. 그 사람이 내 아들한테 목: I tried for fifteen years to resent her. Couldn't manage it. Less still after I read she gave my boy an extra scarf.
The fishermen didn't hate that beast. They feared it. The way you fear a storm.
놈이 품던 배가 수백 척 올라왔소. 주인 찾아 주는 데 한 해는 걸리겠지: Hundreds of the ships it was holding have come up. It'll take a year to find their owners. We're going one at a time, starting with the ones that still have a name on the bow.
저녁별은 못 건졌소. 놈이 안고 내려갔으니. 괜찮소. 데리러 간 배가 같: We couldn't raise the Evening Star. The beast took her down in its arms. It's all right. The ship that went to fetch them went with them.
등불을 껐소. 심지에서 연기가 올라가는데 그게 바다 쪽으로 가더이다. 바: I put the lantern out. The smoke rose from the wick and drifted toward the sea. With the wind blowing to shore.
열다섯 해 켠 등을 끄니 손이 허전해서, 부두에 등을 하나 달았소. 그건: My hands felt empty after putting out a lamp I'd kept fifteen years, so I hung one on the pier. That one is lit for anyone to see.
등불은 아직 내 곁에 있소. 밤이면 그 안에서 웃음소리가 나오. '영감': The lantern is still by my side. At night a laugh comes out of it. 'Old man,' it says.
We agreed to put it out together on the day the sea has fully thawed. You and I. Don't forget.
어부들한테는 옛말이 있소. '저물녘 불은 배를 부른다.' 해 질 녘에 부: Fishermen have an old saying. 'A dusk fire calls the boats.' The fire you light on the pier at sundown. For those coming home to see.
할아버지 말로는 그게 원래 진짜 불 얘기였다더군. 아주 옛날 부두마다 꺼: My grandfather said it was once a tale about a real fire. Long ago every pier had one fire that never went out, and if you called a name beside it, the one out at sea would hear their own name.
그 창에 든 것이 그 불이라면… 한 번만 빌려주시오. 얼음 위에서 이름을: If what's in that spear is that fire… lend it to me just once. Let me call one name out on the ice. No. No, never mind. I'll do it with my own lantern. Call him with someone else's fire and the boy won't know it's me.
브람은 쇠만 보면 손등으로 두드려 보오. 남의 집 문고리도. 속이 찼는지: Whenever Bram sees iron he raps it with the back of his hand. Other people's door handles, too. He's listening for whether it's solid.
그 양반이 내 등불 놋쇠를 해마다 갈아 주오. 값을 안 받아서 생선을 두: That man replaces the brass on my lantern every year. He won't take payment, so I leave him fish. Next day the bones are laid out neatly at my door. Means he enjoyed it.
따뜻한 바다에서 낚시를 하다 보면 소금에 절은 종이가 걸려 올라올 때가: Fishing in warm seas, you sometimes pull up paper soaked in salt. Mostly I throw it away. Once it had a seal on it. 'The One Who Awaits.'
뇌우 치는 밤엔 드라운드들이 이상한 비늘을 떨군다는 얘기가 있소. 아직도: They say that on thundery nights the drowned drop strange scales. Still tingling, so I hear.
What are you after. A blade, or armor.
어서 오게. …(브람이 창날 쪽으로 손등을 내밀었다가 거둔다.) 두드려: Welcome. …(Bram holds the back of his hand toward the spearhead, then draws it back.) I'm holding myself back from rapping on it. It isn't a thing you rap on.
…그거 이리 줘 보게. 아니, 만지진 않겠네. 보기만. 세상에. 이게 진: …Hand that here. No, I won't touch it. Only look. Good heavens. So it was real.
A good blade settles into the hand. A bad one bites it.
Enhancing is luck. But luck seems to come to those who prepared.
Thirty years before the fire. That's why I have no eyebrows.
Rare gear? I sell it only to those in the expedition. That's the rule.
Iron doesn't lie. It hardens as much as you hammer it.
A blade that broke in the enhancing? Melt it down again. Same goes for people.
That crest on the helmet, I saw it too. The crest of the Flame Knights.
우리 할아버지의 할아버지가 그 기사단 칼을 벼렸다고 했지. 옛날얘긴 줄: My grandfather's grandfather said he forged swords for those knights. I took it for an old tale.
이건 벼린 게 아니야. 식힌 거지. 날을 보게, 망치 자국이 하나도 없어: This wasn't forged. It was cooled. Look at the edge, not a single hammer mark. And this isn't iron. Not copper, not gold, not netherite. It's the metal smiths only ever heard of in rumor. One without even a name. Said to hold fire without melting and to cool without growing cold. All my life I thought that was tavern boasting.
대장장이라면 다 아는 옛말이 있네. 그 시절 왕국에 제련으로는 따를 자가: There's an old saying every smith knows. That in those days the kingdom had a smith no one could match at smelting. That he alone could work what others couldn't even melt. That on the eve of the Ashen Sun, that smith shut a handful of fire inside that nameless metal. And that he carved his own name nowhere on the spear. My family is a side branch that borrowed embers from that man's hearth.
▷ 왜 자기 이름을 안 새겼죠?: ▷ Why didn't he carve his own name?
새기면 불이 그 이름부터 삼킬까 봐서라네. 아직 아무것도 삼키지 않던 불: For fear the fire would swallow that name first. It was a fire that had swallowed nothing yet, and the first thing it swallowed must not be its maker's name. That is why no one knows that smith's name. Only that no one could match him. He too served under the King of the Hearth, and they say the king locked the doors with the smiths still in the forge.
그 사람이 가둔 불만 밖으로 나왔네. 창은 사람을 가린다더군. 불을 부리: Only the fire he shut away came out. They say the spear chooses. In a hand that means to command the fire it is only a heavy spear, and it shines only in a hand that has accepted the fire. It shines in yours. The tale of the locked forge can wait until you see the place yourself.
That hook with a place for a name plate and no name. It was the most worn hook of all. Means that of the hundred, he lifted and hung his hammer the most.
문이 잠긴 게 잿빛 해 전날 밤이라네. 그 밤에 백 번째가 문틈으로 뭘: The doors were locked on the night before the Ashen Sun. That night the hundredth passed something out through the gap in the door. A handful of fire, shut away. The one who took it was a village smith who borrowed embers from that hearth. Our founder.
