기록관 이사벨: 왕좌 앞 글을 마저 읽었어요. \"청하는 이에게 대포 둘: Archivist Isabel: I've read the rest of the writing before the throne. "The one who asks is given two cannons. The same as my own. The contest must be fair." A king who hands his opponent his own weapons.
Captain Roran: Gives to the very end. Even in a fight.
기록관 이사벨: \"겨루는 이는 불과 얼음 가운데 하나에 약해진다. 조준: Archivist Isabel: "The one who contends grows weak to either fire or ice. It shows on the crosshair. Only the cannon of the weak side can be fired." And: "The king's armor does not take a blade. Only the cannon of the one who asks can harm the king."
탐험대장 로란: 칼로는 안 된다는 거다. 대포로만. 쏘고 나면 왕이 제: Captain Roran: Blades won't do it, then. Only the cannon. Once you've fired, you can't use it again until the king fires his own. In between, you dodge. When you're weak to fire, ice hurts less; when you're weak to ice, fire hurts less. So you only need to dodge the color you're weak to. The rest you can take and still stand.
▷ 등을 보이면 어떻게 됩니까?: ▷ What happens if you show your back?
기록관 이사벨: \"겨루다 달아난 이에게는 겁쟁이의 표가 붙는다. 표가: Archivist Isabel: "One who flees the contest is marked with the coward's brand. When the brand runs out, that one dies." …Either stand to the end, or never begin at all.
탐험대장 로란: 그건 내가 스무 해 전에 배웠어야 할 법이군. 시작했으면: Captain Roran: That's a law I should have learned twenty years ago. If you've begun, stay standing. Good. Go and get what we'll lay on the braziers. Something of fire for the red, something of ice for the blue. That is our request.
식은 붉은 재 위에 마그마 크림을 얹는다. 재가 숨을 쉰다. 열다섯 해: You lay the magma cream on the cold red ash. The ash draws breath. For the first time in fifteen years, red fire catches. The ice in the room draws back one layer.
기록관 이사벨: (작게) 따라 하세요. \"청합니다. 선물을 거두어 주십: Archivist Isabel: (Quietly) Say it after me. "I ask. Take back your gift."
푸른 불 위에 얼음을 얹는다. 불이 얼음을 녹이지 않는다. 얼음이 불을: You lay the ice on the blue fire. The fire does not melt the ice. The ice covers the fire. The blue light wavers once.
기록관 이사벨: \"묶인 이들이 내리게 해 주십시오.\" …됐어요. 벽을: Archivist Isabel: "Let those who are bound come ashore." …That's it. Look at the wall.
벽에 끌 소리가 난다. 아무도 없는데 글씨가 새겨진다. 그리고 왕좌 쪽에: There is the sound of a chisel on the wall. No one is there, and yet letters are being carved. And from the direction of the throne, the sound of iron dragging. The sound of armor rising to its feet.
달라는 것을 다 주고 가라앉은 나라: The country that gave whatever was asked, and sank
말쿠트, 베푸는 왕\n거절할 줄 몰랐음. 방파제까지 내주고 가라앉음.\n:
Malkuth, the Giving King
Never learned to refuse. Gave away even the breakwater, and sank.
Took back with his own hand the last thing he gave. Asked that his apology be passed on.
말쿠트. 베풀 줄만 알던 분.\n청을 물리칠 줄 몰랐던 것은… 그분만이:
Malkuth. One who knew only how to give.
He was not the only one… who never learned to turn a request away.
얼음이 발밑에서 운다. 길고 낮은 소리다. 금이 하얗게 달려 나간다. 그: The ice cries underfoot. A long, low sound. Cracks race out in white. Black water shows beneath them. Water moving for the first time in fifteen years.
금 사이로 작은 빛들이 올라온다. 수십, 수백. 등불 빛에 잠깐 모였다가: Small lights rise through the cracks. Dozens, hundreds. They gather for a moment in the lantern's glow, then stream off to one side. Northward. Toward the great ship caught in the ice.
어부 오스카: 하산. 마레. …대답을 안 하는군. 선장이 부르는 소리가: Oscar the Fisher: Hassan. Mare. …They don't answer. The captain's call is the louder one.
멀리 유령선의 창마다 불이 켜진다. 하나씩. 삼백 개쯤. 그리고 돛이 올: Far off, a light comes on in every window of the ghost ship. One by one. Three hundred or so. And the sails go up. Though there is no wind.
돛대의 항해법전: The Ship's Code on the Mast
큰 돛대에 놋쇠판이 박혀 있다. 조항은 하나뿐이다. 글씨가 깊다. \"제: A brass plate is set into the mainmast. There is only one article. The letters are deep. "Article 1. No one dies on my ship. — Captain Cornelia"
그 아래 서명이 빽빽하다. 삼백 개. 글을 모르는 선원은 손도장을 찍었다: Beneath it the signatures are packed close. Three hundred. Sailors who could not write pressed a handprint. At the very end, in clumsy letters: "Elric." Added beside it in another hand: "Oscar's son."
놋쇠판 뒷면에도 글이 있다. 선장 혼자 보려고 새긴 것이다. \"아침별의: There is writing on the back of the brass plate too. Carved for the captain's eyes alone. "To the thirty-two of the Morning Star. Back then I had no law. Now I do."
A roll lies open on the table before the captain's cabin. Name, home, day boarded, day discharged. And, in the captain's hand, one line about each and every person.
\"하산. 그물을 잘 기움. 딸이 둘.\" \"마레. 노래를 못함. 그래: "Hassan. Good at mending nets. Two daughters." "Mare. Can't sing. Let her sing anyway." "Elric. Feels the cold. Gave him one more scarf. His father waved from the dock a long time."
All three hundred lines are like that. The captain did not write her crew down as numbers.
명부 마지막 장에 열다섯 해 동안 매일 덧쓴 줄이 있다. 잉크가 층층이: On the last page of the roll is a line written over every day for fifteen years. The ink is layered so thick the paper bulges. "All hands aboard again today. No deaths." Today's is still wet.
어부 오스카: …목도리를 하나 더 줬다고. 선장이. 그럼 내가 들고 뛴: Oscar the Fisher: …Gave him one more scarf. The captain did. Then my running with the spare was a wasted trip. That boy wasn't cold. (He laughs. Briefly.) That's a mercy. That much is a mercy.
돛대에 놋쇠판이 박혀 있다. \"제1조. 내 배에서는 아무도 죽지 않는다: A brass plate is set into the mast. "Article 1. No one dies on my ship. — Captain Cornelia" Three hundred signatures beneath it.
…돛이 올라가 있소. 바람도 없는데. 저 배는 갈 준비가 된 거요. 어디: …The sails are up. With no wind. That ship is ready to go. Anywhere at all.
There's a brass plate on the mainmast. That law. Signatures, too.
선장실 앞 탁자에 명부가 펴져 있소. …내가 찾을 줄이 있소. 같이 봐: The roll is lying open on the table before the captain's cabin. …There's a line I need to find. Look with me.
I've read Elric's line. Go on ahead. I'll stay just a little longer.
선장의 식탁 · 손님 자리: The Captain's Table · The Guest's Seat
Three hundred plates are set on the long table. All empty. All wiped clean. Only the seat beside the head has no plate. Instead, a brass plaque: "Seat of the one who comes from land."
빵을 놓고 앉는다. 식탁 저편 상석의 의자가 소리 없이 당겨진다. 누가: You set down the bread and sit. The chair at the head, across the table, is drawn back without a sound. Someone sits. A breath like ice rises. The voice is low and clear.
코넬리아 선장: 뭍의 빵이군. 열다섯 해 만이다. 손님은 말하라. 들으마: Captain Cornelia: Bread from land. The first in fifteen years. Let the guest speak. I will listen.
▷ 아침별이 올라왔습니다. 서른둘이 뭍에 내렸습니다. 서기가 '귀항 32: ▷ The Morning Star has come up. The thirty-two have come ashore. The clerk wrote, 'Returned to port: 32.'
코넬리아 선장: (오래 말이 없다. 접시 삼백 개가 한꺼번에 가늘게 떤다: Captain Cornelia: (She says nothing for a long time. Three hundred plates tremble faintly, all at once.) …Tobin too. Did little Tobin come ashore too. He was fourteen. He got seasick.
▷ He did. His name was called last.
Captain Cornelia: Yes. That boy was always last. …I would be glad if it were a lie. Gladder still if it is true. The sunken king has taken back what he gave me. You asked it of him, I hear. I bear no grudge. I would have asked the same.
코넬리아 선장: 그러나 내 배의 제1조는 왕이 준 것이 아니다. 내가 세: Captain Cornelia: But Article 1 of my ship was not given by the king. I laid it down. Though the king takes back his gift, the law remains. And as long as the law remains, I cannot put the three hundred ashore. Let the guest rise from the table. Next we meet on deck.
아무도 죽지 않게 하려던 사람: The One Who Tried to Let No One Die
칼을 놓는 코넬리아 선장: Captain Cornelia, Laying Down Her Sword
Three hundred. All hands aboard. No deaths.
…All hands, ashore. Captain's orders.
코넬리아. 하나도 잃지 않으려던 선장.\n지키는 손과 가두는 손이 같은:
Cornelia. The captain who would not lose a single one.
The hand that protects and the hand that imprisons turned out to be the same hand. …Mine as well.
기록관 이사벨: \"회색 망토의 학자가 왔다. '여덟 번째 눈이 있는 곳: Archivist Isabel: "The scholar in the grey cloak came. He held out a sea route, saying it led to 'where the eighth eye is.' That the power to bring back what is forgotten was there. He was someone who knew of the Morning Star. He recited the names of the thirty-two. Names I had never once spoken to another soul."
기록관 이사벨: \"값은 배 한 척 값. 그리고 부탁 하나. '거기 닿으: Archivist Isabel: "The price was the price of a ship. And one favor. 'When you reach it, write down what you hear and bring it to me.' When I asked what I would hear, he only smiled. He was wearing gloves. In high summer."
기록관 이사벨: \"항로 끝에서 폭풍을 만났다. 폭풍이 배를 감쌌다. 부: Archivist Isabel: "At the end of the route we met the storm. The storm wrapped itself around the ship. It did not break it. It looked in. At one person after another. Then someone dropped the anchor. A bell sounded. The crew began to fall. Not from the freezing. From the sound of the bell."
기록관 이사벨: \"바다 밑에서 누가 물었다. 무엇을 청하느냐고. 나는: Archivist Isabel: "From under the sea someone asked. What I would ask for. I asked. When it was the Morning Star, there had been no one to ask." …It ends here.
▷ It wasn't the captain who froze the sea.
기록관 이사벨: 카엘 씨가 마지막에 그랬죠. 네. 이제 다 알겠어요. 얼: Archivist Isabel: That's what Kael said at the end. Yes. Now I understand it all. The one who froze it was the king, the one who asked was the captain, and the one who sent her to that place was the person in gloves. Of the three, only one meant harm.
코넬리아, 선장\n아무도 죽지 않게 하려던 사람. 삼백과 서른둘의 이름을:
Cornelia, captain
The one who tried to let no one die. Never once got wrong the names of the three hundred and the thirty-two.
Last order: all hands ashore.
은신처의 벽 앞: Before the Wall of the Hideout
'내린 서른 중 남은 일곱'이 글을 새긴 벽 앞에서 등불을 든다. 얼음: You raise the lantern before the wall where 'the seven left of the thirty who got off' carved their words. Seven lights walk out of the ice. In a line. The way sailors come off a ship.
빛들이 등불 유리에 닿아 안으로 들어간다. 하나씩. 등불이 조금 무거워진: The lights touch the lantern glass and pass inside. One by one. The lantern grows a little heavier.
유령선의 현문: The Gangway of the Ghost Ship
배에서 뭍으로 내리는 자리, 현문에 등불을 든다. 갑판 위의 빛들이 멈춘: You raise the lantern at the gangway, the place where one steps from ship to land. The lights on deck stop. Close to three hundred lights look this way all at once.
맨 앞의 빛 하나가 먼저 내려온다. 걸음이 빠르다. 다른 빛들을 돌아보고: One light at the very front comes down first. Its step is quick. It turns back to the other lights and sways as if beckoning. And a line forms.
After the last light has come in, there is a sound inside the lantern. Laughter. Young. Loud.
어부 오스카: 선장을 재워 달라고 한 게 나요. 쉬게 해 주라고. 그 입: Oscar the Fisher: I'm the one who asked you to put the captain to sleep. To let her rest. And with the same mouth I'm saying I can't put out the lantern.
어부 오스카: 끄면 내일부터 밤에 할 일이 없소. 열다섯 해 동안 그게: Oscar the Fisher: Put it out, and from tomorrow I've nothing to do at night. For fifteen years that has been the end of my day.
어부 오스카: 그 왕은 준 걸 제 손으로 거뒀다지. 미안하다면서. 선장은: Oscar the Fisher: That king took back with his own hand what he gave, they say. Saying he was sorry. And the captain let go only when she lost the contest. I can't be either. I'm no king and no captain. I'm a fisherman.
등불을 끄자고 한다. 엘릭이 '영감' 하고 웃었으니, 그걸로 인사는 된: You say to put the lantern out. Elric laughed and called 'old man,' so the goodbyes have been said.
You say to keep it lit for now. To put it out together, the day the sea has thawed all the way.
바닥 널 밑 기름천 안에 수정 구슬이 있다. 한가운데 금이 가 있다. 기: Under the floorboards, inside an oilcloth, is a crystal orb. Cracked through the middle. The same size as the orb in the archive, cracked in the same place. They were made as a pair.
Hold an ember close and the inside clouds over. What appears is not a hand but a deck. A star on the prow. Thirty-two people standing. Sharp, down to their faces.
The captain looked at this. Every day for fifteen years. A mirror that 'shows' what is forgotten. It cannot bring it back. It only shows. Did the one who gave it tell her the difference?
구슬 밑에 접힌 양피지. 받침대의 도면이다. 치수, 재료, 다섯 군데에: Beneath the orb, a folded parchment. Plans for a stand. Measurements, materials, the places for stones to be set at five points. The lines are astonishingly straight. A scribe's hand.
글씨는 전부 뒤집혀 있다. 보랏빛. 거울에 비춰야 읽힌다. 불탄 기록고: Every letter is reversed. Violet. It reads only in a mirror. The same ink as the wall of the burned archive, and the bottom of the witch's jar.
도면 여백에 한 줄: \"이것은 되돌리지 못한다. 비출 뿐이다. 그 사람: One line in the margin of the plans: "This cannot bring anything back. It only shows. If that person told you otherwise, do not believe it. That person can only go on living by believing it can be brought back."
그 아래 더 작게: \"그래도 보고 싶을 것이오. 나도 그랬소. 그래서: Below it, smaller: "Even so, you will want to see. So did I. That is why I made it."
장갑 낀 손의 쪽지: The Note in the Gloved Hand's Writing
도면과 따로, 선장의 지갑에 접혀 있던 쪽지. 이쪽은 반듯한 보통 글씨다: Apart from the plans, a note that was folded in the captain's wallet. This one is in a neat, ordinary hand. Black ink. "At the end of the route the storm will look into your ship. It will do no harm."
\"그때 폭풍 속에서 누가 이름을 부를 것이오. 사람 이름이오. 한 번만: "Then, within the storm, someone will call a name. A person's name. It may be called only once. Write it down and bring it to me. Do not get a single letter wrong."
\"그 이름 하나의 값으로 항로 값을 전부 돌려드리겠소.\" 서명은 글자: "For the price of that one name, I will return to you the whole price of the route." The signature is not letters but a drawing. A hand. In a glove.
쪽지 뒷면에 선장의 글씨: \"이름은 못 들었다. 폭풍은 아무 이름도 부: On the back of the note, in the captain's hand: "I heard no name. The storm called no name at all. It seemed to start to call, and stop. Like someone who does not know the name they mean to call."
기록관 이사벨: 미아가 읽은 대로 옮길게요. \"받침에는 돌 다섯을 박는: Archivist Isabel: I'll put it down just as Mia read it. "Five stones are set into the stand. They are not stones but letters. Lay a meaning over them so they do not look like letters. A thing used every day hides them best."
기록관 이사벨: \"구슬은 둘을 만들었다. 하나는 탑의 서기들에게, 하나: Archivist Isabel: "I made two orbs. One for the clerks of the tower, one I carry myself." …The clerks of the tower. The people in the boxes, in the Void. The one my mother received came from them.
▷ Then the one the captain received was the one its maker carried.
기록관 이사벨: 네. 자기 것을 내준 거예요. 회색 망토가 항로를 팔러: Archivist Isabel: Yes. They gave up their own. To the very person the grey cloak went to sell the route to. To stop her, do you think? By writing 'it cannot bring anything back, it only shows.'
Archivist Isabel: The wall of the burned archive, the bottom of the witch's jar, and these plans. All in reversed writing, all the same hand. I hear Lucky once got a receipt written that way, too. This person has been doing something from behind the scenes for a very long time. From the opposite side to the person in gloves.
Oscar the Fisher: I raised the twentieth boat. Carved a name on her. Fifteen years late. Go to the dock and see what I carved. I'd be embarrassed to say it aloud.
어부 오스카: 유령선은 그대로 뒀소. 얼음이 다 녹으면 제 발로 가라앉겠: Oscar the Fisher: I left the ghost ship as she was. When the ice has all melted she'll go down on her own. She's the captain's ship, so she ought to go where the captain goes. The anchor I fished up. To stand it on the dock.
어부 오스카: 웃고 있소. 등불 안에서든, 간 데서든. 그 애는 웃음이: Oscar the Fisher: He's laughing. Whether inside the lantern or wherever he's gone. That boy laughed easily. Took after his mother.
부두 끝의 말뚝: The Post at the End of the Dock
부두 끝 말뚝에 등을 건다. 얼음 위의 등보다 높이 단다. 멀리서도 보이: You hang the lamp on the post at the end of the dock. Higher than the lantern on the ice. So it can be seen from far off.
말뚝 옆에 닻이 세워져 있다. 「코넬리아의 배. 제1조를 지킨다.」 그: An anchor stands beside the post. "Cornelia's ship. Article 1 is kept." Below it someone has added a line in chalk. Oscar's handwriting. "Kept."
A small boat is tied up next to it. A freshly carved name on the prow. "Scarf."
등에 불을 붙인다. 바다 쪽에서 바람이 분다. 열다섯 해 만에 짠 바람이: You light the lamp. Wind blows in from the sea. A salt wind, for the first time in fifteen years. The flame wavers, and does not go out.
한 사람 보라고 켜던 불을 아무나 보라고 켜니 덜 무겁소. …고맙소, 조: A light I used to keep for one person to see weighs less now that it's lit for anyone to see. …Thank you, Surveyor.
장로 에르윈: 일곱 봉인은 천 년 전 일곱 왕이 불을 나눠 가둔 자리일세: Elder Erwin: The seven seals are where the seven kings divided the fire and locked it away a thousand years ago. Each king received one eye and buried it in his own kingdom.
장로 에르윈: 그리고 왕마다 그 눈을 지킬 것을 하나씩 세웠네. 제 손으: Elder Erwin: And each king set up something to guard that eye. Only one king… guarded it with his own hands. The rest entrusted it. If 'entrusted' is a good enough word.
장로 에르윈: 떠넘긴 걸세. 가 보면 아네. 자리마다 떠넘겨진 것이 아직: Elder Erwin: Then it was passing it off. You will know when you go. At each place, what was passed off will still be there. I would have you see it for yourselves.
장로 에르윈: 이번엔 나도 가겠네. 문 앞까지는. 천 년… 아니, 평생: Elder Erwin: This time I will go too. As far as the gate. These are places I have seen only in books for a thousand… no, for a lifetime.
기록고의 벽지도: The Wall Map in the Archive
선장의 지도는 고래 가죽이다. 벽지도 위에 대자 해안선이 맞는다. 선장은: The captain's chart is whale hide. Laid over the wall map, its coastlines match. The captain drew the coastline of a thousand years ago. Not the coastline of today.
첫째 표시, 지옥. 선장의 글씨: \"불. 들어간 자 백. 나온 자 없음: The first mark, the Nether. In the captain's hand: "Fire. Went in: a hundred. Came out: none. The door is locked from outside."
둘째, 사막. \"모래. 들어간 자 하나. 스스로 들어감. 짐승 둘이 기: The second, the desert. "Sand. Went in: one. Of his own will. Two beasts wait." The third, underground. "Iron. Went in: none. A clock stands still. Do not touch the clock."
넷째, 바다 밑. \"물. 들어간 자 대대로. 노래함. 교대 없음.\": The fourth, beneath the sea. "Water. Went in: generation after generation. They sing. No relief of the watch." The fifth, the Void. "The empty seat. Those who went in cannot be written. Write them and they are erased."
여섯째, 설원. \"얼음. 들어간 자 하나와 그를 따른 자들. 간수 없음: The sixth, the snowfield. "Ice. Went in: one, and those who followed him. No jailer." And at the very bottom of the chart, in the seventh place, a line in place of a mark. "My ship cannot go there. Where the fire was first lit."
기록관 이사벨: 선장은 열다섯 해 동안 얼음 속에서 이걸 그렸어요. 누가: Archivist Isabel: The captain drew this in the ice over fifteen years. She was writing down what someone told her. The grey cloak. …Why tell her? What did he mean her to do?
대장장이 브람: 장부 첫 쪽일세. 보게. 문이지. 손바닥 두 개 두께로: Bram the Smith: The first page of the ledger. Look. A door. Drawn two palms thick. Whoever drew it knew that thickness. Because they'd made one.
대장장이 브람: 문틈으로 손이 하나 나와 있지. 손에 든 게 뭔지 보이나: Bram the Smith: There's a hand coming out through the crack of the door. Can you see what it holds? A small lamp. A handful of fire shut inside. The ember in my family's forge came from that. In eighteen generations we never once let it go out. …No, once. The night the sea froze.
▷ 건네는 손은 누구 겁니까?: ▷ Whose is the hand that's passing it out?
대장장이 브람: 몰라. 그림 밑에 이름 쓸 자리가 있는데 비워 놨어. 일: Bram the Smith: Don't know. There's a place for a name under the drawing, and it was left empty. On purpose. They even ruled a line for it and wrote nothing. This wasn't drawn by someone who couldn't write a name. They were asked not to write it.
대장장이 브람: 그리고 문 안쪽에 그린 것. 사람이 아니야. 사람보다 훨: Bram the Smith: And what's drawn on the inside of the door. Not a person. Far bigger than a person. Its head rises above the door. But look. This one is holding out a hand too. Toward the door.
▷ Let's go and see for ourselves.
문은 쇠다. 손바닥 두 개 두께. 빗장이 걸려 있다. 문 안쪽이 아니라: The door is iron. Two palms thick. It is barred. Not on the inside but on the outside.
빗장 위에 왕의 인장이 찍힌 납이 녹아 굳어 있다. 한 번 잠그고, 다시: Lead stamped with the king's seal has melted and set over the bar. Meaning it was locked once, never to be opened again.
문 안쪽 면은 온통 패여 있다. 망치 자국이다. 수천, 수만 번. 사람: The inner face of the door is pitted all over. Hammer marks. Thousands, tens of thousands. There are marks at the height of a person, and far above those, marks the size of a person's torso.
Bram the Smith: …It was beaten from inside. By people. And by something that isn't one. Those marks up high aren't from a hammer. They're from a fist.
대장장이 브람: 문 옆에 망치걸이가 백 개 있네. 걸이마다 이름표가 붙었: Bram the Smith: There are a hundred hammer pegs beside the door. A name plate on every peg. Ninety-nine I can read. One has only the place for a name plate, with nothing carved on it. From the start. And yet that peg is the most worn of all.
화로의 왕 브라간이 맡긴 것: What Bragan, King of the Furnace, left in another's keeping
덥군. 좋은 화로가 있다는 뜻이지. 저 문일세. 우리 집 장부 첫 쪽의: Hot. That means there's a good forge. That door there. The door from the first page of my family's ledger.
Look at the bar first. Which side it's on. A forge door is meant to be barred from inside.
The anvils are all different heights. Each fitted to its smith. This was a good forge, this place.
밖에서 잠갔군. …안에 있던 사람들 망치가 아직 바닥에 있네. 그것부터: Locked from outside. …The hammers of the people who were inside are still on the floor. Let's see to those first.
You pick up a hammer fallen beside an anvil and hang it on its peg. The haft is worn to the shape of a hand. The hand that held it is still there.
대장장이 브람: \"오딘. 풀무꾼.\" \"하렌. 담금질.\" \"하렌의: Bram the Smith: "Odin. Bellows." "Haren. Quenching." "Haren's daughter Miren. Fourteen. Apprentice." …They brought a fourteen-year-old in with them. The apprentice's peg is right under her father's. Within arm's reach.
On the wall under Miren's peg are marks measuring her height. Six of them. One each year. She grew for six more years after the door was locked.
가운뎃줄 걸이는 유난히 닳았다. 이름표마다 옆에 작은 금이 새겨졌다. 망: The pegs of the middle row are worn more than any. Small ticks are cut beside each name plate. A count of the years of hammering. The longest row is sixty-two.
Bram the Smith: Sixty-two years. Meaning they went on hammering sixty-two years after the door was locked. Until they were old and their hands shook. And then… turned into that, and went on hammering.
One peg is made to hold two hammers. The name plate: "Tor and Bel. Twins. Asked for one peg, so given one."
윗줄 맨 끝. 백 번째 걸이. 이름표 자리가 매끈하다. 처음부터 아무것도: The very end of the top row. The hundredth peg. The place for its name plate is smooth. Nothing was ever carved there. And yet the iron of the peg is half worn away. Hung and taken down more than any other.
걸 망치가 없다. 바닥에도, 모루 곁에도. 그 대신 걸이 밑 벽에 그을음: There is no hammer to hang. Not on the floor, not by the anvils. Instead, on the wall beneath the peg, a drawing made in soot. A door. A gap in the door. Two hands.
대장장이 브람: …우리 장부 그림일세. 똑같아. 이 사람이 먼저 그린 거: Bram the Smith: …That's the drawing from our ledger. The very same. This person drew it first. Here. And our founder saw it and copied it. No, how would someone outside the door see this wall?
대장장이 브람: 문틈으로 건넨 게 불만이 아니었던 걸세. 그림도 건넨 거: Bram the Smith: It wasn't only fire that was passed through the gap. The drawing was passed too. To say 'this is what happened.' So it wouldn't be forgotten.
Bram the Smith: Before the fires of the Nether, coal is the answer. Mind the hammer hafts.
I'll pick up the hammers, you hang them. I'll read the name plates.
Start from the bottom row. The apprentices' pegs. Set low.
The middle row. Most worn of all. People who worked a long time.
Look at the end of the top row. The peg with no name plate. The hundredth.
These pegs were forged by hand. Not poured in a mold. A hundred of them, one by one.
아흔아홉 자루. 다 퇴근했네. 한 자루가 모자라. 화로부터 살리고 찾아보: Ninety-nine hammers. All gone home for the day. One is missing. Let's bring the forge back to life and then look for it.
화로 아가리가 사람 키의 세 배다. 안쪽 깊은 데서 불이 숨을 쉰다. 얕: The mouth of the forge is three times the height of a person. Deep inside, the fire breathes. Shallowly. Handprints are baked onto the forge wall. Not the marks of hands warming at the fire, but of hands pushed into it.
막대를 하나씩 넣는다. 불이 받아먹는다. 넷째를 넣자 화로가 운다. 풀무: You feed in the rods one by one. The fire takes them. At the fourth, the forge cries out. A draft comes with no bellows. Firelight stands on all hundred anvils at once.
대장장이 브람: 살았네! 봤나, 색이 달라졌지. 붉은 게 아니라 흰 불이: Bram the Smith: It lives! Did you see, the color's changed. Not red but white fire. The same color as the fire in my family's forge. …Because it is the same fire.
The knocking from inside the door slows. The rhythm of a fear that has passed.
모루 밑의 주문서: The Order Sheet Under the Anvil
쇠판에 글이 깊게 패여 있다. 왕의 주문서다. \"화로의 왕 브라간이 명: Words are cut deep into an iron plate. The king's order. "Bragan, King of the Furnace, commands. Forge a thing to guard the first eye."
\"하나. 이름을 주지 말 것. 이름 있는 것은 불이 먹는다. 둘. 쉬지: "One. Give it no name. The fire eats what has a name. Two. Let it not rest. Three. Let it break any hand that would take the eye, whoever's it may be."
"Four. Those who forge it may not leave the forge until the work is done. Five. The work is never done." Between the fourth and fifth lines someone has cut a question mark with a chisel. Many people, many times.
At the very bottom, a line added in another hand: "Six. Let it not strike the door. It takes our side." The king's writing. Hurried. He came and added it after the order had been filled.
쇠판 뒷면. 대장장이들의 글이다. 망치 끝으로 찍었다. \"놈은 우리 말: The back of the iron plate. The smiths' words. Punched in with the tips of their hammers. "It listens to us. It strikes the door. It is our son. We could not give it a name. We are sorry." Ninety-nine signatures. And one hammer mark struck in place of a signature.
대장간 안쪽 문: The Inner Door of the Forge
망치 자루 끝으로 쇠문을 친다. 셋. 쉬고. 둘. 소리가 대장간 안쪽으로: You strike the iron door with the end of a hammer haft. Three. A rest. Two. The sound rolls away into the forge beyond.
For a long while there is no sound at all. The forge gives a crack as a coal bursts.
Then it comes. From the far side of the door. The sound of flesh, not iron, striking. Slow. Two. A rest. Three. Soot falls from the ceiling.
다시 친다. 셋, 쉬고, 둘. 대답이 바로 온다. 이번에는 빠르다. 둘,: You strike again. Three, rest, two. The answer comes at once. Quick this time. Two, rest, three. Two, rest, three. Two, rest, three. It does not stop. The door cries out.
대장장이 브람: …그만. 그만 치게. 놈이 신이 났어. 천 년 만에 대답: Bram the Smith: …Enough. Stop knocking. It's overjoyed. It has heard an answer for the first time in a thousand years. How am I supposed to put that to sleep?
Elder Erwin: I heard. It carried even outside the door. Bram, I know how you feel. Even so, the seal is rotting. If the eye bursts, it will burn in the fire of its own body. Awake. To put it to sleep is the kinder thing for it.
Bram the Smith: How do you know it so well, Elder? What happens when one bursts?
장로 에르윈: …책에서 읽었네. 터진 것을 본 사람이 쓴 책일세. 그 사: Elder Erwin: …I read it in a book. A book written by someone who saw one burst. He wrote that he could never forget that sound for the rest of his life.
▷ Inside the door, I'll end it quickly.
대장간 길목의 기사들: Knights on the Road to the Forge
It's an edge heated in the forge. It will bite once. From the second blow on, it's down to your skill.
이름을 받지 못한 아들\n대장장이 백 명이 벼림. 천 년 동안 문을 두드:
The son who was given no name
Forged by a hundred smiths. Knocked on the door for a thousand years. The door opened.
Ninety-nine names, and one person whose name was never carved.
두드리는 소리가 그쳤구나. 천 년을 들었다.\n문 앞을 지킨다는 것을,:
So the knocking has stopped. I listened to it for a thousand years.
What it means to keep watch before a door, that child knew better than I.
브람이 달군 쇠를 모루에 올린다. 첫 망치질을 넘겨받는다. 내려친다. 불: Bram sets the heated iron on the anvil. He hands you the first hammer blow. You bring it down. Sparks fly. Bram nods and strikes the rest. In the rhythm of three, rest, two.
식힌 망치를 벽의 걸이에 건다. 닳아서 반쯤 없어진 걸이가 새 망치 무게: You hang the cooled hammer on the peg on the wall. The peg, worn half away, creaks a little under the weight of the new hammer. It holds.
대장장이 브람: 됐네. 이제 이 집에서 일 끝나면 이 걸이부터 채우고 나: Bram the Smith: There. From now on, in this house, when the work's done we fill this peg first before we leave. So the hundredth is the first to go home.
화로 불이 걸이에 비친다. 열여덟 대 동안 꺼뜨리지 않은 불. 문틈으로: The forge fire shines on the peg. A fire not let go out in eighteen generations. A handful passed through the gap of a door.
회랑 벽에 초상이 스물아홉 점 걸려 있다. 가장 오래된 것은 물감이 갈라: Twenty-nine portraits hang on the wall of the cloister. In the oldest the paint has cracked so the face can hardly be seen. The newest is Elder Erwin.
All twenty-nine wear gloves. Black gloves, white gloves, leather, silk. Fashions change, and the gloves never come off.
모두 같은 자세로 앉았다. 왼손을 오른손 위에 얹고. 오른손등을 가리듯이: All sit in the same pose. The left hand laid over the right. As if to cover the back of the right hand.
초상 밑 놋쇠판의 재임 기간을 이으면 빈 날이 하루도 없다. 앞 장로가: Join up the terms of office on the brass plates beneath the portraits and not a single day is left empty. The day after one Elder stepped down, the next arrived 'from a distant chapter.' All twenty-nine times.
기록관 이사벨: …장로님이 글씨 가르쳐 주실 때요. 제 손을 잡고 획을: Archivist Isabel: …When the Elder taught me my letters. He held my hand and drew the strokes with me. He was wearing gloves then, too. I only ever thought that it felt warm.
안내인 모리스: 수도회 지부요? 음. 저 이 일 열 해 했거든요. 동쪽: Morris the Guide: Chapters of the Order? Hm. I've done this work ten years, you know. The eastern pass, the southern desert road, the northern ice road, I've been down them all. The only house flying the Order's banner is the one here.
안내인 모리스: 옛날엔 있었을 수도 있죠. 그런데요, 길은 사람이 다녀야: Morris the Guide: There might have been some long ago. But, you see, a road only lasts if people walk it. If there were a chapter, there'd be a road coming from it, and the only road into the Order is the one going up from town. There's no back door, either. I looked everywhere when I was little. Playing hide-and-seek.
▷ 장로님이 어디서 오셨는지 들은 적 있어요?: ▷ Have you ever heard where the Elder came from?
안내인 모리스: 아뇨. 그러고 보니 장로님은 길을 안 물으세요. 손님들은: Morris the Guide: No. Come to think of it, the Elder never asks the way. Every visitor asks. The Elder just walks, even somewhere he's going for the first time. The other day he took the turn for the shortcut to the desert before I did, and I was a bit embarrassed.
시청 서기 하루: 전입 기록 말씀입니까. 있습니다. 마흔한 해 전, '수: Haru the Town Clerk: The record of arrivals, you mean. There is one. Forty-one years ago, 'Elder Erwin of the Order, posted from a distant chapter.' My predecessor's predecessor wrote it. The space for place of departure is empty. A breach of regulations, though it seems to have been let pass as Order business.
Haru the Town Clerk: There is one more thing. I am the one who records attendance. In forty-one years the Elder has not missed a single day. No sick leave either. Does a person go forty-one years without catching one cold? I caught two last month alone.
▷ 이상하다고 생각한 적은 없습니까?: ▷ Did you never think it strange?
시청 서기 하루: 서기는 생각을 적지 않습니다. 본 것을 적습니다. 본: Haru the Town Clerk: A clerk does not write down what he thinks. He writes down what he sees. To tell you only what I have seen: when the Elder is deep in thought, he adjusts his gloves. I mark it in the margin of the minutes. Lately those marks have increased. Sharply.
문 앞의 마른 수반: The Dry Basin Before the Door
피라미드 문 앞에 돌 수반이 있다. 바닥에 물때가 층층이 앉았다. 맨 아: A stone basin stands before the pyramid door. Scale lies in layers on its bottom. The lowest layer is the thickest. The water of the days when the king was alive.
수로의 끝이 수반 한 뼘 앞에서 끊겨 있다. 끊긴 자리에 발톱 자국이 없: The end of the waterway breaks off a hand's width short of the basin. There is no claw scratch at the break. The last section Sirok could not reach.
시로크가 쓰러진 자리에서 솟은 물이 수로를 타고 여기까지 와서, 끊긴 자: The water that rose where Sirok fell has run along the waterway all the way here, and at the break it seeps into the sand. It cannot cross the hand's width.
기록관 이사벨: 수반 테두리에 새긴 글이에요. \"이 수반이 차는 날 문: Archivist Isabel: These are the words carved on the rim of the basin. "The day this basin fills, the gatekeeper opens the door." A gatekeeper. Someone is inside the door. Waiting a thousand years for the sound of water.
사막의 왕 아므라트가 한 약속: The promise made by Amrat, King of the Desert
물소리 들려요? 여기까지 따라왔어요. 시로크가 쓰러진 자리에서 솟은 물이: Can you hear the water? It followed us all the way here. The water that rose where Sirok fell.
There's a basin before the door. It's dry. With writing on the rim.
The desert is good because paper doesn't rot. But ink dries far too fast.
물이 한 뼘 앞에서 멈췄어요. 수로를 거슬러 가 봐요. 오다가 돌을 봤어: The water stopped a hand's width short. Let's go back up the waterway. I saw stones on the way.
모래에 묻힌 표석 · 첫째: Marker Stone Buried in Sand · The First
모래를 걷어 내자 무릎 높이의 돌이 드러난다. 물동이 끈에 쓸린 자국이: You clear away the sand and a knee-high stone comes to light. It is scored where the cords of water jars rubbed it. And worn where someone laid a hand on it every time they passed.
기록관 이사벨: 읽을게요. \"삼백 해째. 시로크가 오늘 스무 걸음을 팠: Archivist Isabel: I'll read it. "Three hundredth year. Sirok dug twenty paces today. I told it that the king is waiting. Sirok wagged its tail."
기록관 이사벨: 그 밑에 다른 손으로요. \"정원지기 하림이 죽었다. 그: Archivist Isabel: And beneath it, in another hand. "Harim the gardener has died. His daughter has taken up the water jar. Sirok was told that Harim has gone far away." …Here, too, they couldn't say it.
모래에 묻힌 표석 · 둘째: Marker Stone Buried in Sand · The Second
두 번째 돌은 기울어 있다. 밑이 파였다. 모래벌레가 여기서 오래 누워: The second stone leans. The ground beneath it is hollowed. The sandworm lay here a long time. Resting its body against the stone.
기록관 이사벨: \"칠백 해째. 시로크가 판 굴이 무너져 사흘을 못 나왔: Archivist Isabel: "Seven hundredth year. The tunnel Sirok dug caved in, and it could not get out for three days. We dug with our hands. Once out, it began digging again at once. We told it to rest. It did not rest."
Archivist Isabel: "The youngest gardener asked whether the king is truly waiting. No one answered. We shouldered our water jars."
끊긴 수로의 끝: The End of the Broken Waterway
마지막 돌에는 글이 없다. 세우기만 하고 적지 못했다. 그 앞에서 수로가: The last stone has no writing. It was set up, and never written on. The waterway breaks off before it. A hand's width. One palm.
무릎을 꿇고 모래를 판다. 손톱 밑에 모래가 든다. 모래 밑은 젖어 있다: You kneel and dig at the sand. Sand packs under your fingernails. Beneath, the sand is wet. The water had already come this far. It simply could not get across.
둑이 터진다. 물이 한 뼘을 넘어 돌 수로로 떨어진다. 천 년 묵은 수로: The bank gives way. Water crosses the hand's width and falls into the stone channel. The dust on the bed of the thousand-year-old waterway floats up on the water. The water goes toward the door.
기록관 이사벨: (빈 표석에 펜으로 적는다.) \"천 해째. 조사대가 한: Archivist Isabel: (She writes on the blank marker stone with her pen.) "Thousandth year. The Survey Corps dug a hand's width. Sirok, it has arrived." …It's ink, so it will wear off soon. Even so.
Those stones. Only their heads show above the sand. There are three. Let's look at them in order.
The first stone. Clear it, please. There's writing.
The second one leans. It looks like something lay propped against it.
It breaks off here. By one palm. The last stone has no writing.
A different hand wrote on each stone. Written down through the generations. Like our Chronicle.
It arrived. The water crossed over. Let's go to the basin. It needs more water.
첫 동이를 붓는다. 돌이 물을 마신다. 천 년 마른 돌이라 한 동이가 그: You pour the first jar. The stone drinks the water. Stone dry for a thousand years, it soaks up the whole jar. Water fills the letters on the rim and the words grow sharp.

방마다 돌판이 하나씩 벽에 기대어 있다. 아이 글씨로 여덟 마디가 적혔다: A stone slate leans against the wall in every cell. Eight bars written in a child's hand. Where a note is wrong, there are corrections in an adult's hand. Generation after generation got the same place wrong. The sixth bar.
돌판 귀퉁이의 글: \"일곱 살. 오늘부터 밤 당번. 졸면 엄마가 꼬집는: Words in the corner of a slate: "Seven years old. Night watch from today. If I doze, Mother pinches me." Beneath it, in writing from long after: "Forty years old. From today my daughter takes the night watch. I cannot bring myself to pinch her."
어부 오스카: 일곱 살부터요. …우리 엘릭이 배를 처음 탄 게 일곱 살이: Oscar the Fisher: From seven years old. …Our Elric was seven the first time he rode in a boat.
사제의 방 · 벽의 눈금: Priests' Cells · The Tally on the Wall
긴 벽 하나가 눈금으로 덮였다. 하루에 한 금. 방 끝에서 끝까지, 바닥: One long wall is covered in tally marks. One mark a day. From one end of the room to the other, from floor to ceiling. The wall ran out and they went on to the ceiling. The ceiling ran out and they went on to the wall of the next cell.
눈금 사이에 드문드문 글이 끼어 있다. \"교대는 언제 오는가.\" 삼백: Here and there words are wedged between the marks. "When does the relief come?" Some three hundred years later: "The relief does not come. Do not ask." Some six hundred years later: "The children ask what a relief is. I could not explain."
어부 오스카: 여왕은 교대를 보낸다고 했던 거요. 처음엔. 안 보낸 거지: Oscar the Fisher: So the queen said she'd send a relief. At the start. And didn't. Whether she forgot, or had no one to send.
Six bunks are empty. The bedding is folded. These were not people who left in a hurry. They folded it and went. On each pillow lies a single grey coin. They did not take them.
금화를 집는다. 차다. 앞면은 닳아 없고, 뒷면에 문장이 있다. 문장이: You pick up a coin. It is cold. The face is worn away; on the back is a crest. The crest is different on every coin. Furnace. Waterway. Cog. Wave. Snowflake. Closed mouth.
어부 오스카: 돈을 받고도 돈을 두고 갔소. 돈이 필요했던 게 아니란 말: Oscar the Fisher: They took the money and left the money behind. Means it wasn't money they needed. …These crests. Aren't they the ones they say are carved on the thrones? The six kings'. Whoever struck these coins holds the coin dies of all six kingdoms.
마지막 침상 머리맡 벽에 새로 긁은 글: \"그 사람이 말했다. '그만해: Freshly scratched on the wall at the head of the last bunk: "That person said: 'You may stop. I will put it to sleep another way.' We waited a thousand years for those words. We knew it was a lie, and we took it."
어부 오스카: 그만두고 싶은 걸 참는 사람한테 제일 무서운 건 욕이 아니: Oscar the Fisher: To someone holding back the wish to quit, the most frightening thing isn't a curse. It's the words 'you may stop.'
여기서 먹고 자고 불렀던 거요. 마흔 대가. 방이 좁소. 배 선실보다 좁: This is where they ate and slept and sang. Forty generations. The cells are small. Smaller than a ship's cabin.
There's a slate leaning on the wall. A child's writing.
Look at this wall. Tally marks. All of it. They counted the days.
Six bunks empty. There's something on the pillows. I'll pick them up.
They folded the bedding before they went. People who run don't fold their bedding.
Six coins. Every crest different. Let's go up. I'm worried about the two who are left.
닳아서 발 모양으로 패인 돌에 선다. 사제의 목소리가 여섯째 마디에서 갈: You stand on a stone worn into the shape of feet. The priest's voice cracks on the sixth bar. You step into that gap and take up the seventh.
목소리가 물에 실려 내려간다. 발밑 깊은 데서 무언가가 숨을 길게 내쉰다: Your voice is carried down on the water. Far below your feet, something lets out a long breath. The barnacles on the temple pillars all shut at once.
둘째 돌은 더 깊이 패였다. 여기 선 사람이 가장 오래 버텼다. 돌 옆에: The second stone is worn deeper. Whoever stood here held out the longest. There are knee marks beside the stone. When they could not sing standing, they sang kneeling.
어부 오스카: (가운데 돌에서, 틀린 음으로, 크게) …여덟째 마디는 내: Oscar the Fisher: (From the middle stone, off key, loudly) …I'll take the eighth bar! Breathe!
사제가 처음으로 노래를 멈추고 숨을 쉰다. 천 년 만에 남이 불러 주는: For the first time the priest stops singing and draws breath. Hears a lullaby sung by someone else, for the first time in a thousand years. The shoulders shake.
셋째 돌에는 이름이 새겨져 있다. 사제의 것이 아니다. 아이 글씨다. \: A name is carved on the third stone. Not a priest's. A child's handwriting. "I want to ride on its back." Carved before there was a seal.
마지막 마디를 부른다. 밑에서 낮은 소리가 따라 올라온다. 짐승이 잠결에: You sing the last bar. A low sound follows up from below. The beast sings along in its sleep. It knows the eight bars. It has heard them for a thousand years.
사제가 손짓한다. 됐다고. 그리고 제 목에서 조가비 목걸이를 풀어 오스카: The priest gestures. Enough. Then unties a shell necklace from their own neck and presses it into Oscar's hand.
Oscar the Fisher: You can get the notes wrong. So long as it doesn't break off.
(He sings the eight bars low.) …Forgive the wrong notes. It's a fisherman's throat.
리바이어던\n아이들이 등에 올라타 놀던 짐승. 천 년 동안 자장가를 들음:
The Leviathan
The beast on whose back the children rode and played. Heard a lullaby for a thousand years.
Forty generations of priests. They tried not to let a single breath break.
식당 구석 자리: The Corner Seat in the Restaurant
사제는 창가를 피해 구석에 앉았다. 햇빛이 눈부시다고 한다. 손등이 물에: The priest has avoided the window and sits in the corner. The sunlight is too bright, they say. The backs of the hands are white and swollen from the water. They hold the spoon like someone holding one for the first time.
스튜가 나온다. 김이 오른다. 사제가 김을 손으로 잡으려 한다. 잡히지: The stew arrives. Steam rises. The priest tries to catch the steam in a hand. When it will not be caught, they laugh. Without sound. Even the way of laughing is the way of under the water.
식당 주인 로렌초: 천천히 드세요! 뜨거워요! 아, 뜨거운 게 뭔지 모르: Lorenzo the Restaurant Owner: Eat slowly! It's hot! Ah, you don't know what hot is. Um… it's a good thing that you have to be careful with!
\"조용하다.\" 사제가 말한다. 식당은 시끄럽다. 접시 소리, 로렌초: "It is quiet," the priest says. The restaurant is noisy. The clatter of plates, Lorenzo's voice, children shouting outside. In the middle of it all the priest says it is quiet. "There is nothing that must be sung."
어부 오스카: (옆자리에서, 식은 수프를 앞에 두고) …나도 그 말을 알: Oscar the Fisher: (From the next seat, with cold soup before him) …I think I know what that means. It was like that the morning after I hung up the lamp. So quiet my ears rang.
식당 주인 로렌초: 오스카 씨! 오늘은 뜨거운 걸로 드세요! 기다리던 사: Lorenzo the Restaurant Owner: Mr. Oscar! Have the hot one today! It's a day for eating with someone who's been waited for! That one there has waited a thousand years. For the relief!
오스카가 한참 그릇을 본다. 그러고는 식은 수프를 밀어 놓고, 뜨거운 스: Oscar looks at the bowl for a long while. Then he pushes the cold soup aside and takes the hot stew.
둥근 방에 돌 왕좌가 둥글게 놓였다. 등받이마다 문장이 다르다. 화로,: Stone thrones are set in a ring in the round room. A different crest on the back of each. Furnace, waterway, cog, wave, snowflake, closed mouth, flame.
화로의 자리에 망치 한 자루. 물길의 자리에 손바닥만 한 물동이. 톱니의: On the seat of the furnace, a hammer. On the seat of the waterway, a water jar the size of a palm. On the seat of the cog, a winding key. On the seat of the wave, a shell flute. Each a small model of what its king passed off onto his own kingdom.
눈꽃의 자리는 다른 자리보다 작다. 발 받침이 덧대어 있다. 앉은 사람이: The seat of the snowflake is smaller than the others. A footrest has been added. The one who sat there could not reach the floor. Scratched into the back with a fingernail: "I'm scared."
닫힌 입의 자리에는 봉랍 덩어리. 침묵의 왕 벨라스의 것이다. 팔걸이에: On the seat of the closed mouth, a lump of sealing wax. It belongs to Velas, King of Silence. Carved on the armrest: "I will lock the empty seat. So that no one can ask."
장로 에르윈: 벨라스는 조용한 사람이었네. …그렇게 적혀 있네. 그는 말: Elder Erwin: Velas was a quiet man. …So it is written. In place of speaking, he covered things over. The eaten names, and the empty seat. A man who believed that what is covered is not there.
침묵의 왕 벨라스가 잠근 자리: The seat that Velas, King of Silence, locked
…This is the room. Where the thrones stood in a ring. Let us go slowly.
Something has been left on each seat. Look at them one by one. Do not touch.
Sound lingers long in this room. So everyone spoke softly. …So they say.
일곱 자리를 봤군. 벨라스의 자리 뒤에 벽감이 있네. 거기 덮어 둔 것이: You have seen the seven seats. There is a niche behind Velas's seat. What he covered over will be there.
봉랍이 손톱 밑에서 부서진다. 천 년 묵은 밀랍 냄새가 난다. 안에 얇은: The sealing wax crumbles under your fingernail. There is the smell of thousand-year-old beeswax. Inside is a thin stone tablet. The letters are neat. The hand of one who takes things down.
"First day. The way to divide the fire was put forward. One whole name must be fed to it. Silence." "Second day. Whose name? Silence." "Third day. The King of Frost spoke of a prisoner. One against."
Where the name of the one who was against was written, the stone is sunken. It was not dug out. The letters went out by themselves. The stone forgot that name.
\"넷째 날. 화로의 왕: 내 백성 가운데서 뽑을 수는 없다. 물길의 왕: "Fourth day. King of the Furnace: I cannot choose from among my people. King of the Waterway: nor can I. Queen of Cogs: let it be calculated. Silence."
\"다섯째 날. 아무도 오지 않음. 받아 적는 자 혼자 앉아 있었음.\": "Fifth day. No one came. The one taking it down sat alone." Below it in another hand, small: "Only the one whose name went out came. Sat a long while in the empty room, then left. Told me I was working hard."
장로 에르윈: (읽는 것을 어깨 너머로 보다가, 고개를 돌린다.): Elder Erwin: (He watches over your shoulder as you read, then turns his head away.)
\"여섯째 날. 정하지 못함. 불꽃의 왕이 말함: 우리가 정하면 우리 죄: "Sixth day. Could not decide. The King of Flame spoke: if we decide, it becomes our sin. Let us ask the scales. If the scales decide, it becomes law. Seven raised their hands. One did not."
\"물음을 적어 저울의 섬으로 보냄. 물음: 한 이름과 세상. 어느 쪽이: "The question was written down and sent to the Island of the Scale. The question: one name, and the world. Which is heavier?"
넷째 통이 있어야 할 자리는 비었다. 통을 놓았던 둥근 자국만 먼지 위에: The place where a fourth canister should be is empty. Only the round mark where it stood remains in the dust. Inside the niche, a single line pressed in sealing wax: "The answer I do not cover. I destroy it. — Velas"
장로 에르윈: 덮으면 없는 거라고 믿은 사람이 있었네. 틀렸지. 덮은 것: Elder Erwin: There was a man who believed that what is covered is not there. He was wrong. What is covered grows underneath.
The eighth throne is lower than the other seven. There is no crest on its back. It was cut away. The cut is smooth. Done by several hands, with care.
An iron lock is set into the middle of the seat. Something looks out from inside the lock. An eye. The fifth eye. The King of Silence made the empty seat his lock.
팔걸이에 이름이 새겨져 있었다. 긁혔다. 글자가 있던 홈이 여덟 개 남았: A name was once carved on the armrest. It has been scraped away. Eight grooves remain where the letters were. Only the sixth groove is different. Not scraped but burned. To the width of a finger. Someone touched it with a bare hand.
A scrap of grey cloth is caught on the corner of the backrest. The threads were torn downward. It is not from someone who was standing. It is from someone being dragged along the floor.
뒤에서 소리가 난다. 장로가 무릎을 꿇고 있다. 일어나려 하는데 다리가: There is a sound behind you. The Elder is on his knees. He tries to rise and his legs will not obey. He is pressing his gloved right hand down with his left. To keep that hand from going toward the throne.
The Elder avoided answering. It's the first time. That he's ever avoided answering me.
빈 왕좌의 문지기\n묻는 자를 막으라는 명을 받음. 마지막에 그 자리를:
Gatekeeper of the Empty Throne
Ordered to bar those who ask. At the last, it pointed to that seat.
The eighth seat. A name of eight letters. Not yet written.
섬 한가운데로 긴 돌길이 났다. 길 양옆에 돌 걸상이 줄지어 있다. 재판: A long stone path runs to the middle of the island. Stone benches line both sides. The seats of those who waited for judgment. Every bench shines with the polish of hands.
Words scratched into the backs of the benches. "The neighboring country dammed the river. Third day waiting." "Judgment received. I lost. Even so, it was fair." "The scales do not look at faces. That is why I trust them."
기록관 이사벨: 여기는 원래 좋은 곳이었어요. 왕이 아니라 저울이 정하니: Archivist Isabel: This was a good place once. Because the scales decided and not a king, even the powerless could win. I'll write it down. This, too, is part of the record of this place.
법정 · 판결의 벽: The Court · The Wall of Judgments
벽 하나가 판결로 덮였다. 한 줄에 한 재판. \"강물: 나눌 것.\": One wall is covered in judgments. One case to a line. "The river: to be shared." "The border: to follow the old stones." "The debt: to be repaid, the interest reduced." Thousands of lines. The lettering never varies.
맨 아래 줄. \"여덟 왕의 물음. 한 이름과 세상. 어느 쪽이 무거운가: The very bottom line. "The question of the eight kings. One name, and the world. Which is heavier?" In the space for the judgment: "Does not tip. No judgment. Returned to those who asked."
그 밑으로 벽이 달라진다. 같은 글씨인데 줄이 촘촘해지고, 겹치고, 비뚤: Below that the wall changes. The same lettering, but the lines crowd together, overlap, go crooked. "Weighed again. Does not tip." "Weighed again. Does not tip." Without end. At its foot the wall is black with overlapping letters.
기록관 이사벨: 돌려보냈는데 답이 안 왔으니까요. 저울은 재판을 닫지 못: Archivist Isabel: Because it sent the question back and no answer came. The scales could not close the case. For a thousand years they have been weighing it again, alone.
법정 · 새로 새긴 죄목: The Court · The Newly Carved Charges
Recently carved stone tablets lie scattered at the foot of the scales. They are not judgments. They are charges. "The crime of running." "The crime of standing." "The crime of walking sunwise." "The crime of moving the hands too much." "The crime of killing."
돌판마다 날짜가 다르고, 서로 어긋난다. 어제는 뛰는 것이 죄였고 오늘은: Each tablet bears a different date, and they contradict one another. Yesterday running was the crime, and today standing is. Unable to weigh the great question, the scales weigh what they can. Anything at all.
저울 한쪽 접시에는 일곱 개의 인장이 놓였다. 다른 쪽 접시는 비었는데,: On one pan of the scales lie seven seals. The other pan is empty, and yet that empty pan does not rise in the least. There is weight in the empty pan.
기록관 이사벨: 빈 접시에 이름이 놓여 있는 거예요. 우리 눈에 안 보이: Archivist Isabel: A name is lying in the empty pan. One our eyes can't see. An erased name. It was erased, and the weight remained. …I think I know why the Elder won't come here. The scales don't look at faces. They won't look at gloves, either.
Here it is. I can see the scales. They're still turning. That long path is the court.
The benches. The seats of the people who waited. There's writing on the backs.
The whole wall is judgments. Find the bottom line. The last case.
There are stone tablets scattered at the foot of the scales. Newly carved. They're not judgments.
The Elder is sitting at the end of the bridge. He won't look this way. Not once.
판결이 없었어요. 돌아가서 대장님한테 물어봐요. 저런 것 앞에 서 본 사: There was no judgment. Let's go back and ask the Captain. He's someone who has stood before a thing like that.
탐험대장 로란: 조사실에서 배운 거다. 묻는 쪽이 답을 못 정했으면, 답: Captain Roran: I learned it in the inquiry room. If the one asking hasn't settled on the answer, then whatever the one answering does is wrong. So answer only the one thing that's asked.
탐험대장 로란: 저울이 죄목을 내걸면 그 하나만 지켜라. '뛴 죄'가 걸: Captain Roran: When the scales post a charge, keep to that one alone. If 'the crime of running' is posted, you don't run. Standing isn't a crime in the meantime. When the next charge is posted, change then.
▷ 죄인 표식이 붙으면?: ▷ And if the mark of the guilty is put on me?
탐험대장 로란: 더 맞는다. 그게 다다. 죽을죄는 아니다. 붙었다고 허둥: Captain Roran: You get hit harder. That's all. It's no capital crime. The real danger is getting flustered because you're marked and breaking the next charge too. If you got one wrong, stay wrong and keep the next one.
Captain Roran: When crystals rise, break them. They're the vessels where the scales store up guilt. Leave them and they burst. The beams of light draw a line on the floor first. Don't step on the line.
▷ 대장님은 그 조사를 어떻게 견뎠습니까?: ▷ How did you get through that inquiry, Captain?
탐험대장 로란: 인원을 셌다. 조사관 앞에서도. 열둘, 하나. 열둘, 하: Captain Roran: I counted heads. Even in front of the examiner. Twelve, one. Twelve, one. …The archivist told me. That I retie my laces not when it's time to leave, but when I remember what I left behind. She's right. That child sees.
기울지 않는 저울 게부라: Geburah, the Scales That Do Not Tip
제 4 장 · 저울의 섬: Chapter Four · The Island of the Scale
천 년째 닫지 못한 재판: The case left unclosed for a thousand years
Geburah
The scales that weighed the quarrels of the eight kingdoms. Trusted because they did not look at faces.
Given a question that could not be weighed, they weighed it again for a thousand years.
Last judgment: let those who asked give the answer.
So the scales have stopped.
That day I was ordered to guard the door. I did as ordered. That is my charge.
Elder Erwin: It was the night of the sixth day that the scales sent back 'no judgment.' The minutes end there. No one wrote down the seventh day.
Elder Erwin: …So it stands. In the book.
▷ 받아 적던 사람이 있지 않았습니까?: ▷ Wasn't there someone taking it all down?
장로 에르윈: (한참 말이 없다.) 있었지. 일곱째 날 아침에 방에서 내: Elder Erwin: (He says nothing for a long while.) There was. On the morning of the seventh day he was sent out of the room. On someone's orders. So of that day's business, nothing remains but what could be heard outside the door. And the door was thick.
장로 에르윈: 들린 것은 하나일세. 의자 하나가 밀리는 소리. 누가 일어: Elder Erwin: Only one thing was heard. The sound of a single chair being pushed back. Someone stood up. After that there was no sound at all. Meaning that not one of the seven said 'sit down.' That was their judgment. Silence.
▷ 일어선 사람은 누구입니까?: ▷ Who was it that stood up?
Elder Erwin: The name… (The Elder's mouth moves. No sound comes out. It moves once more.) …I cannot. It is not that I will not. Go. To the Frost Prison. You will hear it there. That child remembers better than I. That child was the youngest there that day.
Bram the Smith: Off to the snowfield, are you. Take this. No, it's not a weapon. It's a nail. The nail I pulled from the hundredth peg. Keep it in your pocket. It's no use for anything. Only, isn't it a comfort to have iron in your pocket that held for a thousand years?
대장장이 브람: 거기 있다는 왕이 열여덟이라지. 견습 나이일세. 견습한테: Bram the Smith: They say the king up there is eighteen. An apprentice's age. You don't put the big hammer in an apprentice's hands. Who put a crown in that child's?

어부 오스카: …나는 적어도 누굴 기다리는지는 알았소. 이름을 알았으니까: Oscar the Fisher: …I at least knew who I was waiting for. Because I knew the name. A thousand years without even the name. That means not even knowing how to put the lantern out.
난파선이다. 나는 물은 모른다. 그래도 기다리는 놈들 일이라면 내가 본다: A shipwreck. I don't know water. But if it's the business of those who wait, I'll look at it myself.
The cabin wall. Ropes hanging there. Look at how they're coiled.
구하러 나갈 채비를 한 채로 삭았군. …먼저 올라가라. 젖은 다리는 말을: They rotted still ready to go out and rescue. …Go on up first. A wet leg obeys even less.
궁 한가운데 긴 상이 차려져 있다. 접시, 잔, 수저. 먼지가 없다. 오: A long table is laid in the middle of the palace. Plates, cups, spoons. There is no dust. The table was laid today. There is no food. She has forgotten what the one who is coming likes, and so could not serve it.
상석 두 자리가 나란하다. 의자가 똑같다. 쌍둥이의 자리다. 한쪽 의자는: The two seats at the head stand side by side. The chairs are identical. The seats of twins. One chair is worn from a thousand years of sitting; the other is as straight as new.
반듯한 의자 등받이에 무언가 새겨져 있었던 자리가 있다. 매끈하다. 이름: On the back of the unworn chair is a place where something was once carved. It is smooth. Where a name was. Beneath it, a line gone over countless times with a fingernail: "Your seat."
상 끝에 얼어붙은 배 모형이 하나 놓여 있다. 다른 것과 어울리지 않는다: At the end of the table sits a model ship, frozen. It does not belong with the rest. It is about fifteen years old. On its stand, in a scribe's neat hand: "When this ship comes, please call the name." Signed with the drawing of a gloved hand.
마중 나간 사람: The One Who Went to Welcome
폭풍의 여제, 천 년째 누군가를 맞으러 나온 이: The Storm Empress, who for a thousand years has come out to welcome someone
너는 그 사람이 아니구나.\n…그런데 너는, 그 사람이 어디 있는지 아는:
You are not that person.
…And yet yours is the face of one who knows where that person is.
Archivist Isabel: One of the sailors told me. The Admiral smiled at the end. For the first time in a thousand years she said something other than 'they will come tomorrow.'
기록관 이사벨: 뭐라고 하셨는지는 그분도 못 들었대요. 번개 소리 때문에: Archivist Isabel: What she said, that sailor couldn't hear either. Because of the thunder. Only you will have heard it, Surveyor.
베스탈리아 연대기 · 마중 나간 이름: Chronicle of Vestalia · The Name That Went to Welcome
마중하는 이, 새벽의 섬의 제독\n누구를 맞으러 나왔는지 잊고도 천 년:
The One Who Awaits, Admiral of the Isle of Dawn
Forgot whom she had come out to welcome, and still laid the table for a thousand years
Day discharged: (left empty. She has gone to welcome him.)
\"그는 허공에 있다. 스스로 택한 길이었다. 당신을 잊은 게 아니라,: You said: "He is in the Void. It was the road he chose himself. He did not forget you. It was everyone who forgot him."
You said nothing, and set Oscar's lantern down before her.
지하실에 갇힌 사람: The One Locked in the Cellar
치료소 구석, 쇠창살 너머에 누군가 웅크리고 있다. 살빛이 잿빛이다. 닳: In the corner of the infirmary, behind iron bars, someone sits hunched. The skin is grey. Only the hand around a worn drafting compass will not open.
선반 맨 아래 칸에 봉랍도 뜯지 않은 약병이 하나 남아 있다. 꼬리표:: On the lowest shelf one bottle of medicine is left, its wax seal unbroken. The tag: "Share already paid for. Hand it to whoever comes carrying gold."
약을 뿌리고 황금 사과를 창살 사이로 민다. 잿빛 손이 한참 떨다가 받는: You sprinkle the medicine and push the golden apple through the bars. The grey hand shakes a long while before it takes it. Red steam rises off the skin.
한참 뒤에 쉰 목소리가 난다. \"…선이 틀렸소. 이 방은, 지도에 없소: After a long time, a hoarse voice. "…The line is wrong. This room, it is not on the map."
기록관 이사벨: 하루에 한 장씩 빛나요. 오늘은 셋째 거울이에요. 이 사: Archivist Isabel: One lights up each day. Today it's the third mirror. This person has been repeating one letter a day. So as not to forget. For a thousand years.
침목 밑에 꺼진 등불 하나가 놓여 있다. 손잡이에 책 묶는 끈이 감겨 있: Under the timber sits one dead lantern. A bookbinder's cord is wound round the handle. An archivist's knot.
밤 들판의 시든 것: A Withered One in the Night Fields
달 아래 밀밭 끝에 시든 것 하나가 서 있다. 걷지 않는다. 마을 쪽,: At the edge of the wheat, under the moon, one of the withered is standing. It doesn't walk. It is looking toward the village, at a lit window.
After a long while it starts to walk. Not the walk of a thing attacking. The walk of someone going home. It stops at the fence. A hand comes up and closes on the air at the height of a door latch.
입이 달싹인다. 소리는 없다. 같은 모양을 되풀이한다. 두 글자쯤 되는: Its mouth moves. No sound. The same shape, over and over. A word about two syllables long. Someone's name, or its own.
풀 밟는 소리에 그것이 돌아본다. 눈이 이쪽에 닿는 순간 얼굴에서 그 모: At the sound of grass underfoot it turns. The moment its eyes reach you, that shape is wiped off its face. Only hunger is left. Behind it, two more rise.
다른 한 장은 열다섯 해 묵은 반듯한 글씨: \"한 단지 값 치름. 엘레: The other is a neat hand, fifteen years old: "One jar, paid for. Elena."
선반의 그 단지다. 밑바닥의 보랏빛이 지난번보다 늘어 있다. 누가 채우고: The same jar on the shelf. The purple at the bottom is deeper than last time. Someone has been here to fill it.
Beside the jar stand three empty ink bottles in a row. A grey knot is tied to each. Bottles waiting their turn to be collected.
유리판을 단지 뒤에 세운다. 병 안쪽의 뒤집힌 글씨가 바로 선다. \"쪽: You stand the glass pane behind the jar. The reversed writing inside the bottle rights itself. "Bring the pages and I will fill it. Before that child does."
One more of the witch's tags is stuck on. "The mirror one pays well. Never seen the face, though. Only what the water shows."
유리판에 비춰 본다: Hold it up to the glass pane
길을 막는 종가의 문지기: The house's doorkeeper barring the way
거울에 입김을 분다. 손가락으로 쓴다. 뒤집어서. \"그 아이는 이미 압: You breathe on the mirror. You write with a finger. Backwards. "That child already knows. That the teacher walked in of his own will."
김이 걷힌다. 한참 아무 일도 없다. 그러다 안쪽에서 김이 서린다. 글씨: The fog clears. For a long while, nothing. Then fog forms from the inside. The writing is quick. "Do you think you are the first to bring me those words?"
\"회색 망토를 두른 자들이 셋 왔었다. 셋 다 그렇게 썼다. '그분은: "Three came in grey cloaks. All three wrote the same. 'He knows everything now, hand over the original.' They were hands that child had sent."
다시 쓴다. \"우리는 그가 보낸 사람이 아닙니다.\" 답은 짧다. \": You write again. "We were not sent by him." The answer is short. "In writing, anyone says so. I am a man who lied in writing for a thousand years."
마지막 줄은 천천히 나타난다. \"원본을 원하면 내 손에서 가져가라. 내: The last line comes slowly. "If you want the original, take it from my hand. One who can take it from my hand will keep hold of it in front of that child as well." The mirror goes dark.
기록관 이사벨: 인장부터요. '…중하는 이'. 앞 글자가 깨졌어요. 은화: Archivist Isabel: The seal first. '…Who Awaits.' The front of it is broken off. And on the back of the silver coin, in the same lettering, 'wages for the day of going out to welcome.'
▷ The broken part is 'The One'. 'The One Who Awaits'.
기록관 이사벨: …네. 제가 사흘 본 걸 한 번에 보시네요. 제독의 칭호: Archivist Isabel: …Yes. You saw in one look what took me three days. It was the admiral's title.
기록관 이사벨: 일지 조각. \"누가 오는지는 잊었으나 맞을 채비는 풀지: Archivist Isabel: The log scrap. "Who is coming is forgotten, but we are told not to stand down the welcome." And the scale. There was a scale at every seal. All seven places.
▷ So the storm went round to every guardian. Looking for someone.
Archivist Isabel: To see whether that person was there. For a thousand years.
기록관 이사벨: 항해일지의 그 줄 기억나세요? 회색 망토가 코넬리아 선장: Archivist Isabel: Do you remember that line in the logbook? The route the grey cloak sold Captain Cornelia. 'Where the eighth eye is.'
▷ Not the eye of a seal. The eye of the storm.
기록관 이사벨: 여덟째 왕의 누이가 있는 곳이요. …그걸 알고 판 거예요: Archivist Isabel: Where the eighth king's sister is. …He knew that when he sold it.
장로 에르윈: 수업 전에 하나 묻지. 자네 이름이 뭔가. (대답을 듣고,: Elder Erwin: One question before the lesson. What is your name? (He listens, then writes it in the roll with a gloved hand, one careful stroke at a time.)
장로 에르윈: 됐네. 방금 자네는 한 번 더 태어난 셈일세. 적힌 이름은: Elder Erwin: There. You have just been born a second time, in a way. A name that is written down is not easily taken by the fire. Why that is so is today's lesson.
가져가지 않았다. 세기만 했다. 누군가에게 '여기 한 장 있다'고 알리려: They did not take it. They only counted it. The handprint of someone telling another, 'there is a page here.'
피라미드 입구의 그늘에 앉는다. 모래가 식는 소리가 난다. 이사벨이 챙겨: You sit in the shade of the pyramid's doorway. The sand ticks as it cools. Of the two flasks Isabel packed, one is already empty.
둘째 물통의 끈에 쪽지가 접혀 끼워져 있다. 기록관의 반듯한 글씨다. \: A folded note is tucked under the strap of the second flask, in the archivist's neat hand. "This one is for the way back. You mustn't finish it on the way there."
쪽지 뒷면에 줄을 그어 지운 글이 한 줄 더 있다. 지운 줄 사이로 읽힌: On the back of the note there is one more line, struck through. It can still be read between the strokes. "Mother took only one flask."
물은 미지근하다. 반만 마시고 마개를 닫는다. 해가 기울고, 사막 끝의: The water is lukewarm. You drink half and put the stopper back. The sun leans over, and the sky at the desert's edge darkens first on the village side.
창턱의 먼지 밑에 손톱으로 눌러 쓴 글씨가 있다. 잉크가 걸러지기를 기다: Under the dust on the windowsill there is writing pressed in with a fingernail, by someone who was waiting for the ink to strain. The same neat hand as the tag on the jar.
\"이사벨. 일곱 살. 받침을 아직 틀린다.\" 그 아래 눈금이 두 개: "Isabel. Seven years old. Still gets her final consonants wrong." Below it, two marks are scratched, the way one measures a child's height.
아래 눈금 옆에 \"떠날 때\". 위 눈금 옆에 \"돌아가면\". 위 눈: Beside the lower mark: "when I left." Beside the upper mark: "when I get back." The upper mark is about two finger joints higher.
위 눈금 옆에 한 줄이 더 있다. \"더 컸으면 다시 그을 것.\" 다시: Beside the upper mark there is one more line. "If she has grown more, draw it again." No one has drawn it again.
You hold the jelly close to the trunk. Under the blue light the knife cuts in the bark rise into view. By day the moss hid them. An arrow.
다음 나무에도, 그다음 나무에도 있다. 높이가 같다. 걸으면서 허리께에서: There is one on the next tree, and the one after. All at the same height. Cut at the hip while walking. The lines are straight. Not the hand of a man bewitched.
화살표는 늪으로 가지 않는다. 늪을 비켜 돈다. 그리고 한 둥치에서 끝난: The arrows do not lead to the swamp. They go around it. And they end at a single trunk. The last arrow points out of the wood, to the south.
그 둥치에 명패가 박혀 있다. \"마르코\". 그 아래 껍질에 얕게 새긴: A name tag is driven into that trunk. "Marco." Below it, cut shallow into the bark: "Not the swamp. This way."
젤리 불빛으로 비춘다: Shine the jelly's light on it
쓰러진 코볼레톤의 어깨뼈에 홈이 패어 있다. 양쪽 다. 물지게 끈이 오래: There are grooves worn into the fallen koboleton's shoulder blades. Both sides. Where the straps of a water yoke pressed for a long, long time. These are not a soldier's bones.
A water pail lies on its side nearby. The bottom is gone. Yet the handle is worn smooth. The footsteps going to the basin and back have cut a path into the stone under the sand.
기록관 이사벨: 정원지기예요. 물이 끊긴 뒤에도 물 주는 시간을 지킨 거: Archivist Isabel: A gardener. Even after the water stopped, they kept the watering hour. With an empty pail. …Someone should have told them they could stop.
동이를 바로 세워 수반 곁에 놓는다. 끊긴 수로에서 튄 물방울 하나가 테: You set the pail upright beside the basin. A single drop, thrown from the broken channel, lands on its rim. The bottom is gone, so it does not stay.
Hors, squire to Arden, Grand Master of the Flame Knights.
He kept the words "Guard the door until I return" for a thousand years.
His armor rusted and he forgot his own name, and still he did not leave the door.
His back kept empty, for his lord to ride.
왕국이 얼어붙던 날, 아이들이 마지막으로 맡긴: On the day the kingdom froze, the children gave it one last thing to keep:
an ice crystal. It held it close and slept a thousand years.
The stonemason who carved the seal stones and left them behind.
He stopped partway through the eighth stone. He was given no name to carve.
On the summit he is still asking where that abandoned stone went.
Priest of the second sun the masked tribe worships.
Since one night twenty years ago, the mask has never come off.
Only one person knows the face beneath it. The one who counts heads three times.
The abandoned eighth seal stone. It lay buried beneath the First Cave.
The eight letters where a name should be carved are blank; only one half-carved word remains. Mercy.
스무 해 전 원정대가 처음 사람을 잃은 자리다. 투구 둘이 등을 맞대고: This is where the expedition first lost someone, twenty years ago. Two helmets stood back to back.
삼킨 목소리로 우는 것: The One That Cries in Swallowed Voices
A fish of the deep, trapped in the ice and starved on the night the sea froze.
It calls the next person in the voice of the one it swallowed.
As it fell, it gave back every voice it had swallowed.
It does not break ships. It cradles them and takes them down.
Thirty years ago it took the merchant ship Morning Star and her crew of thirty-two.
When the sea froze it was trapped beneath the Graveyard of Ships, still cradling the Morning Star.
King of a land that gave away everything asked of it, and sank.
He never learned to refuse. He gave away even the breakwater.
선장의 청 \"내 배에서는 아무도 죽지 않게\"도 들어주었다. 그래서 바: He granted the captain's plea too: "Let no one die on my ship." And so the sea froze.
Taking back with his own hands the last thing he gave, he asked that his apology be passed on.
Three hundred. All aboard. No deaths.
A captain who, at twenty-two, lost her first ship and thirty-two crew and survived alone.
After that she had one law. No one dies on my ship.
She asked it of the Giving King, and the ship stopped in the ice with three hundred aboard.
For fifteen years she wrote over the roll every day. So that not one line would fade.
이름을 받지 못한 아들: The Son Who Was Given No Name
A giant forged by a hundred smiths at the order of Bragan, King of the Furnace.
So that the making of it would not leak out, the king locked the forge doors from outside.
For a thousand years it knocked on the door. Two, a rest, three.
In the smiths' code, that means "Come and eat."
The beast that Amrat, King of the Desert, rode.
The king said only, "Let no one in until you hear the sound of water."
He never could bring himself to say that the water would not come.
A thousand years later the water came, and the gatekeeper opened the gate as promised.
The counting machine that the city of Ordel, Queen of Cogs, asked about everything.
When the queen asked, "When is the end?" it answered: twelve o'clock.
The queen stopped every clock in the city at one minute to.
천 년 뒤 깨어나 밀린 답을 한꺼번에 뱉었다. 늦은 답에는 미안하다고 덧: A thousand years later it woke and spat out all its overdue answers at once. On the late ones it stamped an apology.
자장가를 듣는 것: The One That Listens to the Lullaby
A beast raised by Neris, Queen of the Abyss. Children used to climb on its back and play.
Once it held the Eye, the city would fall if it woke, so the priests sang it a lullaby.
Forty generations, with no relief, a thousand years.
It sings eight bars along in its sleep.
The gatekeeper that Velas, King of Silence, set before the empty seat.
It was ordered to stop those who ask.
It was never told what must not be asked.
As it fell, it pointed to that seat.
The scales that weighed the quarrels of the eight kingdoms. Trusted because they did not look at faces.
The kings asked: one name or the world, which is heavier?
The scales did not tip, and for a thousand years weighed the same question again.
Final judgment: those who asked shall answer.
The King of Frost, crowned at sixteen and seated at the council of eight kings at eighteen.
He entrusted the Eye to no one and locked the prison door with his own hand. There are no jailers.
The cook, the drummer child and the writing teacher all followed him in.
Because it didn't seem right to leave him alone.
덮지 않는 자: The One Who Does Not Cover
Believing that what the snow covers is forgotten, he carries the frozen dead to his cave and stands them up.
To him, anyone who comes to collect name tags is a thief.
The beast that Amrat, King of the Desert, set to digging the waterway.
Even after the kingdom was buried in sand, it digs on according to the plans.
For a thousand years it has not reached the last stretch: the king's garden.
재가 될 때까지 따르는 자: The One Who Follows Until It Is Ash
The dragon that Arden, Grand Master of the Flame Knights, rode.
It guards the tower its master left with one word: "Wait."
For a thousand years it has burned the soot off the saddle with its breath. So it can be ridden at any moment.
저승의 문턱을 지키는 이: Keeper of the Threshold of the Underworld
Vice Master of the Flame Knights.
세 대장이 머리를 내놓아 하나의 무기가 되는 「세 머리의 서약」에: He alone opposed the 'Oath of Three Heads',
혼자 반대했다. \"동료를 무기로 만들 수는 없다.\": by which three captains give their heads to become one weapon. "We cannot make weapons of our comrades."
Overruled, he has guarded for a thousand years the door of the place where the oath was sworn.
Do not come, you who hold the embers.
He took the wick of the First Flame into his own body and held it there for a thousand years.
In dreams he always said the same thing. Not yet. Do not come.
Admiral of the fleet of the Isle of Dawn, the Storm Empress.
She carried someone to the council by ship and said, "I'll come out to welcome you when you return."
That person never came back, and even she has forgotten who it was.
For a thousand years she has wrapped every passing ship in storm to look inside.
Belloc, the scribe who rewrote the Order's Chronicle.
\"일곱이 쫓아냈다\"고 썼다. 미워할 대상이 있어야 견디는 아이가 있어: He wrote, "The seven drove it out." Because there was a child who could only endure with someone to hate.
The original, from before he changed it, is still inside his mirror.
최초의 불꽃이 모든 것을 집어 삼키기 이전,: Before the First Flame swallowed everything,
a light from the days when it still kept memory.
잿빛 해가 오기 전날 밤, 왕국에서 제련으로는 따를 자가 없던: On the eve of the Ashen Sun, a smith no one in the kingdom could match at smelting
대장장이가 소문으로만 전해지던 이름 없는 금속 안에: took a nameless metal known only from rumor,
cooled a handful of fire, and shut it inside.
The smith carved his own name nowhere on the spear.
For the first thing the fire swallowed must not be its maker's name.
This flame does not let the name of the one who accepts it burn.
…And so that smith's name alone, no one knows.
행운 상인의 상품 더미에 섞여 있던 낡은 은화. 앞면에 여덟 갈래 번개,: A worn silver coin mixed into the Luck Merchant's pile of wares. On the face, lightning with eight forks; on the back, one line: "Wages for the day of going to welcome. To be paid on return."
그런 돈은 처음 보는데. 품삯을 '돌아와서 치른다'니, 못 돌아온 배의: Never seen money like that. Wages 'to be paid on return'… that'll be coin from a ship that never came back.
Eight forks, eh. Not seven? …I counted, and it really is eight.
잠든 수호자의 재 속에서 나온 비늘. 아직도 찌릿하다. 수호자의 것이 아: A scale found in the ashes of a sleeping guardian. It still tingles. It is not the guardian's. Someone passed close by.
It came from beside a guardian? Then that storm has been calling at every seal. Looking for what, I wonder.
이 비늘… 물고기 것이 아니야. 훨씬 큰 것. 폭풍 속에서 딱 한 번 본: This scale… it's no fish's. Something far bigger. I saw it just once, inside a storm. I took it for lightning.
어느 버려진 상자 바닥에 깔려 있던 악보. 제목만 온전하다: 「마중 가는: Sheet music lining the bottom of some abandoned chest. Only the title is whole: 'The Song of Going to Welcome.' Every place in the lyrics where a person's name would go is blank.
이 가락, 들어 본 것 같은데… 폭풍 치는 밤이면 바다 쪽에서 들리는 그: I think I've heard this tune… isn't it the one that comes from the sea on stormy nights?
Only the places for the name are blank. They weren't erased. Ink never touched them. This was written down by someone who forgot the name they meant to call.
바다에서 낚아 올린, 소금에 절은 종이. \"여덟 번째 함대, 폭풍의 눈: Salt-soaked paper fished out of the sea. "Eighth Fleet, anchored inside the eye of the storm. The Admiral says: she has forgotten who is coming, but the welcome is not to be stood down."
폭풍의 눈 안에 닻을 내린다고? 미친 소리… 라고 하고 싶은데, 눈 안은: Anchor inside the eye of a storm? Madness… I'd like to say, but it is calm in the eye. If you could stay there a thousand years, that is.
An eighth fleet? They say there were seven kingdoms. A ship of an eighth land, then?
여덟 갈래 번개 문양의 인장 조각. 깨진 면에 글자 반 토막: \"…중하: A fragment of a seal bearing eight-forked lightning. On the broken face, part of a phrase: "…ne Who Awaits".
'…중하는 이'? 앞 글자가 깨졌네. 존중? 마중? 인장에 그런 말을 새: '…ne Who Awaits'? The front is broken off. 'No one'? 'The one'? Who carves words like that on a seal?
A ship is coming.
…This time, are you that person?
…뜨거운 바람이 느껴지나? 이 문 너머가 화염의 군주, 이그니스의 처소다: …Do you feel the hot wind? Beyond this gate lie the chambers of Ignis, Lord of Flame.
제단에 불꽃을 바쳐 군주가 깨어나면 문은 닫힌다. 안에 있는 자들만으로: Offer flame at the altar and the Lord wakes, and the gate shuts. Those inside must see it through alone.
Will you hand over a raid ticket and go in? …Do come back alive.
정말 입장하시겠습니까?: Are you sure you want to enter?
